area: hooks, permissions, settings layering, managed policy settings

facts.behavior: command (shell or exec form, stdin JSON in, exit code/stdout/stderr out), http (POST of event JSON, response body is same JSON schema), mcp_tool (calls a tool on a configured MCP server), prompt (single-turn model evaluation returning JSON decision, $ARGUMENTS placeholder), agent (subagent with Read/Grep/Glob, experimental). Matching hooks run in parallel; if more than 12 prompt/agent hooks match, 12 run at once and the rest queue.
facts.limits: Command hooks communicate only via stdout/stderr/exit codes; they can't trigger / commands or tool calls. agent hooks are experimental and may change.

facts.behavior: Session: SessionStart, SessionEnd, Setup (only with --init-only, or --init/--maintenance in -p). Turn: UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, StopFailure. Tool loop: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch. Subagents/tasks: SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle. Context/config: InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged. Worktrees: WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove. Compaction/model: PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch. MCP: Elicitation, ElicitationResult. Other: Notification, MessageDisplay.
facts.limits: EndConversation tool calls skip PreToolUse and PostToolUse. PreToolUse does not fire for files referenced with @ unless CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS=1. Unknown hook event name in settings yields a Settings Warning and that entry is skipped.

facts.behavior: Three nesting levels: hook event -> matcher group -> handler(s). Locations: ~/.claude/settings.json (all projects, local only), .claude/settings.json (project, committable), .claude/settings.local.json (project, gitignored), managed policy settings (org-wide), plugin hooks/hooks.json (while enabled), skill frontmatter (rest of session after invocation), subagent frontmatter (while subagent runs). Hooks and other .claude/settings.json keys load from the current working directory's .claude/ folder with no parent-directory fallback.
facts.limits: No parent-directory fallback for project hooks. Identical handlers across settings files are deduplicated and run once; plugin and skill copies are separate. Hooks in a skill that hasn't been invoked aren't listed by /hooks. Settings edits are normally picked up automatically by a file watcher.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md (Where output styles, hooks, and local settings load from)

facts.behavior: '*', '' or omitted matches everything. Only letters/digits/_/-/space/,/| : exact string or list (Edit|Write, or comma). Any other character: JavaScript regex, unanchored (Edit.* matches NotebookEdit; use ^Edit$). Matched field varies by event: tool_name for tool events; SessionStart source (startup, resume, clear, compact, fork); SessionEnd reason; PreCompact/PostCompact manual|auto; ConfigChange source (user_settings, project_settings, local_settings, policy_settings, skills); InstructionsLoaded load_reason; StopFailure error type; Elicitation MCP server name; Notification type. MCP tools are mcp__<server>__<tool>; mcp__memory__.* matches a whole server. Matchers are case-sensitive.
facts.limits: A bare mcp__memory matches nothing. No matcher support (always fires) for CwdChanged, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, MessageDisplay, PostToolBatch. FileChanged/StopFailure accept only letters, digits, _ and | on the exact path. Canonical tool names required; a display label such as 'Stop Task' (canonical TaskStop) doesn't match. Matcher filters by tool name only; Bash/PowerShell file writes bypass an Edit|Write matcher.

facts.behavior: Filters by tool name and arguments using permission-rule syntax (e.g. Bash(git *), Edit(*.ts)) so the hook process only spawns when the call matches. Holds exactly one rule, no && or ||.
facts.limits: Evaluated only on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied; adding it to any other event prevents the hook from running. Best-effort: when Claude Code can't determine which commands the Bash input runs, it runs the hook regardless.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md (Filter by tool name and arguments with the if field); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md

facts.feature: Hook handler fields: timeout, statusMessage, once, async, asyncRewake, shell, args
facts.behavior: timeout in seconds; defaults 600 for command/http/mcp_tool (30s on UserPromptSubmit, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch; 10s on MessageDisplay), 30 for prompt, 60 for agent. args switches command to exec form (no shell, each element one argument). async runs command hook in background without blocking. asyncRewake runs in background and wakes Claude on exit 2. shell: bash or powershell. SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5s budget, raised by a longer per-hook timeout up to 60s. A timed-out hook has its output discarded.
facts.limits: once is honored only in skill frontmatter. async is command-only; timeout not enforced on async hooks (still enforced for asyncRewake); async hooks can't block or control Claude (decision/permissionDecision/continue have no effect); output delivered on next turn; in -p mode running async hooks are killed at teardown. On PreToolUse a timeout does not block the call unless onFailure:'block'. On PreModelSwitch a timeout blocks the switch.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md (Run hooks in the background; Limitations)

facts.behavior: Exit 0 = success; stdout parsed as JSON if a single JSON object, else plain text (plain stdout added as context only for UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart, PostModelSwitch). Exit 2 = blocking error, stderr is the reason, effect depends on event. Any other code = non-blocking error: action continues and a '<hook name> hook error' notice appears. 'Exit 1 is not a block.'
facts.limits: Exit 0 from PreToolUse does not approve the call; it still goes through the normal permission flow. Exit 2 also blocks when JSON is printed; allow decisions cannot override the block.

facts.behavior: Blocks: PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated (rolls back), TaskCompleted, ConfigChange (except policy_settings), PreCompact, PreModelSwitch, Elicitation (declines), ElicitationResult, PostToolBatch (stops the loop), WorktreeCreate (any non-zero fails), WorktreeRemove (fails if dir remains).
facts.limits: Does not block (stderr shown to user): PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart, SessionStart, SessionEnd, CwdChanged, FileChanged, PostCompact, PostModelSwitch. Ignored: Notification, Setup, InstructionsLoaded, MessageDisplay, PermissionDenied, StopFailure (except terminalSequence). PermissionRequest: exit 2 is not honored (deny via the decision object; exit 2 without decision leaves flow unchanged). PostToolUse hooks can't undo actions because the tool already ran.

facts.behavior: continue (default true): false stops Claude entirely and takes precedence over event decisions, pair with stopReason. systemMessage: warning shown to user. terminalSequence: allowlisted OSC 0/1/2/9/99/777 and BEL only, interactive only. Always include hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName when using hookSpecificOutput.
facts.limits: suppressOutput is accepted but has no effect. additionalContext, systemMessage, initialUserMessage and plain stdout are each capped at 10,000 characters (overflow saved to file, 2,000-char preview). Output that doesn't start with { (e.g. shell-profile echo) is read as plain text and JSON ignored with no error. Fields at the wrong level (e.g. permissionDecision at top level instead of inside hookSpecificOutput) have no effect. Notification hooks discard systemMessage and continue; ConfigChange discards them too; WorktreeRemove discards JSON fields.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (JSON output); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md (Hook JSON has no effect)

facts.behavior: Top-level decision:'block' + reason: UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop, ConfigChange, PreCompact. hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (allow|deny|ask|defer) + permissionDecisionReason: PreToolUse. hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior (allow|deny) plus updatedInput/updatedPermissions/message/interrupt: PermissionRequest. retry:true: PermissionDenied. updatedToolOutput: PostToolUse. worktreePath: WorktreeCreate over HTTP. action accept|decline|cancel + content: Elicitation/ElicitationResult. displayContent: MessageDisplay. additionalContext (injected as system reminder): SessionStart, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop, PostModelSwitch.
facts.limits: Docs advise writing additionalContext as factual statements, not imperative 'system' phrasing, because that can trigger prompt-injection defenses. Setup hooks can't block and their JSON output is discarded. InstructionsLoaded has no blocking or decision control and runs asynchronously for observability. SubagentStart can't block.

facts.feature: PreToolUse decisions, updatedInput and multi-hook precedence
facts.behavior: permissionDecision allow 'skips the permission prompt'; deny blocks; ask forces prompt; defer pauses. updatedInput replaces the entire tool input object. Precedence across multiple hooks: deny > defer > ask > allow. Exit 2 behaves like deny with stderr as reason. A PreToolUse deny blocks the tool even in bypassPermissions mode or with --dangerously-skip-permissions, and in dontAsk mode, because PreToolUse hooks fire before any permission-mode check. When multiple hooks match every hook's command runs to completion before results merge; one hook's deny doesn't stop sibling hooks.
facts.limits: If multiple PreToolUse hooks return updatedInput, Claude Code doesn't merge the rewrites or guarantee which one runs. 'allow' can't override deny/ask rules, and can't suppress the prompt for network-path reads, MCP tools marked requiresUserInteraction, SDK always_ask tools, or org-'ask' connector tools; AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode need allow paired with updatedInput. defer works only with -p, for a single tool call, ends turn with stop_reason tool_deferred. In plan mode, a hook's allow has no effect on file edits or non-read-only calls (except ExitPlanMode with updatedInput).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (PreToolUse); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md (Hooks and permission modes); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md (Extend permissions with hooks)

facts.behavior: PreToolUse hook decisions don't bypass permission rules: 'Claude Code evaluates deny and ask rules regardless of what a PreToolUse hook returns' - a matching deny rule blocks, a matching ask rule still prompts even if the hook returned allow. Conversely a blocking hook (exit 2 / deny) takes precedence over allow rules: the block applies before permission rules are evaluated. Pattern in docs: allow bare 'Bash' then register a PreToolUse hook that rejects specific commands.
facts.limits: Applies to hooks in settings files and plugin hooks/hooks.json. A mod handling tool.check answers after PreToolUse hooks; with no managed settings and no Team/Enterprise /login, a mod can approve a call a deny rule refused or a hook blocked.

facts.behavior: Runs when Claude is about to show a permission prompt (or would otherwise auto-deny a call that can't prompt); output hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior allow|deny with updatedInput, updatedPermissions (e.g. setMode), message, interrupt. In -p mode still runs outside dontAsk mode; a call no hook decides is denied.
facts.limits: Doesn't fire for sandbox network requests. Exit 2 not honored. setMode bypassPermissions is a no-op unless bypass mode was available at launch. permission_suggestions in input are not an exact list of dialog options.

facts.behavior: Fires only in auto mode when the classifier or a safety check denies a call; hookSpecificOutput.retry:true tells the model it may retry.
facts.limits: Does not fire for manual denials, PreToolUse blocks, or deny rules. Claude Code doesn't reverse the denial itself. Exit 2 ignored.

facts.behavior: PostToolUse runs after a successful tool call; updatedToolOutput changes what Claude sees; decision:'block' adds reason next to the result. PostToolUseFailure runs when a tool fails (additionalContext). PostToolBatch fires once after all calls in a batch resolve; block or continue:false stops the loop before the next model call. classifierContext (v2.1.236+) capped at 2,000 chars.
facts.limits: 'The tool has already run by the time the hook fires'; decision block does not replace/undo output; telemetry still records original output. PostToolUseFailure doesn't fire for validation errors or permission denials. Exit 2 does not block on Post events. PostToolUse matcher Edit|Write misses file changes made via Bash.

facts.behavior: Fire whenever Claude finishes responding (not only at task completion). decision:'block' with reason (or exit 2 with stderr) prevents stopping and gives Claude the reason; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext continues the conversation as non-error 'Stop hook feedback'. Input includes stop_hook_active (true when already continuing from a stop hook) and last_assistant_message. Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row with no tool call in between; raise via CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP. A Stop hook scanning the working tree once per turn is the docs' suggestion for compliance coverage of Bash-made file changes.
facts.limits: Stop hooks don't fire on user interrupts; API errors fire StopFailure instead (StopFailure output/exit code ignored). onFailure is ignored on Stop/SubagentStop.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (Stop); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md (Stop hook hits the block cap)

facts.behavior: UserPromptSubmit fires on user prompts (also scheduled tasks, background subagent reports, messages from other sessions); can block (decision:'block' + reason, exit 2), add additionalContext, set sessionTitle, suppressOriginalPrompt. UserPromptExpansion fires when a typed command like /skillname expands (which PreToolUse on Skill misses), matched on command_name.
facts.limits: Default timeout 30s; on timeout output is discarded and prompt proceeds unless onFailure:'block'. 'A blocked prompt never reaches Claude, but its text isn't removed everywhere' (block message can include prompt; transcript keeps it).

facts.behavior: Source startup|resume|clear|compact|fork. Output additionalContext, initialUserMessage (non-interactive -p only), sessionTitle, watchPaths, reloadSkills. CLAUDE_ENV_FILE persists variables for later Bash commands (append with >>); CwdChanged and FileChanged also have CLAUDE_ENV_FILE and variables persist until next CwdChanged. Post-compaction context re-injection is done with SessionStart matcher compact.
facts.limits: Cannot block (exit 2 shows stderr only). On --continue/--resume//clear hooks run in background but Claude's first response still waits for them. Async SessionStart output skipped if identical to last delivered.

facts.behavior: Runs when a settings file, a managed policy file, or a skill file changes (sources user_settings, project_settings, local_settings, policy_settings, skills). Exit 2 or JSON decision block prevents the change taking effect in the running session. For managed policy runs only when managed-settings.json or a file in managed-settings.d/ changes.
facts.limits: policy_settings changes can't be blocked (hooks fire for logging; blocking decision ignored). Not run for server-managed settings, macOS managed preferences or Windows registry policy changes, or for MDM/console-delivered settings. A blocked change surfaces no message to user or Claude (debug log only); systemMessage and continue discarded.

facts.feature: Other lifecycle hooks (InstructionsLoaded, CwdChanged, FileChanged, DirectoryAdded, PreCompact/PostCompact, PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch, Elicitation, Notification, TaskCreated/TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, SubagentStart)
facts.behavior: InstructionsLoaded fires when CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md load (observability only). PreCompact can block (exit 2 or decision block). PreModelSwitch can block a model switch (timeout also blocks). TaskCreated exit 2 rolls back/deletes the task; TaskCompleted exit 2 blocks completion; TeammateIdle blocks. Elicitation exit 2 declines. Notification matchers include permission_prompt, idle_prompt, auth_success, elicitation_dialog, agent_completed.
facts.limits: InstructionsLoaded, Notification, Setup, MessageDisplay, PermissionDenied: exit code ignored. PostCompact, PostModelSwitch, CwdChanged, FileChanged, SessionEnd, SubagentStart cannot block. Notification hooks are for side effects only.

facts.behavior: WorktreeCreate replaces Claude's default `git worktree` creation (allows SVN/Perforce/Mercurial); hook must return the worktree directory path (stdout for command hooks, hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath for HTTP); any non-zero exit fails creation. WorktreeRemove runs when Claude cleans up a worktree created by WorktreeCreate hook; no matcher on either.
facts.limits: WorktreeCreate does not run for worktrees Claude adds through Bash, nor for a plugin hook with --worktree --tmux (define in settings file). Claude Code never deletes a branch belonging to a hook-created worktree. For subagent/workflow-agent worktrees made by the hook, Claude keeps the worktree and doesn't run WorktreeRemove. WorktreeRemove JSON output discarded. For git-based worktrees Claude handles cleanup itself.

facts.feature: Hook failure handling (onFailure) and non-blocking default
facts.behavior: onFailure:'block' (command/http, v2.1.295+) makes these block the action: can't start, exit code other than 0 or 2, HTTP error/non-2xx, timeout, invalid output. Default: hook failure/timeout does not block (e.g. PreToolUse timeout doesn't block). On Windows without Git Bash, shell-form PreToolUse and PermissionRequest command hooks can block when they fail and only exit 0 or 2 counts; docs recommend shell:'powershell', exec form, or explicit onFailure.
facts.limits: onFailure is ignored on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, and async hooks. Invalid JSON/schema on stdout produces a hook error notice even on exit 0.

facts.behavior: prompt hooks: single-turn model evaluation, model returns JSON decision (ok/reason schema), $ARGUMENTS placeholder, model field. agent hooks: subagent with Read/Grep/Glob that verifies conditions. Docs position them for judgment-based decisions rather than deterministic rules.
facts.limits: Only supported on a subset of events (list in docs includes ConfigChange, WorktreeCreate etc.); agent hooks experimental; default timeouts 30s prompt / 60s agent; non-deterministic (model-evaluated).

facts.feature: HTTP hooks and env var interpolation
facts.behavior: POST event JSON to url; response body uses same JSON schema as command output; headers support $VAR / ${VAR} interpolation only for variables listed in allowedEnvVars (others stay empty).
facts.limits: Run only if URL matches allowedHttpHookUrls allowlist (merged); httpHookAllowedEnvVars limits interpolable vars. Non-2xx/HTTP error is non-blocking unless onFailure:'block'.

facts.feature: Hook environment variables and path placeholders
facts.behavior: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (project root where session started, fixed even in a worktree), CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE='true' in remote web environments, CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH. ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} etc. work as placeholders in both exec and shell form. Stdin common fields: session_id, transcript_path, cwd, scratchpad_dir, permission_mode, effort.level, hook_event_name, agent_id/agent_type.
facts.limits: No $CLAUDE_MODEL; $ANTHROPIC_MODEL doesn't reflect /model switches. transcript_path may lag the in-memory conversation (use last_assistant_message on Stop/SubagentStop). If cwd is deleted mid-session, hooks fall back to start dir, project root, home or temp.

facts.behavior: In interactive sessions Claude Code holds back hooks from every settings file, including ~/.claude/settings.json, until the workspace trust dialog is accepted for the folder or a trusted parent. Project subagent frontmatter hooks run only after trust and are stricter than settings-file hooks. Command hooks run with the user's full permissions ('Review and test all hook commands'). Docs best practices: validate/sanitize inputs, quote shell variables, block path traversal, use absolute paths, skip sensitive files.
facts.limits: -p/SDK sessions never show the dialog and treat the folder as trusted, so hooks committed in a repo's .claude/settings.json run in a never-trusted folder; mitigate with --bare, --setting-sources user, or --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'. Trusting only a parent folder: settings-file hooks are used; subagent-frontmatter hooks not used.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md (Security considerations); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md (What runs before you trust a folder)

facts.behavior: disableAllHooks in settings disables hooks; --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' overrides project/local for one run. allowManagedHooksOnly (managed-only) blocks user, project, local and plugin hooks (/hooks shows 'Only hooks from managed settings run here'), also narrows statusLine, fileSuggestion, subagentStatusLine and disables command-source plugins. strictPluginOnlyCustomization blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources (true locks all four, array names which).
facts.limits: disableAllHooks cannot disable managed hooks unless set at managed level; setting it in user settings alone is not enough against a repo because project settings take precedence and can set it back to false. allowManagedHooksOnly only honored from managed sources (placing in user/project has no effect); under merge managed behavior the strictest value across sources applies.

facts.behavior: Each skill source can register at most 1,024 hooks with matchers totaling 16,384 characters (v2.1.304+); over-limit skills lose their hooks and the debug log says 'registers none of its hooks'.
facts.limits: Applies to skill-frontmatter hooks only.

facts.behavior: /hooks lists configured hooks by event; claude --debug shows hook execution; piping sample JSON to the script tests it; the transcript shows 'PreToolUse hook error' notices for non-zero/non-2 exits and blocking messages (except ConfigChange and Elicitation which show none).
facts.limits: /hooks doesn't list hooks from a skill not yet invoked, or hooks suppressed by allowManagedHooksOnly. File watcher may miss a change; restart forces reload.

facts.behavior: Read-only (file reads, Grep) need no approval within working directory/additional directories; Bash commands require approval except built-in read-only set ('Yes, don't ask again' is permanent per repository and command); file modification requires approval ('don't ask again' lasts until session end); WebFetch requires approval except preapproved documentation domains (permanent per repo and domain); WebSearch requires approval.
facts.limits: Rule saved from a permanent approval goes to .claude/settings.local.json at the git repo root (resolved to main checkout from worktrees); outside git repo, home dir root, on Windows, or when root/.git/.claude not owned by user it stays with .claude/settings.json. Some prompts offer only one-time approval.

facts.behavior: Rules evaluated deny, then ask, then allow; first match determines outcome and 'rule specificity doesn't change the order'. A broad deny blocks calls even if a narrower allow matches; an ask rule prompts even if a more specific allow matches. A bare tool-name deny (e.g. Bash) removes the tool from Claude's context; a scoped deny (Bash(rm *)) leaves the tool and blocks matching calls. 'Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model.' Instructions in prompt or CLAUDE.md shape what Claude tries but don't change what Claude Code allows.
facts.limits: Bare-name removal doesn't apply to EndConversation (deny can't remove it while other tools remain; ask never prompts for it). Rule changes via /permissions apply starting with Claude's next tool call in the same turn.

facts.behavior: default (Manual): prompts on first use of each tool; acceptEdits: auto-accepts file edits and mkdir/touch/mv/cp in working dir or additionalDirectories; plan: read-only exploration, no source edits; auto: background classifier checks actions; dontAsk: auto-denies every call that would otherwise prompt (pre-approved tools still run); bypassPermissions: skips prompts except 'actions no mode auto-approves'. permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode / permissions.disableAutoMode set to 'disable' prevent those modes.
facts.limits: bypassPermissions skips prompts including for writes to protected paths such as .git and .claude; only for isolated environments. auto and bypassPermissions as defaultMode don't take effect from project or local settings (user or managed or --permission-mode only). disableBypassPermissionsMode works from any scope (typically managed). dontAsk still denies AskUserQuestion, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, network-path reads, org-ask connector tools.

facts.feature: Permission rule syntax: Tool and Tool(specifier), parameter rules, tool-name globs
facts.behavior: Format Tool or Tool(specifier); bare name matches all uses. Deny/ask rules can match a top-level scalar input parameter with Tool(param:value) (e.g. Agent(model:opus), Bash(run_in_background:true)), * wildcard allowed. Deny/ask accept glob in tool-name position ('mcp__*', '*'); allow globs only after literal mcp__<server>__ prefix.
facts.limits: Primary content fields (command, file_path, path, notebook_path, url) can't be matched by param: rules; Bash(command:rm *) is ignored with startup warning. Parameter rules can't be allow rules. Unanchored allow globs like '*' or 'mcp__*' are skipped. settings loader skips any mcp__ rule that has parentheses (use --disallowedTools). Deny/ask rule matching no known tool gives a startup warning.

facts.behavior: * matches any text including spaces anywhere in the rule; rule with no * matches exactly one command. Trailing ' *' also matches the bare command (Bash(ls *) matches ls) when it is the only wildcard; space before * matters (ls* matches lsof). :* suffix equivalent to trailing wildcard. Claude Code warns at startup about an allow rule with * before the subcommand (Bash(git * main)).
facts.limits: Bash(git *) allows every git command including -c options. Bash rules constraining arguments are 'fragile' (curl URL patterns miss options, protocols, redirects, variables).

facts.behavior: Recognized separators: &&, ||, ;, |, |&, &, newlines; every subcommand must be allowed for a compound command to run without a prompt. Deny and ask rules apply when any subcommand matches, including inside subshells, command substitution and control-flow bodies. Built-in stripped wrappers: timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, bare xargs, and leading assignments of known-safe env vars (deny/ask match past any leading assignment). Approving a compound command saves up to 5 separate rules.
facts.limits: Wrapper list is built-in and not configurable; npx, direnv exec, devbox run, mise exec, docker exec are NOT stripped, so Bash(devbox run *) matches devbox run rm -rf. xargs with flags not stripped. A trailing '&&' with nothing after makes command unparseable for allow matching. Prefix rules can't auto-approve exec wrappers (watch, setsid, ionice, flock) or find with -exec/-delete/-rm/-fprint/-files0-from.

facts.feature: What a Bash deny/ask rule does not match (not a security boundary)
facts.behavior: Docs table: Bash(curl *) stops `curl https://example.com` but not /usr/bin/curl or `sh -c 'curl ...'`; Bash(rm *) doesn't stop /bin/rm or bash -c 'rm -rf'; Bash(git push *) doesn't stop `git -C . push`, `git -c ... push`, `git 'push'`. 'a deny or ask rule covers the invocation Claude usually produces and isn't a security boundary around the program.' Docs recommend sandboxing for filesystem/network enforcement and a PreToolUse hook to inspect full command text.
facts.limits: Rules are text-pattern matches on the command Claude writes after splitting/wrapper stripping.

facts.behavior: A built-in non-configurable set (ls, cat, echo, pwd, head, tail, grep, find, wc, which, diff, stat, du, cd, read-only git forms) runs without prompt in every mode; to require a prompt add an ask or deny rule. Unquoted globs allowed when every flag is read-only.
facts.limits: Still prompts for: unquoted globs with write-capable flags (find, sort, sed, git), docker pointed at another daemon, file -m/-f, ps that could print env (ps auxe), UNC paths on Windows, writes to PATH/IFS, unparseable commands, commands over 10,000 chars, cd+git into different directory, cd+redirect with unresolvable target.

facts.behavior: Output redirects (>, >>, 2>) are checked against Edit allow/deny rules, protected paths and working directories; input redirects (<) against Read rules and working directories (v2.1.257+); tee targets checked (v2.1.269+). Bash(git commit *) allows the command, not the redirect target; ~ or glob targets need approval.
facts.limits: No check for /dev/null, fd forms (2>&1), here-docs/strings. Allow rule Bash(tee *) doesn't cover destination outside working dirs.

facts.behavior: Edit rules apply to all built-in tools that edit files. Read rules are applied on a 'best-effort' basis to built-in read tools (Grep, Glob), @file mentions, IDE selection context, pasted image paths and @-mentioned directory listings. A Read deny rule also blocks Edit and Write on that path (creating files), but not NotebookEdit (add Edit deny). Read/Edit denies apply to Bash file commands Claude Code recognizes (cat, head, tail, sed, tee) and redirection targets. .claudeignore has no effect; use Read deny rules.
facts.limits: They do not apply to commands that read files without naming them (grep -r pattern .) or to arbitrary subprocesses (a Python/Node script opening files); for OS-level enforcement enable the sandbox. Path rules for Write, NotebookEdit, Glob, MultiEdit are accepted but never match - use Edit(path) and Read(path).

facts.behavior: gitignore syntax. //path = absolute from filesystem root; ~/path = home; /path = relative to settings source (project/local settings: primary working directory; user settings: ~/.claude; --settings file: that file's directory; CLI/session rules: primary working directory); path or ./path = relative to cwd. Bare filenames match any depth. Deny/ask rule Read(secrets/**) matches at any depth; allow Edit(src/**) matches only <cwd>/src. A deny/ask pattern starting with ! is a gitignore negation carving out earlier rules from the same source only.
facts.limits: '/Users/alice/file' is not absolute (single slash anchors at settings source). ! carve-out can't cross sources, can't reach //, ~/ or / anchored rules, and can't reopen a file inside a directory a rule blocks as a whole. Local-settings rules anchor at the session's primary working directory, not repo root.

facts.behavior: Permission check covers both the requested path and the resolved target. Allow rules apply only when both match; deny rules apply when either matches. Edit/Write refuse to write when the path itself is a symlink and direct Claude to the target. Tools confirm a path still resolves to the approved location when opening.
facts.limits: Writes can still pass through a symlinked parent directory or via Bash/PowerShell; in acceptEdits mode those resolving outside working dirs aren't auto-approved; in auto mode they prompt.

facts.behavior: WebFetch(domain:example.com) matches hostname only, case-insensitive, supports * wildcards (v2.1.172+); *.example.com matches subdomains at any depth but not apex; mid-position wildcard matches only text between dots. Bare WebFetch deny removes the tool; WebFetch(domain:*) deny keeps tool and refuses each fetch and also denies sandboxed command network access. Bare WebFetch allow doesn't change sandbox allowlist.
facts.limits: WebFetch alone doesn't prevent network access: if Bash is allowed, Claude can use curl/wget. A bare WebFetch deny/ask doesn't apply to Artifact reads (domain: rule covering claude.ai does).

facts.feature: MCP, Agent, Cd and PowerShell rules
facts.behavior: MCP: mcp__<server> or mcp__<server>__* matches whole server; mcp__<server>__<tool> one tool; plugin servers use mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__. Agent(Name) deny disables a subagent (e.g. Agent(Explore)). Cd rules govern /cd only (not model-invocable); any Cd allow rule switches /cd to allowlist mode. PowerShell(...) rules mirror Bash, aliases canonicalized, case-insensitive.
facts.limits: Org-set connector 'ask' overrides allow rules even in auto/bypassPermissions (denied in dontAsk). In Cowork, Bash deny rules extend to mcp__workspace__bash but Bash allow rules never carry over.

facts.behavior: Default access is the launch directory (primary working directory until /cd). Extend with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories. Files in additional directories follow same rules (readable without prompts). permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories / blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories (v2.1.314+) make the file tools refuse outside paths in every mode including bypassPermissions.
facts.limits: Additional directories grant file access, not configuration: only --add-dir/ /add-dir (not settings additionalDirectories) load skills, commands, subagents, and enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces keys; CLAUDE.md only with CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1. blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories doesn't limit shell commands, MCP tools, or hook programs (use sandboxing). Removing blockReads... mid-session doesn't lift it in the running session. Network paths can't be added as working dirs.

facts.behavior: /cd <path> keeps the conversation, loads new directory's CLAUDE.md, applies new directory's project settings (permission rules, hooks), .mcp.json servers, plugins, skills, subagents and env; prompts for workspace trust if untrusted and lists allow rules, additional directories, hooks, helper commands it would activate. Hooks still receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to the original session start root.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.246+ to read project files from new directory. Restrictable with Cd permission rules.

facts.behavior: Permissions control which tools/files/domains Claude can use (apply to every tool); sandboxing is OS-level enforcement for Bash, PowerShell, Monitor commands and child processes. Docs recommend both for defense in depth; sandbox paths/domains and permission rules merge. With sandbox enabled and autoAllowBashIfSandboxed default true, sandboxed Bash runs without prompting even with a bare Bash ask rule.
facts.limits: Content-scoped ask rules (Bash(git push *)) still prompt; plan mode skips the substitution; excluded commands respect bare Bash ask rule.

facts.feature: Workspace trust for project allow rules
facts.behavior: permissions.allow rules and permissions.additionalDirectories in a project's .claude/settings.json apply only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted; deny and ask rules apply immediately. Trust keyed on git repo root (main checkout for worktrees). .claude/settings.local.json allow rules apply without trust while untracked; if tracked in git or .claude is a symlink, held until trusted.
facts.limits: Dialog is interactive only; -p/SDK never shows it and project allow rules are not used (stderr warning 'this workspace has not been trusted'). In home directory trust is session-only.

facts.behavior: User ~/.claude/settings.json; shared project .claude/settings.json (commit it); project local .claude/settings.local.json (Claude Code adds **/.claude/settings.local.json to global git excludes the first time it writes it); managed (managed-settings.json, MDM, server-managed). Separate ~/.claude.json holds account details, MCP configs, per-project trust and global config keys. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates home-directory files. Settings files are strict JSON (comments/trailing commas are errors).
facts.limits: If you create settings.local.json by hand you must gitignore it yourself. Shared settings read from the session's primary working directory (start Claude at repo root). Cloud sessions read shared project settings only; user/local settings not read; multi-repo cloud sessions read only enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces.

facts.behavior: Highest first: managed settings, command line (--settings), project local, shared project, user. A higher level overrides the same key lower down. Environment variables are not a level; per-pair (ANTHROPIC_MODEL overrides model key; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL only when no file sets model). An env block inside a settings file follows the levels.
facts.limits: Managed model is a default not a lock (locks are availableModels/deniedModels). Other flags (--model) aren't part of the stack. Some values can't come from repo files (permissions.defaultMode auto/bypassPermissions from project/local; telemetry env vars in project/local env).

facts.behavior: Same list key (e.g. permissions.allow) in multiple files is combined, not replaced. Exceptions: fallbackModel (whole value from highest-precedence file), modelPicker (whole value, ignored in project/local), availableModels (managed list applied as-is), modelSettings (per model).
facts.limits: Deny from any scope beats allow from any scope: 'If a tool is denied at any level, no other level can allow it'; a managed deny can't be overridden by --allowedTools; --disallowedTools can add restrictions beyond managed. A local-file 'allow' doesn't outrank an ask rule from project/managed file.

facts.feature: Reload behavior: when settings edits take effect
facts.behavior: Claude Code watches settings files and reloads them, applying most edits (permissions, hooks, apiKeyHelper) to the running session without restart; ConfigChange hook runs per settings-file change. Settings file created mid-session is loaded if its folder existed at start. Managed settings via MDM/console reach a running session on a schedule (server-managed polled hourly; MDM checked every 30 minutes).
facts.limits: Some keys are read only at session start (e.g. model via /model, requiredMinimumVersion). Removing permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories mid-session doesn't lift the block until restart.

facts.behavior: /status shows 'Setting sources' (which files loaded, and how managed settings arrived); claude doctor lists rejected entries. Settings Error (invalid JSON/rejected value in user/project/local file) shows a dialog at interactive start; Settings Warning for individual bad entries (malformed permission rule, unknown hook event) skips just those values. /permissions lists all rules and the source file of each.
facts.limits: /status doesn't show which file supplied each key. In -p no dialog; broken file/values skipped silently (run claude doctor). $schema URL gives editor validation but can lag newest keys.

facts.behavior: --settings <file-or-json> applies above user/project/local and below managed; can set any key the user settings file can; lasts one session, writes nothing. Some keys have own flags (--model, --effort) or env vars.
facts.limits: Can't set Managed or Global config keys. Cannot override managed values.

facts.behavior: Server-managed settings (claude.ai admin console or self-hosted Claude apps gateway; fetched at startup, polled hourly); MDM/OS policy (macOS configuration profile, Windows HKLM registry value 'Settings' under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode; read at startup, checked every 30 minutes); managed-settings.json file (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\) plus optional managed-settings.d/ drop-in dir; HKCU registry fallback; SDK managedSettings from an embedding host.
facts.limits: Claude Code doesn't read legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json. Local device file/MDM doesn't reach cloud sessions (only server-managed does); console can't target groups. Local admins can edit the managed source; managed settings bind only Claude Code, not other tools calling the API. Server-managed cache edits last only until next fetch. HKCU used only if no admin document present.

facts.feature: Precedence within the managed tier and managed-settings.d merge
facts.behavior: By default the first source with a policy key supplies the policy and the rest are skipped; order: remote/server-managed, MDM/OS policy, managed files (managed-settings.d/*.json plus managed-settings.json), HKCU. managedSourcesBehavior:'merge' composes all admin sources. Within files: managed-settings.json merged first, then drop-ins alphabetically; single values: later replaces; lists: combine and dedupe; nested blocks: merge key by key.
facts.limits: Some keys read from every admin source (allowManagedMcpServersOnly, sandbox allowManagedDomainsOnly/allowManagedReadPathsOnly). Hidden files and non-.json ignored. A file with only control keys doesn't count as a policy.

facts.behavior: Read only from a managed source (no effect in user/project files): allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly (makes managed settings the only source of permission rules; drops parent-supplied allow rules and additionalDirectories), allowManagedMcpServersOnly, sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly, sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly, strictPluginOnlyCustomization, disableSideloadFlags, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh (fail-closed startup), policyHelper, managedMcpServers, strictKnownMarketplaces, blockedMarketplaces, disableCommandPluginSources, channelsEnabled, allowedChannelPlugins, managedSourcesBehavior, parentSettingsBehavior, wslInheritsWindowsSettings. Also availableModels/deniedModels, forceLoginMethod/forceLoginOrgUUID, allowedProviders, requiredMinimumVersion.
facts.limits: Most are locks: the governed value is an ordinary key any level can set; the lock tells Claude Code to honor only the managed value. For any key not in the doc's table, check the Scope column of the settings reference index.

facts.feature: Exceptions to managed precedence (stricter lower-level value honored)
facts.behavior: For restrictive keys a stricter lower-scope value still counts over managed: disableClaudeAiConnectors true (any scope), enableArtifact false/disableArtifact true (any scope), isolatePeerMachines true, permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories true (v2.1.257+), permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories true (v2.1.314+), autoMode.classifyAllShell true (user or --settings), remoteControlAtStartup false (project/local), crossSessionInbound stricter value (project/local), useAutoModeDuringPlan/syncClaudeAiSkills/syncClaudeAiPlugins false (managed, --settings, user, local but not shared project), maxEffortLevel lowest cap wins.
facts.limits: A project/local 'true' for remoteControlAtStartup is ignored; shared-project false is ignored for useAutoModeDuringPlan/sync* keys. An app setting CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST takes its own model config over managed model keys.

facts.feature: Invalid managed entries and fail-closed keys
facts.behavior: Invalid managed entries are repaired or dropped with warning; keys with a single restrictive value (allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, disableAutoMode, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt) read as that value until fixed. If a permissions deny or ask list can't be read, allow and additionalDirectories are withheld. allowedProviders fails to empty allowlist; strictKnownMarketplaces to empty allowlist. A managed document present but not parseable JSON makes Claude Code refuse to start.
facts.limits: An absent managed file/profile/registry value is not a failure. Malformed HKCU never blocks launch. Pre-v2.1.283 sandbox drops all fields on one invalid value.

facts.feature: Managed settings: verifying and developer limits
facts.behavior: /status 'Setting sources' line names the managed source ((HKCU), file, MDM, remote); claude doctor reports dropped entries. A developer's own settings, --settings, project files never override a managed value.
facts.limits: Managed model and autoCompactWindow are defaults (--model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, --autocompact still apply); deploy availableModels to restrict. Long-lived sessions may lag a rollout; requiredMinimumVersion blocks outdated binaries from starting but doesn't end running sessions. Cowork sessions don't fetch server-managed settings but read device policy unless requireCoworkFullVmSandbox.

facts.feature: Authentication precedence and login restriction (iam page, now /authentication)
facts.behavior: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam.md serves the Authentication page. Credential order: cloud provider env (Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Anthropic profile/federation, subscription OAuth from /login. Managed forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID restrict logins to a method/org (claude.ai logins to other orgs refused, exit at startup); allowedProviders (v2.1.285+) restricts which API providers a managed machine may use. Under forceLoginOrgUUID/forceLoginMethod sessions using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper are blocked at startup.
facts.limits: This page covers authentication, not permission rules (permissions content is at /permissions). forceLoginOrgUUID not checked for Console credentials; setup-token and /install-github-app enforce only forceLoginMethod; server-managed-only allowedProviders is 'a convenience, not enforcement'. Server-managed settings arrive only after authenticating, so can't redirect a first login.

facts.behavior: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/configuration.md resolves to the 'Settings files and precedence' page (same content as /settings); full key list lives at /settings-reference, which was not among the assigned URLs.
facts.limits: Per-key detail (e.g. exact effects of allowManagedHooksOnly) lives in settings-reference, not read.

unreachable: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md (not in assigned list; linked for per-key detail such as 'what runs under allowManagedHooksOnly', not read)

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md characters 200000-284276 (final ~84k characters, covering later sections such as additional hook reference material, were not read; Stop/ConfigChange/Worktree sections were obtained from the hooks.md 100000-200000 slice and the hooks guide)
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md (protected paths table, auto-mode classifier details; not in assigned list, not read)

area: Plugins: components, marketplaces, plugin validate, plugin details and token cost, rules/CLAUDE.md in plugins (as of 2026-11-03)

facts.behavior: A Claude Code plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit. The manifest is .claude-plugin/plugin.json; it is optional, and only `name` is required in it. Without a manifest Claude Code loads components found in the standard layout.
facts.limits: Unrecognized top-level manifest keys are stripped (plugin still loads). Unknown keys inside userConfig options, channels entries, lspServers configs or monitors entries are errors and the plugin does not load. All non-manifest files go at plugin root, not inside .claude-plugin/.

facts.feature: Plugin components (skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP, LSP, monitors, output styles, themes, workflows, bin/, settings.json, channels, hooks module/mods)
facts.behavior: Standard layout: skills/<name>/SKILL.md; commands/ (flat .md, older format, prefer skills); agents/; hooks/hooks.json; .mcp.json; .lsp.json; output-styles/; workflows/; themes/; monitors/monitors.json; bin/ (on Bash tool PATH while enabled); settings.json. Everything is namespaced under the plugin name (e.g. /my-plugin:review, my-plugin:security-reviewer, mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>).
facts.limits: No component type for rules or CLAUDE.md. Plugin bin/ comes after the user's own PATH entries so it cannot shadow system commands. claude.ai and Cowork do not install a plugin with a top-level bin/. Plugin monitors do not start with -p, and do not load for project-scope repository plugins. A different component set loads on claude.ai/Cowork.

facts.feature: Plugins cannot ship rules or CLAUDE.md (no rules component)
facts.behavior: Docs: 'A CLAUDE.md at the plugin root isn't loaded as context, and claude plugin validate warns when it finds one. To include instructions that load into Claude's context, put them in a skill.' Validator warning text: 'CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is not loaded as project context'. The documented component list (skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP, LSP, monitors, output styles, themes, workflows, bin, settings, channels) has no .claude/rules/ or paths:-scoped rules component.
facts.limits: The docs do not describe any way for a plugin to deliver .claude/rules files or CLAUDE.md content. Instructions can be shipped only as a skill (loaded when its description matches), an output style, or a hook (for rules that must hold every time). The docs do not say whether a skill can be always-loaded.

facts.feature: Hook vs skill guidance for plugin rules
facts.behavior: Docs: 'If a rule must hold every time, such as blocking edits to protected files, add it to the plugin as a hook rather than a skill.' Plugin hooks are registered when a session loads the plugin and fire on their events from then on, without waiting for a plugin skill to be used.
facts.limits: Advisory guidance only; use matcher to narrow when a hook runs.

facts.feature: Plugin hooks (hooks/hooks.json and manifest hooks key)
facts.behavior: hooks/hooks.json (top-level 'hooks' wrapper, same shape as settings.json hooks) and the manifest `hooks` key (path, inline object, or array) are merged. Hook processes get CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>. A `modules` key in hooks/hooks.json lists JavaScript hooks modules (a plugin with one is a 'mod').
facts.limits: A hooks file without the top-level 'hooks' wrapper fails to load. Hooks in a marketplace entry load only as an inline object; a file path or array passes validate but never runs. When two enabled plugins share a manifest name, only one registers its hooks.json hooks (the other gets a note in /plugin Errors tab). Shell-form hook commands reject ${user_config.*}. Managed allowManagedHooksOnly does not trust hooks from plugins users enable themselves.

facts.behavior: Skill is skills/<dir>/SKILL.md, command name /<plugin>:<dir>; frontmatter name replaces the last segment only. Commands (commands/*.md) take the same frontmatter as skills. 'skills' manifest key ADDS to the default skills/ scan; 'commands' key REPLACES commands/ scan. A SKILL.md at plugin root with no skills/ dir and no skills key loads as a single skill (set frontmatter name).
facts.limits: validate does not check a SKILL.md at the plugin root.

facts.behavior: Supported frontmatter: name, description, model, effort, maxTurns, autoCompactWindow, tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, omitClaudeMd, isolation (only "worktree"), color, and experimental cacheTtl. Subfolders of agents/ become part of the scoped name (my-plugin:review:security). Agents manifest key replaces the agents/ scan and accepts .md files only, not directories.
facts.limits: Ignored fields in plugin agents: permissionMode, hooks, mcpServers, initialPrompt. A name over 256 characters is ignored (file name used). Unparseable frontmatter still loads the agent with all fields ignored and description 'Agent from <plugin> plugin'.

facts.behavior: A settings.json at plugin root (or inline `settings` manifest key) applies while the plugin is enabled. Only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` take effect.
facts.limits: Every other key is dropped. settings.json wins over the manifest settings key when it sets a supported key. Plugin defaults are the lowest settings layer, so a user's own agent setting overrides it. If two plugins set the same key, the last loaded wins.

facts.behavior: Declared in .mcp.json or manifest mcpServers (path, inline map, .mcpb/.dxt bundle path or https URL). Server name shows as plugin:<plugin>:<server>; tool names mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} substituted in command, args, env. /reload-plugins keeps unchanged connections.
facts.limits: Hook matcher on server name alone never fires; use the full tool name. Project-scope (repository) plugins: MCP bundles and files outside the plugin dir are skipped, and servers need the same per-server approval as project .mcp.json. Local stdio servers do not run on claude.ai. A reload that adds or removes a plugin MCP server may be refused to protect the prompt cache unless --force.

facts.behavior: Declared in .lsp.json or manifest lspServers; plugin configures the connection but does not install the language-server binary. One server per file extension; first registered wins on conflict.
facts.limits: validate does not read .lsp.json (an invalid entry makes the whole file skipped at load, shown in /plugin Errors tab). validate does check lspServers paths in the manifest (v2.1.283+).

facts.behavior: monitors/monitors.json (or experimental.monitors) defines shell commands that run in the background for the session; output reaches Claude as notifications. 'when' can be always or on-skill-invoke:<skill>.
facts.limits: Do not start with -p; do not load for repository (project-scope) plugins; run with full user permissions outside the sandbox; cannot reference ${user_config.*}; not stopped when plugin is disabled mid-session; auto-update needs a session restart for monitors.

facts.behavior: Every component path must start with ./ (skills also accepts "."), resolve inside the plugin root, and exist. Replace default: commands, agents, outputStyles, workflows, experimental.themes, experimental.monitors. Add to default: skills. Merge: hooks, mcpServers, lspServers. Setting a replacing key makes the default folder ignored with warning 'Default <folder>/ folder is ignored because the manifest sets "<key>"'.
facts.limits: Paths containing .. , escaping the plugin root, or missing do not load. On macOS/Linux a path containing a backslash is rejected. Symlinks leading outside the plugin are rejected except links between plugins in one marketplace.

facts.feature: Plugin name rules and reserved names
facts.behavior: name must be non-empty, no spaces, @, :, path separators, control or bidi characters; kebab-case recommended. validate errors for names starting claude-, anthropic-, anthropics-, cc-plugin-, or equal to claude/anthropic/anthropics/claude-code/claude-mods, or 'official' beside claude/anthropic; warns when claude/anthropic/anthropics is a whole word elsewhere. claude plugin init and tag refuse a name that draws the error.
facts.limits: Claude Code still installs and loads a plugin whose name validate rejects.

facts.behavior: `version` in plugin.json pins users to that version until changed (not checked against semver). Version precedence: manifest version, then marketplace entry version, then source-derived (12-char commit SHA for github/url/git-subdir/relative in git marketplace; sha256 prefix for archive; 'unknown' for npm and non-git local). Update detection depends on the computed version; background auto-update refreshes marketplaces with autoUpdate on (default on for official marketplaces, off for others).
facts.limits: If version is pinned, new commits do not reach users until the string changes. Updated plugins need /reload-plugins or restart to apply. Previous version cache dirs are deleted 14 days after update/uninstall. DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER / DISABLE_UPDATES / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC turn auto-update off unless FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS=1.

facts.behavior: userConfig declares values Claude Code prompts for at enable (types string, number, boolean, directory, file; fields title, description required, sensitive, default, options, multiple, min/max). Non-sensitive values saved under pluginConfigs in settings.json; sensitive values go to the platform secure credential store. Referenced as ${user_config.KEY} (MCP/LSP config, exec-form hook args, skill/agent content - sensitive values become a placeholder in skill/agent content) or env CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> for hooks.
facts.limits: `claude plugin install` never prompts; use --config KEY=VALUE or `claude plugin configure --values-stdin`. Options field needs v2.1.271+. ${user_config.*} rejected in shell-form hook commands, monitor commands and MCP headersHelper.

facts.feature: Plugin path variables and persistent data
facts.behavior: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (installed version dir, changes on update), ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (~/.claude/plugins/data/<id>/, survives updates, deleted on uninstall from last scope unless --keep-data), ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}. Substituted in hook/monitor commands, MCP/LSP config, and skill/command/agent Markdown bodies.
facts.limits: Variables are not in the environment of commands Claude runs through the Bash tool. Do not write state under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. Marketplace plugins are copied to cache so files outside the plugin dir (../shared) are not present.

facts.behavior: `dependencies` lists plugins that must be enabled (name, name@marketplace, or object with version). `claude plugin prune` removes auto-installed dependencies no longer needed. For marketplace-installed plugins Claude Code installs Node dependencies into the cached copy when a package.json plus npm (package-lock.json / npm-shrinkwrap.json) or bun.lock lockfile exists.
facts.limits: Node install: registry packages only, pinned in lockfile, --ignore-scripts, 60-second timeout, skipped for yarn.lock/pnpm-lock/bun.lockb, cannot be disabled. Prune never removes plugins the user installed. Cross-marketplace dependencies need allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn.

facts.behavior: `claude plugin|plugins` subcommands: configure, details, disable, enable, eval, help, init|new (scaffold at ~/.claude/skills/<name>/), install|i, list, marketplace (add, list, remove|rm, update), prune|autoremove, tag, test (runs a mod's tests), uninstall|remove, update, validate. In-session: /plugin, /reload-plugins; `plugin details`, `update`, `prune`, `eval`, `init`, `test` have no session form (validate does: /plugin validate <path>).
facts.limits: claude plugin update requires restart to apply. install scope defaults to user (user, project, local). update scope also allows managed. prune and install require -y when non-TTY for confirmations.
facts.citation: claude plugin --help ; claude plugin install --help ; claude plugin update --help ; claude plugin prune --help ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference.md

facts.behavior: CLI help: 'Validate a plugin or marketplace manifest, or the skills, agents, and commands in a directory'. Flags: --json (report as JSON, same exit codes), --strict ('Treat warnings as errors (exit 1). Use in CI to fail on unrecognized fields, missing metadata, and other issues that the runtime tolerates'), --profile directory (also exit 1 when Anthropic's plugin directory would refuse a submission on a check this command runs, e.g. missing README; with --strict also fails on warnings). Exit 0 passed (or passed with warnings), 1 failed, 2 unexpected error. Directory target: picks marketplace.json first, else plugin.json, else component files by directory name; with both marketplace.json and plugin.json (v2.1.289+) validates both. Checks manifest types and required fields, path existence/containment, name rules, MCP server entries in .mcp.json/manifest (v2.1.281+: dropped entries, undeclared ${user_config.KEY}, invalid url as errors; http:// or ws:// to non-loopback and literal-credential-looking headers as warnings), agent/skill/command frontmatter, shell-form ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} quoting in hooks files (warning), and warns on CLAUDE.md at plugin root.
facts.limits: It is a CI-style check, not runtime enforcement: Claude Code tolerates warnings. Does not check a SKILL.md at plugin root, does not read .lsp.json, does not follow symlinks inside the directory, and in a marketplace-directory run does not open skill/agent/command/hook files or MCP files of plugins listed in other directories (validate each plugin directory). Does not catch fetch errors for a marketplace entry source or a missing relative source directory (install fails with 'Source path does not exist'). A README 'Advice' block (v2.1.295+) never changes exit code. Unknown top-level plugin.json fields are warnings; in a marketplace entry the directory-listing fields are reported as unknown.

facts.feature: claude plugin details (component inventory and projected token cost)
facts.behavior: CLI help: 'Show a plugin's component inventory and projected token cost'; takes <name> or name@marketplace and no flags beyond --help. Prints name, version, description, source, then 'Component inventory' (skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers; commands counted with skills), 'Projected token cost' (Always-on tokens added to every session), and 'Per-component (rounded)' always-on vs on-invoke per skill/agent/command. Always-on counts each component's name plus its description and when_to_use frontmatter; on-invoke is the body that loads only when the component runs.
facts.limits: Estimates only ('Token counts are estimates and may differ from actual usage'). Hooks are labeled harness-only with no model-context cost; MCP servers get no estimate ('tool schemas resolved at runtime; not counted' - use /context MCP tools category). Plugin must be loaded (installed, in a skills dir, or --plugin-dir/--plugin-url in the same command) else exits 1. Run in shell, not in a session. No built-in budget or threshold: it only reports.

facts.behavior: An enabled plugin is part of every session: for each skill, agent, and command Claude can invoke on its own, the name and description are in context every turn and count toward usage, even if nothing from the plugin runs; full text loads only on use. Plugin MCP server cost follows MCP tool search. Lower it by shortening skill/agent descriptions or splitting the plugin. Official-marketplace plugins show a 'Context cost' (Every turn / When invoked) in /plugin before install, highlighted at 2,000 tokens or more.
facts.limits: Your own marketplace's plugins show no Context cost section. Shorter descriptions can stop skills triggering. No automatic cap or warning in Claude Code for user-authored plugins.

facts.behavior: /plugin Installed tab moves a marketplace-installed plugin under 'Not used recently' after at least 14 days and 10 sessions unused (with a Last used: line). /skill-doctor flags skills never invoked; /doctor recommends disabling unused plugins; /usage attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers. OpenTelemetry events: claude_code.plugin_installed, plugin_loaded, skill_activated, hook_plugin_metrics (official-marketplace only); Analytics API GET /v1/organizations/analytics/plugins on Enterprise.
facts.limits: Not-used header never shows for --plugin-dir/skills-dir plugins, managed or seed-dir plugins, or plugins with a theme, output style, monitor or workflow, or when strictKnownMarketplaces is set. Third-party plugin names are redacted in telemetry unless OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1. Claude Code does not report usage back to plugin authors.

facts.behavior: A marketplace is a directory/repo with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json listing plugins and where to fetch each. Required top-level: name, owner (owner.name required), plugins. Other fields: description, version, metadata.pluginRoot, forceRemoveDeletedPlugins, allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn, renames. Plugin entry requires name and source; also accepts every plugin.json field (except directory-listing fields), plus category, tags, strict, relevance, defaultEnabled, displayName, headers, headersHelper. Each entry is validated on its own.
facts.limits: Unknown top-level or entry keys are ignored at load (typos load silently; validate warns). A user cannot register two marketplaces with the same name. Marketplace/plugin names: letters, digits, . _ - starting with letter/digit, no '..'; invalid names cannot be installed. Duplicate plugin names in one marketplace are a validate error.

facts.behavior: Reserved: official names (claude-code-marketplace, claude-code-plugins, claude-plugins-official, anthropic-marketplace, anthropic-plugins, agent-skills, anthropic-agent-skills, etc.), community names, names impersonating them, non-ASCII names, inline/builtin/skills-dir/synced/claude-plugin-test, npm/pip/uv/cargo/github/gh, JS-object member names, names starting claudeai-.
facts.limits: Official names are allowed only for marketplaces sourced from github.com/anthropics/. validate flags some names; others (the exact official names) pass validate and are refused only at `marketplace add`.

facts.feature: Plugin sources in a marketplace entry
facts.behavior: source is a relative path string (must start ./ , or bare name under metadata.pluginRoot) or an object: github (repo, ref, sha), url (git URL, ref, sha), git-subdir (url, path, ref, sha; sparse checkout), npm (package, version, registry; install scripts never run), archive (https zip, optional sha256), command (runs a command on the user's machine printing the plugin dir; copy or link mode). ref/sha pin git sources.
facts.limits: Relative paths with .. fail validate; relative paths cannot resolve for url-type or settings-type marketplaces. Missing relative directory passes validate but fails at install. archive URL must be https and not loopback/link-local/metadata. command source can be disabled by admins (disableCommandPluginSources) and link mode is refused on Windows. npm refuses git addresses, github/gitlab tarballs, http tarballs.

facts.feature: Strict mode and entry vs plugin.json precedence
facts.behavior: strict (default true): when the plugin has its own plugin.json, entry commands/agents/skills/hooks/outputStyles/themes are appended to it (hooks matchers replace the manifest's per event). With no plugin.json the entry is the manifest. version: manifest overrides entry; defaultEnabled and display fields: entry overrides manifest.
facts.limits: strict:false with plugin.json present and any entry component field fails to load ('Plugin <name> has conflicting manifests'). Entry mcpServers, lspServers, userConfig, channels do not apply when plugin.json exists. Entry name vs manifest name: install id uses the entry name, components namespaced by manifest name; installing by the manifest name when they differ fails.

facts.behavior: `claude plugin marketplace add <source>` (URL, path, or GitHub repo) registers a marketplace (written to extraKnownMarketplaces in user settings); install id is <plugin>@<marketplace>; `marketplace update [name]` refreshes (all if none named); `marketplace remove|rm` removes the marketplace and uninstalls its plugins. Anthropic's official marketplace is auto-added on first interactive terminal session unless managed policy blocks it; the community marketplace is not auto-added. Edits to a plugin in a locally-added (path) marketplace take effect at next session start or /reload-plugins without a version bump.
facts.limits: Hosted-marketplace users receive plugin copies from cache keyed by version. Private repos need user git credentials. Declared marketplaces and plugins not on disk are fetched in the background after session start, not at load. Project settings enabledPlugins for external-source plugins do not auto-fetch ('is enabled in project settings but isn't installed').

facts.behavior: Creates an annotated git tag {name}--v{version} for a plugin release, validating that plugin.json and any enclosing marketplace entry agree on version. Flags: --dry-run, -f/--force, -m/--message, --push, --remote.
facts.limits: Exits 1 if no version, tag already exists, or dirty working tree (unless --force). If push fails the local tag remains.

facts.behavior: Install scopes: user (all projects), project (committed .claude/settings.json, each collaborator still installs), local (this repo, you only). enabledPlugins precedence low to high: --add-dir, user, project, local, flag (--settings), managed (true force-enables, false blocks; nothing overrides). Project-scope plugins load only after the workspace trust check.
facts.limits: Claude Code does not scan a project's .claude/plugins/ directory; share via enabledPlugins in .claude/settings.json or place plugin dirs under .claude/skills/ (skills-dir plugins load only from the session's primary working directory, not parents). Cloud sessions do not load local-settings plugins and do not add repository extraKnownMarketplaces.

facts.feature: Session-only and skills-dir plugins (--plugin-dir, --plugin-url, claude plugin init)
facts.behavior: --plugin-dir <path or .zip> and --plugin-url load a plugin for one session without installing (id <name>@inline); a plugin dir with .claude-plugin/plugin.json saved under ~/.claude/skills/ or .claude/skills/ loads as <name>@skills-dir. `claude plugin init <name>` scaffolds at ~/.claude/skills/<name>/. A session-only plugin overrides a same-named installed plugin.
facts.limits: Admin disableSideloadFlags rejects --plugin-dir/--plugin-url/CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS; strictKnownMarketplaces without a skills-dir entry or strictPluginOnlyCustomization stops skills-dir plugins loading silently. Name-conflict order: managed enabledPlugins > session-only > installed marketplace > skills-dir > claude.ai synced.

facts.feature: Managed policy controls for plugins and marketplaces
facts.behavior: Managed-settings keys: strictKnownMarketplaces (allowlist of marketplace sources; [] blocks all including official), blockedMarketplaces (checked first), enabledPlugins (true force-enables, false blocks and hides), extraKnownMarketplaces, syncClaudeAiPlugins, disableSideloadFlags, disableCommandPluginSources, allowManagedHooksOnly, strictPluginOnlyCustomization, pluginSuggestionMarketplaces, pluginTrustMessage, allowedChannelPlugins. Lists are applied before download and again at session start (installed plugin from a no-longer-allowed source does not load).
facts.limits: Allowlist matches marketplace sources, not entries inside an allowed marketplace (block a single plugin with managed enabledPlugins false). Allowlist does not cover --plugin-dir (use disableSideloadFlags) or claude.ai-synced plugins (use syncClaudeAiPlugins false). No key hides /plugin or targets per-user groups from server-managed settings. Only one managed source applies by default unless managedSourcesBehavior is merge.

facts.behavior: Plugins run code as the user; marketplaces are tiered official, community, third-party (a coworker's or organization's marketplace is third-party). Docs say 'Whatever the tier, a plugin you install can run code with your user privileges' and point to Plugin security and trust for review before install. npm-source install scripts never run; Node dependency install disables lifecycle scripts.
facts.limits: No sandboxing of plugin hooks, monitors, or MCP servers described; monitors run outside the sandbox. Trust review is the user's responsibility.

facts.behavior: `claude plugin eval [target]` runs eval cases (evals/**/case.yaml or prompt.md + graders/*.md) against a plugin and reports scored results, with a no-plugin baseline arm; `claude plugin test [dir]` runs *.test.ts/.tsx tests of a mod with no session or network.
facts.limits: Eval runs on the user's machine as the user; only evaluate trusted plugins; first run in an untrusted plugin directory asks confirmation (--trust-plugin answers for CI). Bundled suite passing is not a security vetting.

facts.behavior: icon, documentationUrl, supportUrl, privacyPolicyUrl, termsOfServiceUrl in plugin.json are read only by Anthropic's directory on submission; `metadata` is a free-form object Claude Code does not read.
facts.limits: Claude Code ignores them at load. Valid only in plugin.json, not marketplace entries (validate reports them there as unknown). validate on versions before 2.1.281 warns Unknown field for them.
