area: skills, slash commands, disable-model-invocation, skill frontmatter, skill-doctor, plugin init scaffolding

facts.behavior: A skill is a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and Markdown instructions; Claude uses it when relevant or you invoke it with /skill-name. 'Custom commands are merged into skills': .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy. Existing .claude/commands/ files keep working and support the same frontmatter except name and paths.
facts.limits: If a skill and a .claude/commands/ file share a name, the skill wins. Docs say prefer skills for new work.

facts.behavior: Enterprise (managed settings .claude/skills/), Personal (~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md), Project (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md), Nested (<subdir>/.claude/skills/), Additional directory (--add-dir), Plugin (<plugin>/skills/, as /plugin-name:skill-name), claude.ai account sync. Same name across levels: enterprise over personal, personal over project; plugin skills are namespaced and never conflict.
facts.limits: Personal skills are not read by Cowork or cloud sessions (they load only claude.ai-enabled skills or skills committed to the repo). Project skills not loaded in cloud threads in a project. permissions.additionalDirectories grants file access only and loads no skills.

facts.feature: Monorepo, nested, worktree and added-directory skill loading
facts.behavior: Claude loads project skills from the start directory and each parent up to the repo root. In a linked git worktree the parent search stops at the worktree root; from v2.1.277, if the worktree has no .claude/skills, the main checkout's project skills load. Nested subdirectory skills load the first time Claude reads or edits a file there; /add-dir loads sooner (v2.1.257+); /cd adds the new directory's project skills (v2.1.246+). Same-name clashes with an added directory get a prefix such as /cli:verify (v2.1.309+).
facts.limits: Live detection watches only .claude/skills/ in added directories; restart after changing .claude/commands/ or .claude/agents/ there. A root deploy and nested apps/web deploy both load; /deploy runs the root one, /apps/web:deploy the nested one.

facts.behavior: Claude Code watches ~/.claude/skills/, project .claude/skills/, and .claude/skills/ in --add-dir directories; changes apply without restart. /reload-skills re-scans skill and command directories and reports how many were added or removed.
facts.limits: Run /reload-skills after creating a new top-level skills directory mid-session. Detection covers SKILL.md text only; for plugin skill folders, changes to hooks/, .mcp.json, agents/, output-styles/ need /reload-plugins. Bare mode disables watching.

facts.behavior: Frontmatter is read only if the opening --- is the file's first line (otherwise the whole file is content). If the YAML does not parse, the skill loads with no fields set (so /skill-name works but Claude cannot match on description). Field names must match exactly; unknown fields are ignored without error. Booleans accept true/false, yes/no, on/off, 1/0 in any case. Only description is recommended.
facts.limits: No error or warning for unknown or misspelled fields; --debug shows the parse error. claude plugin validate on a skills directory finds SKILL.md files whose frontmatter does not parse (v2.1.233+).

facts.behavior: Command name in the / menu; defaults to the directory name.
facts.limits: Names containing zero-width or control characters, private-use or unassigned characters, direction-changing characters, blanks other than one plain space between words, or < or > are refused. A command file or skill folder with these does not load; a frontmatter name with these is not shown or invocable. Reserved: folder named synced (any capitalization) and anthropic-skills or anthropic-skills:* outside a plugin do not load (startup notice names the item). No max name length stated in the fetched text.

facts.behavior: description says what the skill does and when to use it; falls back to the first non-empty content line. when_to_use is appended to description. Combined text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing (configurable via skillListingMaxDescChars). Docs advise putting the key use case first.
facts.limits: The cap applies regardless of budget. Angle brackets in description/when_to_use display as < and >; use square brackets or argument-hint instead.

facts.behavior: Claude Code loads a listing of skill names and descriptions into context. The listing always contains every skill name, but when it overflows its character budget it drops descriptions starting with the least-invoked skills. Budget scales at 1% of the model's context window. Overflow writes a warning to the debug log (--debug). The Skills row in /context reports the post-budget size. Raise with skillListingBudgetFraction (e.g. 0.02) or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET (fixed char count); set low-priority skills to name-only in skillOverrides.
facts.limits: Warning only in debug log; no user-facing block. /doctor estimates listing cost and biggest contributors.

facts.behavior: true blocks automatic loading by Claude; the description is not in context, the skill still runs when you type /name. Also blocks preloading into subagents and running from session-scoped scheduled tasks. Default false. If Claude tries to invoke such a skill, Claude Code blocks the call and tells Claude not to reproduce the steps another way. Docs pair it with task skills (deploy, commit) and say it removes the skill from Claude's context.
facts.limits: Does not stop the user invoking it. Skills with this set cannot be cycled in /skills visibility. A skill with it set does not count for the pre-commit verify/simplify behavior. Natural-language mention after plain text still counts as permission only if not disabled for Claude; 'Claude invokes: No (on its own)'.

facts.behavior: false hides the skill from the / menu and blocks /name; Claude can still invoke it and the description stays in context. Default true.
facts.limits: Blocks only the user's invocation, not Claude's. Add disable-model-invocation: true to block Claude's Skill tool calls too.

facts.behavior: allowed-tools lists tools usable without prompting during the invoking turn only (space/comma string or list); clears on the next user message. disallowed-tools removes tools from the pool while active; also clears on next message and cannot remove EndConversation while other tools remain. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} work inside Bash rules.
facts.limits: allowed-tools does NOT restrict other tools; every tool stays callable under normal permission settings. Deny and ask rules still override it. Not gated by workspace trust (project skills' allowed-tools apply even in an untrusted folder under -p). Under strictPluginOnlyCustomization listing hooks, a personal/project skill with hooks loses its allowed-tools grant; under allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly (v2.1.282+) allowed-tools from project and personal skills is ignored (/status lists them).

facts.behavior: model sets the model for the current turn only (accepts /model values or inherit; not saved to settings; session model resumes next prompt). effort is low, medium, high, xhigh or max for the current turn.
facts.limits: effort does not override CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. Excluded model values fall back silently; in auto mode and plan mode with classifier, unsupported models also fall back.

facts.feature: Frontmatter fields: context, agent, background (forked skills)
facts.behavior: context: fork runs the skill in a forked subagent; the skill body becomes the subagent's prompt and it does not see conversation history. agent picks Explore, Plan, general-purpose (default) or a custom agent from .claude/agents/. Runs in background by default; background: false waits in the invoking turn.
facts.limits: Not a fork of the current conversation. Waits regardless when non-interactive (-p/SDK), CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1, same skill re-invoked while running, or session-scoped scheduled task. Background forks use a narrower tool set and their edits are outside checkpoints (/rewind does not revert; use git). Explore and Plan start without CLAUDE.md and git status. Pure guideline content returns nothing useful.

facts.behavior: Hooks registered on invocation and kept until the session ends. Docs recommend this (or a settings hook) for rules that must hold every time, since hooks run on every event occurrence whether or not Claude follows the skill.
facts.limits: Applies only after the skill is invoked. Under strictPluginOnlyCustomization with hooks listed, such a skill loses allowed-tools pre-approval.

facts.behavior: Glob patterns limiting automatic activation (comma string or list), relative to the current working directory, same format as path-specific rules.
facts.limits: Does not activate for files outside Claude's current working directory (e.g. sibling git worktree, even if added with /add-dir). Not supported in .claude/commands/ files.

facts.feature: Frontmatter fields: argument-hint, arguments, shell, metadata, license, compatibility
facts.behavior: argument-hint is an autocomplete hint (e.g. [issue-number]); arguments declares named positional args for $name substitution; shell is bash (default) or powershell for !`cmd` blocks; metadata is a free-form map ignored by Claude Code (non-map values dropped); license and compatibility (max 500 characters) are spec fields accepted and not acted on.
facts.limits: metadata contents are not interpreted; do not reuse field names like paths in it. bash shell without Git Bash on Windows fails the invocation.

facts.feature: Frontmatter portability to claude.ai uploads and Skills API
facts.behavior: claude.ai uploads, Skills API and package_skill.py accept only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools. Claude Code skills accept all fields.
facts.limits: Extra keys such as argument-hint fail packaging with a hard error ('Unexpected key(s) in SKILL.md frontmatter: ...'). Body features like dynamic context injection do not work in claude.ai chat or the API.

facts.feature: SKILL.md length guidance and supporting files
facts.behavior: Docs say keep SKILL.md under 500 lines and move detail into reference.md, examples.md, scripts/ referenced from SKILL.md. Skill body loads only when used; once loaded its content stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring cost.
facts.limits: The 500-line figure is guidance; no check or enforcement is described.

facts.behavior: Rendered SKILL.md enters the conversation once as one message and persists; Claude Code does not re-read the file. Re-invoking identical content adds a short 'already loaded' note. On auto-compaction the most recent invocation of each skill is re-attached keeping the first 5,000 tokens of each, within a 25,000-token combined budget filled from the most recently invoked skill; older skills may be dropped.
facts.limits: After compaction only the start of a skill may survive, so put the most important instructions near the top; re-invoke to restore the full content. allowed-tools permissions do not persist.

facts.behavior: $ARGUMENTS (all args; if no placeholder receives input, 'ARGUMENTS: <value>' is appended), $ARGUMENTS[N]/$N (0-based, shell-style quoting), $name, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}, ${CLAUDE_EFFORT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (plugin skills only).
facts.limits: Indexed placeholder with no argument stays literal. Argument values are inserted literally and not re-expanded. Escape with one backslash (\$1.00); the escape does not cover ${CLAUDE_*}. Not substituted in synced claude.ai skills in other local sessions.

facts.behavior: !`command` (or a fenced ```! block) runs before Claude sees the skill and its output replaces the placeholder; run once, output not re-scanned. Inline form only when ! starts a line or follows whitespace. Runs in the session shell's current directory with a 2-minute default timeout. Any failing command aborts the whole invocation (Claude never sees the skill): 'Shell command failed for pattern ...'; bash exit code 1 from search/comparison commands is treated as success; use || true otherwise. Injected commands never prompt: deny rules abort, and outside auto mode anything not allowed (including ask rules) aborts unless pre-approved via allowed-tools.
facts.limits: disableSkillShellExecution: true replaces commands with '[shell command execution disabled by policy]' for user, project, plugin and additional-directory skills (bundled and managed unaffected). Never runs on this machine for skills synced from claude.ai (v2.1.228+).

facts.behavior: A command is only recognized at the start of a message; /deploy staging runs directly. After plain text, '/deploy' as a separate word only counts as permission and Claude judges from wording. At the terminal prompt several skills can be stacked in one message (/write-tests /fix-issue 123): up to six skills expand, trailing text becomes $ARGUMENTS for each.
facts.limits: Expansion stops at the first token that is not an inline user-invocable skill (forked skills or ones like /loop end it). Through the Agent SDK or claude -p only the first skill loads. Leave off the slash to mention a skill without permitting a run. A command sent while Claude is responding is queued, except some run immediately (/status, /tasks, /usage).

facts.feature: Restricting Claude's skill access via permissions
facts.behavior: Add Skill to deny rules to disable all skills; Skill(name) exact and Skill(name *) prefix rules allow or deny specific skills. A deny on an unqualified name also blocks nested skills (v2.1.260+). Synced skills approved with Skill(anthropic-skills:pdf) or Skill(anthropic-skills *). Built-ins like /init and /security-review are reachable through the Skill tool; /compact is not.
facts.limits: Skill(anthropic *) does not match anthropic-skills:*. Allow rules match only the skill's own name and the name in Claude's invocation.

facts.behavior: skillOverrides maps skill name to on, name-only (listed with name only, still in / menu), user-invocable-only (hidden from Claude, in / menu) or off (hidden from Claude and / menu, also Remote Control and SDK lists). Absent means on. /skills lists skills; Space/Enter cycles visibility, t sorts by token count, Esc saves to .claude/settings.local.json.
facts.limits: Plugin skills not affected (use /plugin). Cannot cycle plugin skills, skills with disable-model-invocation: true, or skills with skillOverrides in managed settings or --settings. In user/project/local settings entries match skill names only, not aliases.

facts.behavior: Bundled command that reports each skill's context cost and usage frequency, lists never-invoked skills and where to turn them off starting with the highest cost, and lists plugins not used recently. Interactive: opens in the /plugin manager's Stats tab; with -p prints text. Requires v2.1.252+.
facts.limits: Reporting only; changes nothing. Excludes bundled and enterprise skills. Needs feature-flag fetching (unavailable where skipped). Over Remote Control replies 'Skill usage reports are not available on this connection.' It is not a linter of SKILL.md content.

facts.behavior: /doctor (alias /checkup, bundled skill) runs a setup checkup: installation health, extensions (unused skills, MCP servers, plugins vs context cost, slow hooks), CLAUDE.md files (duplicates, derivable content, always-loaded guidance that can move to skills), permissions, and usage (Pro/Max/Ultra/Team/Enterprise, v2.1.305+). Reports findings first and asks before changing anything. /doctor prompt-audit [path] checks CLAUDE.md, skills and other config for outdated or conflicting instructions (v2.1.283+). claude doctor gives read-only diagnostics from the terminal.
facts.limits: Applies fixes only after confirmation. /doctor stays typable when disableBundledSkills is on; hide with DISABLE_DOCTOR_COMMAND or skillOverrides doctor: off.

facts.behavior: Prompt-based skills shipped with Claude Code (/doctor, /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop, /claude-api, /verify, /run, /run-skill-generator, /skill-doctor, /simplify); marked Skill in the commands reference. Most other built-in commands run fixed logic. disableBundledSkills turns all off. /verify runs only when invoked manually; /workflow-authoring needs dynamic workflows enabled. A local skill replaces a bundled command of the same name but not its aliases.
facts.limits: Bundled skills are not matched by pre-commit verify/simplify behavior (only user-supplied skills count).

facts.behavior: If a skill named verify or simplify exists when a session starts, Claude runs it before each commit, except for docs or test changes (v2.1.286+).
facts.limits: Skill must come from enterprise, personal, project, additional-directory or .claude/commands/; bundled, plugin and claude.ai skills do not count. Must not be disable-model-invocation: true, and includeGitInstructions must not be off.

facts.behavior: /run launches and drives the app; /verify builds and runs the app to confirm a change; /run-skill-generator records the recipe as a project skill at .claude/skills/run-<name>/. /verify records its own recipe to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md at the repo root (or touched package in a monorepo), replacing the bundled /verify there. Claude edits a recorded file only when it steered a run wrong.
facts.limits: Run /run-skill-generator once per project and again if build or launch changes.

facts.behavior: Terminal sessions signed in via /login download enabled account/org skills (plus pdf, xlsx) to ~/.claude/skills/synced/ in the background (v2.1.273+), checking about every 10 minutes active / 40 minutes idle; a skill downloads only when invoked. Invoke as /<name> or /anthropic-skills:<name>. Turn off with syncClaudeAiSkills: false (synced skills move to ~/.claude/skills/.trash/).
facts.limits: Download-only; local edits under synced/ can be overwritten. Does not sync with API key/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN/apiKeyHelper auth, without feature flags (Bedrock, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC), in bare mode/--safe-mode, under managed strictPluginOnlyCustomization for skills, or if --setting-sources omits user. Display text is sanitized; ! commands and @ references and some variables do not work in most local sessions.

facts.behavior: Enterprise over personal over project; skill over .claude/commands/ file; local skill replaces a bundled or built-in command (local terminal sessions) but not its aliases; root and nested skill both load; plugin skills are namespaced /plugin:skill and coexist with local ones; .claude/commands/frontend/component.md becomes /frontend:component; plugin name already prefixed is not double-prefixed (v2.1.246+).
facts.limits: Name comparison ignores case, spacing, invisible characters and compatibility forms (so Commit and commit clash); look-alike letters from other alphabets count as different. Diagnose refused names with claude --debug and search for [names].

facts.feature: Skill as plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json in a skill folder)
facts.behavior: A .claude-plugin/plugin.json in a personal or project skill folder loads it as <name>@skills-dir, with its own agents, hooks and MCP servers.
facts.limits: In a project this requires accepting the workspace trust dialog first.

facts.behavior: 'Scaffold a new plugin at ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ (auto-loads next session as <name>@skills-dir)'. Options: --author <name> (default git config user.name), --author-email <email> (default git config user.email), --description <text> (manifest description), -f/--force (overwrite an existing .claude-plugin/ at the target), --with <components...> (also scaffold: skills, agents, hooks, mcp, lsp, output-style, channel). Usage: claude plugin init|new [options] <name>.
facts.limits: Help text states only the ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ target; no option to choose another directory is listed. Does not validate or test the plugin. Installed CLI version 2.1.317.

facts.feature: claude plugin validate and claude plugin eval (skill checks)
facts.behavior: claude plugin validate <dir> (e.g. claude plugin validate .claude/skills or ~/.claude/skills) finds SKILL.md files whose frontmatter does not parse (v2.1.233+). claude plugin eval runs eval cases (case.yaml or prompt.md + graders) against a plugin with and without it, scores with graders, and exits non-zero below a threshold for CI gating; the docs suggest a tool_used: Skill grader to measure trigger rate.
facts.limits: eval is for plugins (skills-dir plugins resolve too), not plain personal/project skills (use skillOverrides off for the baseline there); runs on your machine as you, only evaluate trusted plugins; first run in an untrusted plugin directory asks for confirmation (--trust-plugin for CI). validate in the docs is described for frontmatter parse errors; other checks not stated in the fetched text.

facts.behavior: Installable with /plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official; stores test cases in evals/evals.json, spawns one subagent per case, grades assertions pass/fail with evidence, benchmark with/without skill, blind A/B version comparison, description tuning with should-trigger/should-not-trigger prompts, HTML review viewer. Format not interchangeable with claude plugin eval.
facts.limits: Optional tooling the user runs; nothing runs automatically.

facts.feature: Skill troubleshooting guidance (not triggering, over-triggering, stops following, disappeared)
facts.behavior: Docs: check description has natural keywords; ask 'What skills are available?'; invoke /skill-name directly; run --debug for YAML parse errors; to stop over-triggering make description specific or add disable-model-invocation: true; if Claude skips a rule that must hold every time, move it into a hook; after compaction re-invoke the skill. Personal skills moved by claude.ai sync or older manifest.json behavior (before v2.1.280) go to ~/.claude/skills/.trash/ (retention sweep default 30 days).
facts.limits: Advisory documentation only.

area: Plugin eval runner (claude plugin eval): case format, graders, runs, ablation, thresholds, reports, availability; Anthropic eval guidance

facts.feature: claude plugin eval command (what it is)
facts.behavior: Runs eval cases (<eval dir>/**/case.yaml or prompt.md + graders/*.md) against a plugin and reports scored results. Target is a path, a plugin name, or plugin@marketplace id. Docs: 'The claude plugin eval shell command runs your plugin against a suite of test cases and scores the results. Each case is a realistic prompt plus one or more graders.' Every run and every judge grader is a real model call on your account, counted against plan usage or API bill.
facts.limits: Pass/fail checks on Claude output only. It tests behavior, not syntax or schema; use `claude plugin validate` for files. Separate from skill-creator evals: neither tool reads the other's case files (skill-creator uses evals/evals.json).

facts.behavior: Requires Claude Code v2.1.269 or later; Git 2.31+ if git is installed (older git: stops before running any case, exit 1; no git: runs normally); a plugin dir with plugin.json or .claude-plugin/plugin.json, or a skills-directory plugin; same auth/provider as normal sessions. Troubleshooting lists 'plugin eval is currently in early access' (build predates general availability; run claude update) and 'plugin eval is currently unavailable' (Anthropic switched the command off server-side; nothing local re-enables it). Installed CLI here is 2.1.317 and has the command.
facts.limits: Server-side off switch exists. Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry users must export the same provider variables in the shell. Cost figures are list-price estimates.

facts.behavior: Default eval dir is evals/ inside the plugin. Override with manifest key experimental.evals (path, or array of paths where only the first entry is used) or --eval-dir flag on both `eval` and `eval init`; flag wins over manifest. Cases, results and init output move to that dir. Results go to <plugin>/<dir>/results/ (for an installed-plugin target, ./<dir>/results/ or ./evals/results/).
facts.limits: Must be a relative path of plain directory names; absolute or '..' paths: error as flag, but for an unusable manifest value prints a Warning and uses evals/. experimental.evals is not a component path, so manifest path rules do not apply; checked when claude plugin eval runs. The `experimental` container's manifest shape 'may still change'.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (Fields table, Path rules); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md#use-a-different-eval-directory; claude plugin eval --help

facts.behavior: A case is a directory under the eval dir holding prompt.md, case.yaml, or both. Each case needs at least one grader, as graders/<name>.md or a graders: entry in case.yaml. Nest cases under a non-case directory to group them. Suite-wide mocks live at evals/mocks/, results at evals/results/<timestamp>/ (add results/ to .gitignore).
facts.limits: A case without a grader fails to load with an 'invalid case.yaml' error naming graders. Anything inside a case directory belongs to that case.

facts.behavior: Fields: schema_version (default "1.1", auto-set), name (default dir name), description, tags, plugins (default nearest enclosing plugin), runs (default 3, 1 to 50), expected_outcome, model, max_turns (default 10, up to 200), timeout_seconds (default 300, up to 3600), allowed_tools (default []), append_system_prompt, env. The body is the prompt, received exactly as written.
facts.limits: Unknown key is an error. description and expected_outcome are not used at run time. env keys must match EVAL_[A-Z0-9_]*, any other key fails the run. @path mentions in the body are not expanded into attachments. Hitting max_turns is recorded as a run error and usually lowers the score. Each run starts in an empty working directory.

facts.behavior: Alternative or companion to prompt.md. Requires schema_version: "1.1" and name. description, tags, plugins, runs, expected_outcome at top level; model, max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools, append_system_prompt, env under execution:. case.yaml-only fields: context.scaffold_script, context.history_file, context.add_dirs, execution.prompt, graders (list; each with name plus the keys a graders/*.md frontmatter takes; llm rubric goes in criteria). When both files exist, prompt.md frontmatter overrides matching case.yaml fields, prompt.md body is the prompt, and graders/*.md are added after case.yaml graders.
facts.limits: Neither eval tool reads skill-creator's evals.json.

facts.behavior: `claude plugin eval init [name]` runs an authoring interview in an interactive Claude Code session: reads the plugin, proposes should/should-not-trigger prompts, designs graders, runs them once as a trial, writes one case dir per prompt under the eval dir. `--bare <name>` writes a blank template (prompt.md + graders/criteria.md) and runs nothing. -i/--interactive forces the interview (default in a terminal). Docs call init the recommended path.
facts.limits: The interview needs an interactive terminal; in CI use `init --bare <name>`. init calls the model with your credentials. Asks 'Trust this plugin directory?' if untrusted.

facts.behavior: Six types: regex (pattern, flags, match, target; JavaScript regex; match: not_contains or "count:N"; flags: i), tool_used (tool, input_match, min default 1, max default unlimited; min:0 max:0 asserts never called), tool_order (before, after; first matching before call precedes first matching after call), file_exists (path glob, exists; only files created during the run count), llm (criteria, focus; judge votes PASS in at least two of three votes), baseline (baseline_file .jsonl, criteria; judge finds run satisfies criteria at least as well as the reference transcript). regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists are computed from transcript/files and cost nothing; llm and baseline call a judge model and add cost.
facts.limits: 'There are no custom-code graders.' Inline (?i) is not supported in regex. file_exists cannot see scaffold-created or merely modified files. llm judge refuses non-image binary files (.pptx, PDF).

facts.feature: Grader frontmatter keys: type, weight, arm
facts.behavior: Each grader file takes type (required), weight (default 1, any positive number; relative weight in the run's score), arm (unset; with-only excludes the grader from scoring in a two-arm run; both forces scoring in both arms). Grader name is the filename without .md.
facts.limits: A run's score is the fraction of graders passed, weighted if weights set.

facts.feature: What a grader can look at (target/focus)
facts.behavior: regex takes target, llm takes focus; same values: last_message (default; final response text), trace (session as JSON one message per line; regex sees all, llm judge sees first 12 and last 12 messages; quotes JSON-escaped), files (list of paths Claude created, not contents), { source: file, path } (contents of one workspace file after the run; PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP shown to llm as image), mock_calls (calls to mocked MCP tools with input and answer).
facts.limits: files target lists paths only, not contents, and not scaffold-created or only-modified files. Everything scoring zero despite right files usually means files was used instead of {source: file}.

facts.behavior: Default judge is the model Claude Code uses for background tasks (help text: default haiku). Override with --judge-model <model>. llm graders use three votes, pass on two. Docs say small judges may mark correct answers wrong on formatting; re-run with --judge-model sonnet and tighten rubric.
facts.limits: llm verdicts vary between runs, more so on long text. Docs advise regex over file contents for long output and llm graders only for short outputs with concrete PASS/FAIL rubrics. Pin the judge in CI.

facts.behavior: Docs advise: give each case one grader on the result and one on the steps taken (tool_used or tool_order); to check a build/test passed, have the prompt write the outcome to a file, grade that file, and assert the command ran via tool_used with input_match; if tool_used: Skill passes but delta is negative suspect the judge first.
facts.limits: Advice only; nothing checks that suites follow it.

facts.behavior: Each case runs 3 times per arm by default (case.runs ?? 3); --runs <n> overrides (case runs 1 to 50). A run's score is the fraction of graders passed (weighted); the case score is the mean across runs. Docs: 'One run of a non-deterministic agent tells you little, so each case runs three times by default.' Suite makes roughly cases x runs agent runs with plugin and same again for baseline, plus three short judge calls per llm/baseline grader per run.
facts.limits: A single run is noisy; docs say confirm any change at the default three runs. API-error runs score 0 without grading.

facts.behavior: -j/--concurrency <n> runs up to n agent runs at once (1 to 8, default 1). Results and report keep case order.
facts.limits: Each run is a full claude child on your own credential, sharing one rate limit; shortens wall-clock time, not throughput past the limit.

facts.behavior: --ablation none | with-without. Default is with-without whenever a plugin resolves (by name or from target path), none when nothing resolves. Under with-without each case's runs repeat with no plugin loaded; output shows WITH, W/OUT and delta (with-arm minus without-arm). none runs one arm, halving cost, and the table shows SCORE and PASS% instead.
facts.limits: Single-arm by default for: --ablation none; cases using context.history_file when the target is a path (stderr 'single-arm (no delta)' notice; pass --ablation with-without to compare); cases where no plugin was located. The delta is reported but never changes the exit code. In baseline runs, the plugin's own agents fail with "Agent type ... not found", which is expected.

facts.behavior: In a two-arm run, graders that cannot pass without the plugin are excluded from the score in both arms and reported in the with-arm as pass/fail indicators only (scored: false, badge 'plugin-fired indicator'): every tool_used grader with tool: Skill; every regex target: mock_calls and llm focus: mock_calls grader when each mocked server is one the plugin declares; any grader marked arm: with-only. arm: both scores a grader in both arms (e.g. a must-not-invoke check with min:0 max:0).
facts.limits: If every grader in a case is excluded they are scored normally. Under --ablation none nothing is excluded, so absolute scores can differ between modes.

facts.behavior: --threshold <0..1>, default 1.0: a case passes when its with-arm score is at least the threshold; any case below it makes the command exit 1 ('Exit 1 if any case score is below this threshold'). Exit codes: 0 suite passed; 1 case below threshold, case file failed to load, no cases found, run could not start, run ended on API error, untrusted dir without --trust-plugin, invalid option, or --json write failure; 2 partial run (--max-cost-usd ceiling hit, or credential rejected); 130 interrupted (partial results written); 143 terminated.
facts.limits: Default 1.0 means any imperfect case fails the job. Delta never affects exit code; HTML report write/publish problems never affect it. Baseline-run API errors can fail the command even when every case passes.

facts.behavior: Optional hard ceiling on the run's list-price cost estimate; checked before each run launches; abort and report partial results if hit (exit 2). Paid graders (llm/baseline) are skipped for a breaching run while free graders still score it.
facts.limits: No ceiling by default. Not a ceiling on plan usage. Runs already in flight finish, so spend can overshoot by up to --concurrency runs. Skipped runs flagged skippedPaidGraders and partial results marked partial:true; leave them out of trend charts. Runs already bounded by max_turns and timeout_seconds.

facts.behavior: Runs never stop to ask permission. Built-in tools needing a grant you did not give (Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch) are removed from the session. A case's allowed_tools grants only read-only tools: Read, Glob, Grep, NotebookRead, Skill, AskUserQuestion, Agent, TodoWrite, TaskCreate/Get/List/Update/Stop. --allow-tools grants more (supports Tool(pattern:*) syntax) and applies to every case in the run. --disallow-tools keeps built-in tools from Claude in every case even if granted. Ungranted requests show as 'not granted' in progress output.
facts.limits: A case's allowed_tools and a skill's own allowed-tools frontmatter cannot widen the operator grants. If Bash or PowerShell is granted on a machine with no sandbox backend, each run is refused (usually scores 0); native Windows has no backend (use WSL2); Linux needs bubblewrap and socat. Granted Bash runs under the OS sandbox: writes confined to run workspace, home and Claude config unreadable, network limited to WebFetch(domain:...) grants.

facts.behavior: Each run gets a temporary home dir, working dir and Claude Code config; the agent runs as a `claude -p` child with only the plugin under test loaded. Git hooks, credential helpers and similar repo-config programs are switched off per run (hence git 2.31). The case definitions are hidden: the run cannot read the eval directory. The Artifact tool is off.
facts.limits: Absent in runs: user settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers, other plugins, memory, skills; no project-scoped config (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json) loads even if scaffold wrote it; add_dirs grant read only; only an allowlist of shell env vars plus EVAL_* reach the run. Managed-policy settings still apply. Plugin's own hooks and real MCP servers run outside the agent sandbox and could modify files graders read; treat scores as advisory unless in isolated environment. Isolation limits the agent under test, not the plugin's own code; passing says nothing about plugin safety.

facts.behavior: First run against a directory asks 'Trust this plugin directory?' unless already accepted in an interactive claude session; in a git repo yes trusts the whole repository, for interactive sessions too. --trust-plugin asserts trust and skips the prompt (for CI). Named targets (installed or skills-dir plugin) skip the prompt.
facts.limits: If stdin/stdout is not a terminal or under --json, an untrusted dir is refused with exit 1 without --trust-plugin. --trust-plugin does not imply --scaffold, --allow-tools or --mocks off.

facts.behavior: context.scaffold_script names a Bash script in the case dir that runs in the empty workspace before Claude starts to create fixture files or git state. Runs only with --scaffold; --no-scaffold explicitly skips it. Runs as you, outside the agent sandbox, with minimal env (PATH, HOME as the run's temp home, TMPDIR, TERM=dumb); EVAL_* not passed.
facts.limits: Off by default; only use on case files you authored. Non-zero exit or >120 seconds scores that run 0 with 'scaffold failed'. Only files and git state; project config it writes is not loaded.

facts.feature: Conversation history and read-only fixture dirs
facts.behavior: context.history_file names a .jsonl transcript to resume; the case prompt becomes the next user turn. context.add_dirs lists case-dir directories Claude may read during the run, read-only.
facts.limits: history_file cases run single-arm by default when the target is a path.

facts.behavior: --mocks record (default) | off. record: plugin's real MCP servers are NOT started; a substitute server is registered under each server's name; tools with a mock file (evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md, or case-level mocks/) answer from it and need no --allow-tools grant; tools without a mock are unavailable. Mock features: {{input.<field>}} and {{file:...}} substitutions, expect: input guard (violation aborts run, score 0), error: true, type: agent (judge model answers as server; shared budget 4x max_turns, overrun aborts run score 0), abort_when, _server.md, _tools.json. Agent-mock answers saved in results mock-recordings/ with ADOPT.txt for replay via mocks/.replay/. --allow-real-servers with record also starts real servers lacking a mock; --mocks off starts every real server.
facts.limits: Real servers run as you outside the OS sandbox and need --allow-tools by name (mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>). Agent mocks vary run to run. expect regex is a limited dialect (no groups, alternation, backreferences, lookaround; flags i and s only); a pattern outside it stops the case loading (score 0).

facts.behavior: Every run with at least one case writes results/<timestamp>/aggregate-result.json and report.html (self-contained, no external requests). Report shows verdict line, summary tiles (suite score, ablation delta, baseline score, cases at threshold, perfect runs), per-case cards with threshold tick, per-run grader chips with explanations, llm judge votes and evidence, prompt and graders. If signed in with claude.ai subscription and artifacts are available, the report is published as a private artifact (Published: <url>). Flags: --report <path>, --output-dir <dir>, --no-publish, --publish-report, --json [path] (quiet output, versioned schemaVersion: 1 camelCase document with partial, aggregates.overallScore, casesPassed, meanDelta, cases[].arms..., costUsd, durationSeconds, claudeVersion), --keep-temp, --verbose.
facts.limits: Publishing is by default only where the account supports it (not with API-key auth); a run started by a Claude Code session stays local unless --publish-report. --json suppresses progress lines and summary table; put target before --json. Ignore unknown JSON fields. Partial documents (partial:true) and skippedPaidGraders runs should be left out of trends.

facts.behavior: Target: plugin root dir (all cases), single prompt.md/case.yaml, installed plugin name or name@marketplace, name@skills-dir, or omitted (current dir). --case <glob> filters by name; --tag <tag...> keeps cases with any given tag. --model overrides the agent model for all cases (else case model, else ANTHROPIC_MODEL, else default).
facts.limits: Put target before --tag, --allow-tools, --json (list/optional-path options swallow a following target). No cases matched gives 'No eval cases found' and exit 1. Docs advise pinning --model and --judge-model in CI so a model rollout is not mistaken for a plugin regression.

facts.behavior: Docs example: claude plugin eval . --trust-plugin --json results.json --threshold 0.8 --model claude-sonnet-5 --judge-model claude-haiku-4-5 --no-publish --max-cost-usd 20. Runner needs Claude Code install and credentials in env. Keep cost predictable: use judge-free graders for every-change suites, --ablation none where delta is not needed.
facts.limits: Advisory examples only; nothing forces these flags.

facts.behavior: Authoritative check of plugin.json and component paths; reports Validation passed, passed with warnings, or failed; --strict turns warnings into failures. Validates name rules, path containment/existence, MCP entries.
facts.limits: Checks files for syntax and schema, not behavior; does not run evals. Claude Code loads a plugin with unknown top-level fields (stripped), but strict objects (userConfig, channels, lspServers, monitors entries) reject unknown keys.

facts.behavior: Post names three grader types. Code-based: 'Brittle to valid variations that don't match expected patterns exactly'; fast, cheap, reproducible. Model-based: flexible, but 'Non-deterministic', 'More expensive than code', 'Require calibration with human graders for accuracy'. Human: gold standard but expensive and slow, 'Used to calibrate model-based graders'. 'We recommend choosing deterministic graders where possible.'
facts.limits: Guidance in a blog post, not enforced by the harness.

facts.behavior: 'Because model outputs vary between runs, we run multiple trials to produce more consistent results.' pass@k 'measures the likelihood that an agent gets at least one correct solution in k attempts'; pass^k 'measures the probability that all k trials succeed'; use pass@k 'for tools where one success matters, pass^k for agents where consistency is essential.'
facts.limits: claude plugin eval reports mean score across runs and threshold on that mean; it does not compute pass@k or pass^k (not stated in docs; derivable per-run scores in JSON only).

facts.behavior: Scoring can be weighted ('combined grader scores must hit a threshold'), binary (all graders must pass), or a hybrid.
facts.limits: Plugin eval implements weighted mean per run (weight key) with a case threshold; threshold 1.0 default approximates binary.

facts.behavior: 'Each trial should be isolated by starting from a clean environment.' Shared leftover state can cause 'correlated failures due to infrastructure flakiness rather than agent performance.'
facts.limits: Plugin eval implements this automatically via per-run temp home/workdir/config.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: grade outcomes, not path
facts.behavior: Recommends grading 'what the agent produced, not the path it took', since rigid path checks punish creative valid solutions; still 'often useful to also grade the transcript' (code quality, tool use).
facts.limits: Plugin eval supports both (file/last_message targets, and tool_used/tool_order/trace); docs separately recommend one result grader plus one steps grader per case.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: capability vs regression evals
facts.behavior: Capability evals ask 'What can this agent do well?' and should 'start at a low pass rate'. Regression evals ask whether the agent still handles past tasks and 'should have a nearly 100% pass rate'. High-pass capability evals can 'graduate' into regression suites.
facts.limits: Nothing in the harness distinguishes the two; tags and --threshold could be used (default 1.0 suits regression).

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: read transcripts, start small
facts.behavior: 'You won't know if your graders are working well unless you read the transcripts and grades from many trials.' Teams wrongly think they need hundreds of tasks; '20-50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start.' 'Evals get harder to build the longer you wait.'
facts.limits: Advisory; the HTML report exposes each run's graders, explanations and judge evidence for reading.

facts.behavior: Skill-creator 'helps you write evals', with test prompts, optional files and what good output looks like. Benchmark mode runs a standardized assessment tracking eval pass rate, elapsed time and token usage. Multi-agent parallel runs each in a clean context with own token/timing metrics. Comparator agents A/B compare two skill versions or skill vs no skill and 'judge outputs without knowing which is which'. Description tuning suggests edits to cut false and missed triggers (improved triggering on five of six public document-creation skills). Evals/results can be stored locally, sent to a dashboard, or run in CI.
facts.limits: Separate tool from claude plugin eval with its own evals/evals.json format; neither reads the other's case files. Blog post is product guidance, not enforcement.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: when skills need evals
facts.behavior: Blog: run evals for regression checks (models and infrastructure change; run on new models for early warning); capability-uplift skills (if the base model passes without the skill, the skill may no longer be needed); encoded-preference skills (check fidelity to team workflow); isolating failures (PDF skill example); confirming a skill that seems to work does work.
facts.limits: Advisory; the plugin eval baseline arm and delta are the mechanism that measures whether the base model already passes.

area: sessions and resume, worktrees and their cleanup, sandboxing, checkpoints, background tasks, what carries between sessions

facts.behavior: A session is a saved conversation tied to a project directory. Sessions are saved continuously to local JSONL transcript files at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl.
facts.limits: Local only. Entry format is internal and changes between versions. Default retention 30 days (cleanupPeriodDays). Storage moved with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; writes suppressed with CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY or --no-session-persistence (-p only).

facts.behavior: claude --continue reopens the most recent session in the current directory; claude --resume opens the picker; --resume <name> or <session-id> or <transcript-path> resumes directly; /resume switches sessions in-session; --from-pr filters to PR-linked sessions.
facts.limits: --continue and the picker skip sessions created with claude -p, the Agent SDK, or whose first prompt was /loop (resumable by session ID). If no stored session matches an ID: 'No conversation found'. Ambiguous names open the picker (or error under /resume <name>).

facts.behavior: Restores conversation history (from last compaction summary onward), model, agent (--agent), permission mode (terminal resume), active goal, unexpired session-scoped scheduled tasks. Interrupted tool calls are not rerun. Ended background subagents/Bash/workflows appear as notes that they did not finish.
facts.limits: Not restored: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, --add-dir and /add-dir directories (pass again). Background Bash and monitor tasks are not restored. Settings files are re-read at launch. bypassPermissions is not restored on resume; plan mode is. Goal turn count, timer and token baseline reset.

facts.behavior: Terminal --continue/--resume <id|name> restores the mode the session was in; session picker and /resume start in the mode a new session would, except plan mode resumes as plan; bypassPermissions is never restored; auto restored only if account still qualifies.
facts.limits: Pass --permission-mode or --dangerously-skip-permissions to override. Plan mode not restored if a deny rule removes ExitPlanMode or with --fork-session. -p resume uses new-run mode except plan under specific conditions.

facts.behavior: On Pro/Max/Ultra, shown when resuming a long conversation after a long break or on a different model; estimate is the share of the 5-hour usage limit the saved conversation alone would use.
facts.limits: Estimate does not count usage already consumed; cost lands on first message after Resume. Offers Resume or Start a new conversation.

facts.behavior: By default shows sessions from the current worktree (including bg background sessions) and sessions that added the cwd via /add-dir. Ctrl+W widens to all worktrees of the repo, Ctrl+A to all projects, Ctrl+B filters to current git branch, Ctrl+R renames, Space previews, / searches (accepts PR/MR URL).
facts.limits: Ctrl+W only shown in multi-worktree repos. Sessions from an unrelated project: Claude copies a cd+resume command to clipboard rather than resuming. If a session's worktree is gone it resumes in the current directory.

facts.feature: Resume by ID or name across directories
facts.behavior: claude --resume <session-id> works from any directory: searches current project and its worktrees, then every other project. Name resolution spans the current repository and its worktrees; exact match resumes directly.
facts.limits: Cross-project lookup resolves only if exactly one other project holds a transcript for the ID; duplicates give not-found.

facts.behavior: Name via claude -n <name>, /rename <name>, Ctrl+R in picker, plan-accept auto title, Remote Control rename, desktop rename. Unnamed sessions get a generated title (Haiku-class summary of first prompt) usable with --resume, and a default display name like my-app-3f.
facts.limits: The default display name is not a resume handle. claude -p runs started from a shell get no generated title. /clear keeps a set name but not an AI-generated title.

facts.behavior: /branch [name] copies the conversation so far and switches into it, leaving the original intact; CLI form: claude --continue --fork-session. Branch inherits history, 'Allow for this session' grants (same-process only), in-flight background subagents and Bash (output shows in the branch), and Remote Control connection.
facts.limits: --fork-session in a new process does not carry session grants. Resuming the same session in two terminals without forking interleaves messages into one transcript.

facts.behavior: claude --resume / /resume on a still-running background session opens that session itself (attach) rather than loading the transcript; /resume moves the current conversation to background and attaches. --continue opens finished background sessions but not running ones.
facts.limits: Not opened when command line has piped I/O, session-configuring flags (--permission-mode, --model, --settings), output flags, or --max-turns/--max-budget-usd: exits status 1 with claude attach hint. Prompts starting with / or ! are not sent. --fork-session resumes a copy instead.

facts.behavior: /clear starts fresh with empty context and saves the previous session (resume via /resume, or the rewind menu's previous-session entry in the same process). /compact [instructions] replaces history with a summary. /context shows what consumes context.
facts.limits: The previous-session rewind entry is available only until you exit Claude Code or resume a different session. /clear keeps a name you set, not a generated title.

facts.feature: Export and script access to sessions (/export, hooks transcript_path)
facts.behavior: /export copies or saves a plain-text rendered transcript; claude -p --resume <id> --output-format json for structured follow-ups; hooks and status line receive transcript_path; a SessionEnd hook can archive the transcript.
facts.limits: Direct parsing of JSONL is unsupported (format internal, can break on any release).

facts.feature: Transcript retention and deletion (cleanupPeriodDays, claude purge, claude rm)
facts.behavior: Transcripts age out under a retention sweep, default 30 days; cleanupPeriodDays changes it. claude purge deletes a project's transcripts, tasks, file history and its ~/.claude.json entry from this computer only.
facts.limits: claude rm <id> on a background session leaves its transcript on disk and resumable. desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays governs Desktop/Cowork transcripts separately.

facts.behavior: With CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR also set, names the <project> directory so transcripts and auto memory live under it (e.g. $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/work/memory/).
facts.limits: Ignored when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is unset; 1-64 letters/digits/hyphens/underscores; must be in shell env at start (not settings env block); requires v2.1.234+.

facts.behavior: --system-prompt-snapshot on (default) records the system prompt on the conversation's first request and reuses it verbatim on every later request and resume, even if a later launch passes different text, until compaction.
facts.limits: Off under --bare outside cloud/background sessions by default. Use off to iterate on prompt text.

facts.behavior: claude --worktree <name> creates an isolated worktree under .claude/worktrees/<name>/ at the repo root on a new branch worktree-<name>; omit name for a generated one (e.g. bright-running-fox). If a worktree with that name exists, it is opened instead.
facts.limits: Requires a git repo (or WorktreeCreate hook). Interactive runs require workspace trust; -p skips the trust check. Docs recommend (advisory) adding .claude/worktrees/ to .gitignore. --tmux requires --worktree.

facts.behavior: Claude can create a worktree mid-session via EnterWorktree and switch to another one under .claude/worktrees/ by path; previous worktree stays on disk. Entering a path outside .claude/worktrees/ asks for approval.
facts.limits: An EnterWorktree permission rule or 'don't ask again' does not suppress that prompt; only bypassPermissions skips it. Tools are removed when permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories is on. ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} in hooks stays at the original project root; hook cwd follows the worktree.

facts.behavior: On exit Claude checks for changed/untracked files, submodule work, and new commits. Clean + unnamed session: worktree and branch removed automatically. Clean + named session: prompts first. Has work, another branch checked out, or state unverifiable: prompts keep or remove. Keeping preserves directory and branch; remove deletes worktree directory and its branch with the work.
facts.limits: Applies to worktrees Claude created with git; WorktreeCreate-hook worktrees use WorktreeRemove. Non-interactive -p runs have no exit prompt: worktree not cleaned up and its creation lock stays until a later sweep; remove manually with git worktree remove (git worktree unlock first if locked).

facts.feature: Periodic sweep of subagent and background-session worktrees
facts.behavior: Claude Code runs a periodic sweep that removes worktrees Claude created for subagents and background sessions once older than cleanupPeriodDays, per the retention sweep rules.
facts.limits: Leaves a worktree if it holds changed/untracked files or unpushed commits, submodule changes, filter-driver cases, a --worktree session you haven't backgrounded (any age), one you made yourself with git worktree add, or any worktree lacking the marker Claude writes into git metadata (including WorktreeCreate-hook worktrees). Never releases a lock you set with git worktree lock.

facts.behavior: Ask Claude to 'use worktrees for your agents' or set isolation: worktree in a custom subagent's frontmatter. Each subagent gets a temporary worktree removed automatically when it finishes without changes; one with changes stays until the sweep can remove it without losing work.
facts.limits: Uses the same base branch as --worktree. Subagent takes instruction files from the main conversation; under default .claude/worktrees/ location it does not load the worktree-root CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ as it reads files there.

facts.behavior: While an agent runs, Claude Code holds git worktree lock on its worktree (also for a backgrounded session) so concurrent cleanup and git worktree remove refuse; released when the agent finishes; sweep releases locks of exited sessions.
facts.limits: Manual removal: git worktree remove (--force for uncommitted changes), git worktree unlock first if locked.

facts.behavior: While isolated in a worktree, Claude Code blocks: Edit/Write/NotebookEdit targeting a main-checkout path; Bash/PowerShell/Monitor commands whose working directory resolves to (or can't be verified outside) the main checkout; Bash/Monitor git redirects into main checkout (git -C, --git-dir, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, cd); commands whose git destination can't be verified from text (cannot be turned off). Applies to subagents spawned from the session and to background sessions.
facts.limits: Does not track files shell commands write: cp or a shell redirect into the main checkout is not refused by these checks. PowerShell gets only the working-directory check. Falls back to normal permissions and sandboxing.

facts.behavior: New worktrees branch from the repository's default branch on the remote ('fresh', default) or from current local HEAD ('head'). For fresh, origin/HEAD is refreshed by a fetch if not fetched in 24 hours, capped at 5 seconds, falling back to cached ref or local HEAD.
facts.limits: Cannot be set to a branch name; use git worktree add for a specific branch. Fetch never prompts for credentials (fails instead).

facts.behavior: --worktree accepts #number, GitHub PR URL or GitLab MR URL; fetches the head commit from origin and creates .claude/worktrees/pr-<number>.
facts.limits: Only the number is read from URLs; always fetches from origin; fetch fails rather than prompt for password/passphrase/host confirmation. Reopened PR worktrees return at old tip.

facts.behavior: A .worktreeinclude file at project root (gitignore syntax) lists files copied into every worktree Claude Code creates with git (--worktree, subagent worktrees, desktop parallel sessions).
facts.limits: Only files that match a pattern AND are gitignored are copied; tracked files never duplicated. Not processed when a WorktreeCreate hook is used. **/ patterns have special handling inside wholly ignored directories.

facts.feature: Reuse of an existing worktree name
facts.behavior: Passing an existing name opens that worktree. With baseRef fresh it resets to default branch only if no uncommitted/untracked files, still on its own branch, and no own commits (or PR merged and remote branch deleted).
facts.limits: Otherwise reopens at old tip; also at old tip if state unverifiable, baseRef is head, or the name is a PR reference. Errors 'belongs to a different repository' / 'is a leftover worktree' after copy/move of a project.

facts.behavior: Resuming a session that ended inside a worktree without exiting returns it to that worktree (interactive, -p --continue/--resume, Agent SDK). Entering/exiting a git-created worktree moves the transcript to the worktree's project storage. Deleted worktree: session resumes in launch directory and binding is cleared.
facts.limits: Claude Code verifies the worktree is a separate checkout and declines otherwise (messages 'Did not re-enter', 'Could not re-enter', 'Could not verify'); in -p/SDK modes most refusals abort with stderr error. Never resumes into a network-path worktree. --fork-session starts in launch directory.

facts.feature: What worktrees share with main checkout
facts.behavior: Shared: the repo's .git directory (sandbox allows those writes), project-scope plugins, permission approvals ('Yes, and don't ask again' saves to main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json, applies to all worktrees and survives removal), and read-through of main checkout .claude/skills, agents, commands when the worktree has no such directory.
facts.limits: On Windows and where repo root isn't used, approvals stay with the worktree. Desktop-app worktree sessions read settings, hooks, skills, agents, .mcp.json from main checkout root; CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules load from the worktree. Skills read-through requires v2.1.277+.

facts.feature: Worktree creation safety (symlinks, filter drivers, git replace, partial clones)
facts.behavior: Claude Code refuses to create a worktree when .claude, .claude/worktrees or the worktree dir is a symlink; skips repository-local filter drivers (so git lfs install --local yields LFS pointer files; run git lfs pull); checks out with GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1; refuses directories whose git metadata resolves into the main checkout (Refusing to use <path> as an isolation worktree).
facts.limits: Creation fails in four filter-driver config cases (unreadable config, unneutralizable name, includeIf in repo config, LFS program keys). Partial clones can fail if objects can't be fetched. Refused directory is left in place.

facts.feature: Non-git VCS via WorktreeCreate / WorktreeRemove hooks
facts.behavior: A WorktreeCreate hook replaces the default git logic entirely (including location other than .claude/worktrees/); a WorktreeRemove hook handles cleanup. Also enables /batch outside a git repo (v2.1.281+).
facts.limits: Without a hook, --worktree in a non-git dir errors 'Can only use --worktree in a git repository'. .worktreeinclude not processed; hook-created worktrees are kept by the sweep (no marker). Hook must create dirs outside any repository.

facts.behavior: A background session's edits in the main checkout are refused until it calls EnterWorktree, when permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories is on; allowed by claude --bg --worktree, worktree.bgIsolation: "none", or a worktree made with git worktree add under the start directory.
facts.limits: Applies only when blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories removes the worktree tools. Details on agent-view page not fetched.

facts.behavior: OS-enforced boundary around shell commands Claude runs (Bash, PowerShell, Monitor) and the processes they start; lets Claude run sandboxed commands without per-command approval. Off by default; enable with /sandbox or sandbox.enabled: true. macOS Seatbelt; Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap+socat.
facts.limits: WSL1 unsupported; native Windows runs commands unsandboxed. Not sandboxed: built-in Read/Edit/Write/WebFetch/WebSearch (permission rules govern them), hooks, local MCP servers, plugin monitors, LSP servers, status-line commands, apiKeyHelper, commands typed at the ! prompt, excluded commands, approved unsandboxed retries.

facts.behavior: Writes default to working directory, per-user temp dir and added directories; protected paths stay write-denied. Config: filesystem.allowWrite/denyWrite/denyRead/allowRead. Writes to the shared .git of a worktree's main repo are allowed except hooks/ and config.
facts.limits: Reads default to most of the machine, including ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials, unless denyRead or permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories. filesystem.disabled turns off filesystem isolation (risky). Sandbox paths use /tmp/build and ~/.kube, not //path.

facts.behavior: Even in writable directories, writes are denied to files Claude Code loads config/code from: .claude/settings*, .claude/hooks, .mcp.json, shell startup files, .gitconfig, .git/hooks, .git/config, ~/.claude; also bare-repo layout (HEAD, objects, refs) in the working directory.
facts.limits: Applies only to sandboxed shell commands; file tools governed by permissions. List is 'including', not exhaustive.

facts.behavior: No direct route out; traffic goes through a local proxy that checks each hostname against an allowlist that starts empty (network.allowedDomains, deniedDomains, strictAllowlist, allowManagedDomainsOnly). Hosts resolving only to loopback/link-local (incl. 169.254.169.254) refused except localhost.
facts.limits: Tools ignoring proxy vars (plain ssh, most DB drivers) can't connect; non-TCP (UDP, QUIC, ICMP) can't leave. Proxy doesn't inspect TLS unless network.tlsTerminate (experimental). Off-allowlist hosts: bypassPermissions allows, Manual/acceptEdits prompt, auto refuses unless listed and classifier approves, dontAsk refuses.

facts.behavior: sandbox.credentials.files/envVars with mode deny blocks file reads and unsets env vars; mode mask gives a per-session sentinel that the proxy swaps for the real value on injectHosts requests (needs TLS termination).
facts.limits: There is no built-in credential deny list. On macOS masked files are blocked outright.

facts.feature: Sandbox auto-allow vs regular permissions mode
facts.behavior: Auto-allow: sandboxed commands run without a prompt regardless of permission mode. Regular permissions: every Bash command goes through the normal permission flow.
facts.limits: Auto-allow still prompts for deny rules, critical-path rm, content-scoped ask rules, and commands like FOO=bar npm test, make CC=clang, eval "ls".

facts.feature: Sandbox unsandboxed retry (dangerouslyDisableSandbox) and strict mode
facts.behavior: When a command fails in the sandbox Claude may retry with dangerouslyDisableSandbox; approval depends on mode (bypass runs, Manual/acceptEdits prompt, auto uses classifier, dontAsk denies). allowUnsandboxedCommands: false makes Claude Code ignore the parameter.
facts.limits: An allow rule matching the command also approves the retry; an ask rule on Bash(dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true) forces a prompt.

facts.behavior: sandbox.excludedCommands patterns (e.g. 'docker compose *') run unsandboxed with no filesystem restrictions or proxy; still go through the permission flow.
facts.limits: Every command in a chain must match; commands with redirects, cd or $(...) stay sandboxed; absolute paths and scripts don't match. Docs: 'An excluded command runs with your full access.'

facts.behavior: Managed settings: enabled, failIfUnavailable (exit at startup instead of running unsandboxed), allowUnsandboxedCommands false, allowManagedDomainsOnly, allowManagedReadPathsOnly, locks on weaker-isolation keys. Under admin-required sandbox, loosening keys in repo settings (excludedCommands, allowWrite) are ignored. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB scrubs credentials and sandboxes every command.
facts.limits: Last ~7.8K characters of the sandboxing page (troubleshooting/security limitations) were not read.

facts.behavior: Commands you type at the ! shell-mode prompt run outside the sandbox even when sandboxing is enabled, because the sandbox applies to commands Claude runs.
facts.limits: Unless the session is one covered by strict sandbox mode.

facts.behavior: Claude Code automatically tracks changes made by its file editing tools; every prompt you send that starts a turn creates a checkpoint. Checkpoints are saved with the conversation, so /rewind works after resuming a session.
facts.limits: Snapshots kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints per session. Snapshots deleted by retention sweep about 30 days after the session last saved one (cleanupPeriodDays); rewinding later can fail with 'No files were restored'.

facts.behavior: /rewind or double Esc on empty input opens a menu of prompts with actions: Restore code and conversation, Restore conversation, Restore code, Summarize from here, Summarize up to here, Never mind. Summaries compress context without changing files; originals stay in the transcript.
facts.limits: Double Esc with text in input clears it instead (saved to history). Code-restore options appear only if tracked file changes exist. Rewound messages can return if you exit before sending another prompt.

facts.behavior: Once Claude has edited a file with its file tools, /rewind also undoes later Bash changes to that file.
facts.limits: A file only Bash commands changed isn't tracked and stays as is; use Git to revert.

facts.feature: Checkpoint limitation: subagents, external edits, mid-turn messages, links
facts.behavior: Foreground forked skills (context: fork, background: false) are restored by rewind as usual.
facts.limits: Other subagent edits (including background forked skills and background /code-review --fix) are generally not restored beyond files already edited in the conversation. Manual edits outside Claude Code and concurrent-session edits are not captured. Mid-turn typed messages can be marked 'No code restore'. Symlinked and hard-linked paths are skipped on restore with a warning. Checkpoints are 'not a replacement for version control'.

facts.behavior: Commands run asynchronously and return a background task ID; Ctrl+B moves a running Bash invocation to the background (tmux: press twice). A command reaching its timeout is moved to the background instead of stopped, unless it starts with sleep.
facts.limits: Background tasks are cleaned up automatically when Claude Code exits (detached processes on macOS/Linux stop too); not restored on resume. Terminated if output exceeds 5GB. On macOS/Linux stopped under critical memory pressure when session idle 30+ minutes. No time limit in local interactive sessions; unattended (-p, cloud) sessions have a time limit. A foreground subagent's background command ends when the subagent ends. Disable with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 (also removes Ctrl+B).

facts.behavior: /tasks shows running shells and subagents. Ctrl+X Ctrl+K (press twice within 3s) stops all running background subagents in the session.
facts.limits: Ctrl+T toggles Claude's task checklist, which is not the background-task view.

facts.behavior: claude --bg starts a session in the background and prints an id; claude attach <id|name> opens it; claude logs prints recent terminal output; claude stop|kill stops it (conversation kept, attach/--resume still work); claude respawn restarts it on the current version; claude rm deletes it and its worktree when safe; claude agents lists/manages them. Moving a session to background keeps its background tasks and queued messages running there.
facts.limits: claude rm leaves the transcript on disk and resumable. Commands/! shell commands and messages with IDE selections can't move to background (session stays foreground with 'Cannot open agents').
facts.citation: claude --help (--bg, agents, attach, logs, stop, respawn, rm) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode.md#background-a-session-with-messages-queued

facts.behavior: Typing and pressing Enter mid-turn queues the message; messages are delivered after current tool calls finish within the same turn, or when the turn ends; commands and ! commands wait until turn end. Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+X Ctrl+S sends now; Up takes queued items back; Esc interrupts and sends queue.
facts.limits: Queued items are not checkpointed separately (rewind may show 'No code restore'). Ctrl+Enter requires v2.1.275+.

facts.feature: Task list (Claude's to-do checklist) and CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID
facts.behavior: Claude's checklist of pending/in-progress/complete items; Ctrl+T toggles; tasks persist across context compactions; expanded view restored on --resume/--continue when tasks exist. CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID=<name> shares a task list across sessions via a named directory in ~/.claude/tasks/.
facts.limits: Fills only on models with the task-tracking tools by default (Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and earlier); other models need CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1. Shows up to five tasks at a time. Separate from /tasks.

facts.behavior: Prompts are kept per working directory and Up-arrow recall reaches prompts from past sessions of the same project; Ctrl+R searches history (fullscreen can scope to session, project, all projects); duplicates collapsed. Cleared drafts: ten most recent kept for the current session.
facts.limits: /clear starts a new session but earlier sessions' prompts remain after the new ones. Cleared-draft store discarded on exit (v2.1.292+). History expansion with ! disabled by default.

facts.behavior: Recap: a one-line summary generated in the background once 3+ minutes pass since last completed turn with terminal unfocused, after at least 3 turns; on by default (400 char cap; /recap on demand). Automatic continue: when a claude.ai usage limit stops Claude mid-task, Claude Code waits in the open session and continues after reset.
facts.limits: Recap never appears in non-interactive mode. Auto continue is on by default only for interactive claude.ai-subscription sessions (v2.1.234+).

facts.behavior: Answers a question from the existing conversation without adding to conversation history and without tools; runs while Claude is working; press f to fork into a background subagent with full tools.
facts.limits: Single response, no tools; not in conversation history; replays newest 20 earlier side questions until cleared.

facts.feature: What carries between sessions: restored vs not
facts.behavior: Carries: transcript/conversation, model, agent, permission mode (not bypass), active goal, unexpired session-scoped scheduled tasks, checkpoints, shared task list (if CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID), prompt history per directory, settings files (re-read), auto memory stored under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/.
facts.limits: Does not carry: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, --add-dir/ /add-dir directories, background Bash and monitor tasks, 'Allow for this session' grants in a new process, in-flight background work (shown as did-not-finish notes), bypassPermissions mode, files outside Claude's edit tracking. The CLAUDE.md/auto-memory loading rules were not covered by these pages.

facts.behavior: claude --help lists: -c/--continue, -r/--resume [value], --fork-session, --session-id <uuid>, -n/--name, --from-pr, --no-session-persistence (print mode only), -w/--worktree [name], --tmux, --bg/--background, --teleport, --cloud, --remote-control, --autocompact <auto|tokens>, --permission-mode, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, --restricted, --safe-mode, --bare (skips hooks, auto-memory, CLAUDE.md auto-discovery), --add-dir.
facts.limits: --no-session-persistence works only with -p. --restricted removes code-running tools, ignores user/project/local settings, confines file tools to working directories, refuses bypassPermissions. --bare skips hooks, LSP, attribution, auto-memory, CLAUDE.md auto-discovery.

unreachable: Final ~7.8K characters of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md (troubleshooting and security limitations sections) were truncated by WebFetch and not read

Linked but not fetched (outside assigned sources): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (retention sweep rules), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (auto memory), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window.md (what survives compaction)

area: subagents, agent definitions, model and effort selection, agent teams, workflows, how an omitted model is resolved

facts.behavior: Markdown files with YAML frontmatter; the body is the system prompt. 'Subagents receive only this system prompt plus basic environment details like the working directory, not the Claude Code system prompt.' Only name and description are required. Hot-reloaded within a few seconds from ~/.claude/agents/ and .claude/agents/.
facts.limits: Unrecognized frontmatter fields are ignored without error (find with claude --debug, search 'does not recognize or apply'). Files with no name, name starting with '-', containing ':', over 256 chars, name without description, or bad YAML are skipped. Restart needed for first agent file in a new directory, for --add-dir agent dirs, or with --disable-slash-commands.

facts.behavior: Priority 1 managed settings, 2 --agents CLI flag, 3 .claude/agents/ (project), 4 ~/.claude/agents/ (user), 5 plugin agents/ dir. Project discovery walks up from cwd to repo root; closest definition wins on same name. Both dirs scanned recursively; identity comes only from name, not subfolder.
facts.limits: Duplicate names within one directory load only one file, 'chosen by filesystem read order rather than a documented precedence'; /doctor reports them. Plugin agents are namespaced (my-plugin:review:security).

facts.behavior: Accepts sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full model ID such as claude-opus-5-5, or inherit.
facts.limits: If omitted the subagent falls through to CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL then the main conversation's model (see resolution order fact). Ignored under CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1.

facts.behavior: Order: 1) per-invocation model parameter on the Agent tool call (aliases only: sonnet, opus, haiku, fable); 2) the definition's model frontmatter (inherit = main conversation's model); 3) CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (alias or model ID); 4) the main conversation's model. A family alias like opus resolves to the main conversation's exact model when it is in the same family (including [1m]). A mod's agent.spawn hook can override the per-invocation parameter. /tasks shows each subagent's model.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL was checked before the frontmatter until v2.1.251. Subagents that inherit use the model the session is using when Claude starts them, so a /model switch reaches them.

facts.behavior: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: 'default model for subagents, agent team teammates, and workflow agents that aren't assigned a model another way'; accepts alias or full name. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257+) alongside it overrides definitions and per-invocation models. FORCE alone runs subagents on the main conversation's model, except built-in Explore keeps its listed model.
facts.limits: Without FORCE, a per-invocation model or a definition's model (including inherit) takes precedence. Under force, model frontmatter is ignored; forks and model: inherit skill subagents stay on the main model. Subject to availableModels.

facts.behavior: Explore (read-only, Write/Edit denied; quick/medium/very thorough; on subscription/Console/ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway runs on the Opus the opus alias resolves to, on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry stays on main model); Plan (read-only research agent for plan mode; inherits main model unless CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL); general-purpose (all tools; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL if set and nothing else assigns a model, else main model); claude (catch-all); statusline-setup (Sonnet); claude-code-guide (Haiku).
facts.limits: Explore and Plan start without CLAUDE.md and git status snapshot and are one-shot (no resumable ID). A user/project subagent named Explore overrides the built-in. Disable Explore/Plan with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1; SDK/non-interactive CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1 removes all.

facts.behavior: tools: comma string or YAML list; 'Inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted.' disallowedTools removed from inherited or specified list; 'If both are set, disallowedTools is applied first, then tools is resolved against the remaining pool.' MCP: mcp__server__* in tools; mcp__server or mcp__* in disallowedTools.
facts.limits: A disallowedTools entry with a specifier like Bash(git push *) 'still removes the whole tool'; use permissions.deny for command-level blocking. If no tools entry resolves the agent 'usually fails to launch'. First filter always removes Agent (at depth limit), AskUserQuestion, EndConversation, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode (unless plan mode), ScheduleWakeup, WaitForMcpServers, Workflow. Background subagents keep only an allowlisted tool set plus MCP tools.

facts.feature: Restricting which subagents can be spawned
facts.behavior: Agent(worker, researcher) in tools is an allowlist of spawnable types. Agent alone allows any; omitting Agent prevents spawning. permissions.deny with Agent(Name), or claude --disallowedTools 'Agent(Explore)', blocks specific types; deny Agent to block all. The old Task(agent_type) syntax is now Agent(agent_type).
