facts.limits: The type list applies only when the agent runs as the main thread via claude --agent; inside a subagent definition a type list is ignored.

facts.behavior: 'By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation.' CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH changes it; 1 disables nesting. At the limit Agent is withheld from non-fork subagents.
facts.limits: A fork cannot spawn further forks.

facts.feature: Concurrent subagent limit and spawn totals
facts.behavior: 20 concurrent subagents by default; beyond that spawning fails with 'Concurrent subagent limit reached'. CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS (v2.1.217+) changes it. 'There is no limit on the total number of subagents Claude can spawn over a session.'
facts.limits: Ultracode sessions are exempt; limit does not apply to /subtask forks or resumes (resumes can push count past it).

facts.behavior: 'When the combined descriptions of your subagents, except the built-in ones, exceed 15,000 tokens, Claude Code shows a warning at startup.' Claude delegates based on description; 'use proactively' encourages delegation.
facts.limits: Descriptions still load; warning only.

facts.behavior: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Overrides session effort; Claude can pass an effort parameter per invocation for non-fork subagents (v2.1.292+). While a subagent/skill frontmatter effort applies, it runs at that level whatever level you launch with, save, or pick.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL takes precedence over frontmatter and per-invocation effort. An organization or maxEffortLevel cap still limits the level.

facts.behavior: 'Subagents inherit the main conversation's extended thinking configuration' (v2.1.198+).
facts.limits: No per-subagent thinking setting.

facts.behavior: default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan, manual. Unset = inherits main conversation's mode.
facts.limits: If main is bypassPermissions, acceptEdits, or auto, the subagent runs in that mode and permissionMode is ignored. If main is plan, subagent stays plan (except agent-team teammates). bypassPermissions only applies if main also runs it. Ignored for plugin subagents.

facts.behavior: 'Maximum number of agentic turns before the subagent stops.' Output marked partial (v2.1.246+); Claude can resume it.
facts.limits: Only a turn cap; no cost cap.

facts.behavior: Full skill content (not just description) of up to the first 32 distinct names is injected at startup.
facts.limits: Controls preloading, not access: without skills the subagent can still invoke project/user/plugin skills via the Skill tool unless Skill is omitted from tools or in disallowedTools. Skills with disable-model-invocation: true can't be preloaded. Missing skills skipped with debug-log warning. In agent teams, a teammate does not apply the definition's skills.

facts.behavior: Server name string (shares parent's connection) or inline definition (stdio/http/sse/ws) connected at subagent start and disconnected when it finishes.
facts.limits: Ignored for plugin subagents. Inline servers from project .claude/agents/ load only after folder trust. --strict-mcp-config does not filter inline servers from --agents or SDK. Blocked servers skipped with a warning.

facts.behavior: Frontmatter hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop->SubagentStop) run only while the subagent is active. Settings-level PreToolUse/PostToolUse also fire for subagent tool calls; SubagentStart and SubagentStop fire in the main session with matchers. A PreToolUse hook exiting code 2 blocks the tool call.
facts.limits: For project-level agent files the workspace trust dialog must be accepted (parent folder trust and -p sessions don't count); until then hooks are skipped and an error logged. Ignored for plugin subagents.

facts.behavior: user (~/.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/), project (.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/), local (.claude/agent-memory-local/<agent>/). First 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md included; Read/Write/Edit enabled automatically.
facts.limits: Part of auto memory: disabling via autoMemoryEnabled or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY makes it have no effect. Subagents do not inherit the parent's auto memory.

facts.behavior: 'Set to true to keep this subagent in the background even when Claude asks to wait for it.'
facts.limits: An in-process agent-team teammate that spawns a background: true subagent gets an error.

facts.behavior: Runs the subagent in a temporary git worktree, 'branched by default from your default branch rather than the parent session's HEAD', auto-cleaned if no changes. In a worktree-isolated subagent, commands resolving to the main checkout fail and Bash git redirects into main checkout are checked/refused.
facts.limits: PowerShell gets only the working-directory check. A subagent otherwise starts in the main conversation's cwd; cd does not persist between Bash calls.

facts.feature: Other frontmatter fields (omitClaudeMd, autoCompactWindow, color, initialPrompt, experimental.cacheTtl)
facts.behavior: omitClaudeMd: true starts without user/project/local CLAUDE.md (managed policy files still load; v2.1.271+; ignored via --agent). autoCompactWindow 100000-1000000 (v2.1.296+) compacts that subagent earlier. initialPrompt auto-submits first turn when run as main agent. experimental.cacheTtl 5m or 1h (v2.1.248+).
facts.limits: autoCompactWindow: write plain integer (200k is read as 200 and ignored); CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW overrides it; no effect when running whole session as the agent. initialPrompt ignored for plugin subagents.

facts.feature: What a non-fork subagent loads at start
facts.behavior: Its own system prompt plus environment details, the Claude-written task message, CLAUDE.md files (unless omitClaudeMd or Explore/Plan), git status snapshot, preloaded skills, sibling roster if it has SendMessage.
facts.limits: Not inherited: output style, auto memory, parent's context window size, the parent's conversation history.

facts.behavior: JSON defining session-only subagents (priority 2 above project/user); fields mirror frontmatter with prompt replacing body. Non-interactive -p can take a JSON file path (v2.1.281+). --append-subagent-system-prompt (v2.1.205+) and -file (v2.1.261+) append text to every subagent's system prompt in non-interactive mode.
facts.limits: Not saved to disk; names must not start with '-'; color and experimental ignored; interactive sessions refuse a file path; append flags exclude forks.

facts.feature: Running a whole session as an agent (--agent / agent setting)
facts.behavior: claude --agent <name> or 'agent' in .claude/settings.json: 'A custom subagent's system prompt replaces the default Claude Code system prompt entirely' (unless prompt empty). CLAUDE.md still loads. Choice persists on resume. @-mention (@"name (agent)") guarantees that subagent runs.
facts.limits: CLI flag overrides settings. Natural-language delegation is Claude's discretion, not guaranteed.

facts.behavior: Subagents spawned from the main conversation start in the background by default (fork mode on by default in interactive terminal/VS Code/desktop). Background permission prompts surface in main session; Esc denies one call. Ctrl+B backgrounds a task. CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 lets Claude wait; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 makes Claude wait and disables background commands.
facts.limits: While fork mode is on Claude can't wait for a subagent in interactive sessions. Background results arrive as a completion notification in a later turn.

facts.behavior: A fork inherits the entire conversation: same system prompt, tools, model, message history; shares the parent's prompt cache; only its final result returns. Claude can start forks itself while fork mode is on. Can take isolation: worktree.
facts.limits: A fork can't spawn further forks. Block with Agent(fork) in permissions.deny or CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0. Fork mode on by default from v2.1.302 (interactive terminal from v2.1.232).

facts.behavior: Claude resumes via SendMessage with agent ID or name as 'to'; resumed subagents keep full history; no agent teams needed. Transcripts at ~/.claude/projects/{project}/{sessionId}/subagents/agent-{agentId}.jsonl, deleted after cleanupPeriodDays (default 30). Subagents support auto-compaction; CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE applies.
facts.limits: Explore/Plan are one-shot with no ID. A subagent you stopped yourself doesn't auto-resume. Name-based messaging only for subagents named at spawn and only within the current conversation; /clear resets names.

facts.behavior: Final reports are scanned before Claude reads them; imitated tags such as <\system-reminder> get a backslash inserted and a '[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):' line may be prepended. Reports arrive under a header saying instructions inside carry no authority from the user. A report starting '⚠ This agent switched to <model> because its earlier model could not be used.' ran on a fallback model.
facts.limits: The scan doesn't remove content; tool calls still go through permission checks and sandboxing.

facts.behavior: Load from enabled plugins under scoped names (my-plugin:code-reviewer); lowest priority. claude plugin validate <dir> (v2.1.233+) validates; claude plugin eval evaluates delegation reliability.
facts.limits: hooks, mcpServers, and permissionMode frontmatter are ignored for plugin subagents 'for security'.

facts.behavior: Subagent requests 'count toward the same usage limits as your main conversation'. Docs advise choosing a smaller model per subagent (e.g. model: haiku), delegating verbose operations (tests, logs, docs) to subagents so only a summary returns, or running every subagent on one model. A switch to Opus also applies to subagents that inherit the session model.
facts.limits: Guidance only; no automatic cost routing or per-subagent budget.

facts.behavior: default (clears override), best (fable where available else opus), fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan. On the Anthropic API opus/sonnet/haiku resolve to Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5; on Microsoft Foundry to Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5. Aliases 'point to the recommended version for your provider and update over time'; pin with a full model name or ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL.
facts.limits: Aliases move over time unless pinned. Third-party providers should pin versions before rollout.

facts.feature: Setting the session model and precedence
facts.behavior: Priority: 1) /model during session; 2) claude --model at startup; 3) ANTHROPIC_MODEL; 4) model field in settings; 5) ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL for new sessions (v2.1.236+). /model saves to user settings (Enter) or session only (s). Resumed sessions keep their saved model unless --model/ANTHROPIC_MODEL given.
facts.limits: --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, and model setting values aren't validated up front; a typo errors on first request ('There's an issue with the selected model'). In -p mode /model is session only. ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL ignored if default, inherit, opusplan, or haiku.

facts.behavior: Opus 5.5 on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform; Sonnet 4.5 on Microsoft Foundry. An organization default model (Enterprise, v2.1.196+) replaces it.
facts.limits: Fable models are not the account-type default on any plan or provider.

facts.behavior: Uses opus in plan mode and automatically switches to sonnet for execution; each phase uses that model's context window. opusplan[1m] for 1M in both (/model support v2.1.265+).
facts.limits: Plan-mode Opus phase honors [1m] on pinned ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL.

facts.behavior: Levels low/medium/high/xhigh/max (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.x, Fable, Opus 4.7/4.8); Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 lack xhigh (runs as high). Order: 1) CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; 2) level picked in session (/effort, /model picker); 3) --effort; 4) settings (modelSettings per-model level or effortLevel); 5) model default: high, except medium on Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5/Haiku 5.5 and xhigh on Opus 4.7. /effort auto clears saved level.
facts.limits: effortLevel setting accepts low, medium, high, xhigh only; 'max isn't accepted as a level in either key'. max applies to the current session only unless set via CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=auto/unset sends no effort level.

facts.behavior: Including 'ultrathink' in a prompt requests deeper reasoning for that turn without changing session effort (can raise that turn to xhigh, v2.1.311+). Ultracode (/effort ultracode, --effort ultracode, ultracode setting) is a setting not a model level: starts at xhigh and Claude plans a workflow for every substantive task.
facts.limits: 'think hard' and similar phrases are passed through as ordinary text. Ultracode raises tokens per request and hits plan limits sooner; ultracode is unavailable when workflows are disabled; no managed setting disables ultracode alone.

facts.behavior: Thinking on by default; billed as output tokens. Lower cost with lower effort or /config disable, or MAX_THINKING_TOKENS on fixed-budget models.
facts.limits: Cannot be turned off on Fable 5.x, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5; alwaysThinkingEnabled:false and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 have no effect there. Adaptive-reasoning models ignore nonzero budgets.

facts.behavior: Fable, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7+ run 1M by default; Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 need [1m]. /autocompact, autoCompactWindow, --autocompact, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW set the window (100K-1M; env var wins). Native-1M models compact at about 967K by default. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 treats default-1M models as 200K.
facts.limits: Window capped at model's context window; unrecognized gateway model IDs assume 200K unless CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS or [1m] set.

facts.behavior: availableModels restricts /model, --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, model, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL, resume, subagents, teammates, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, skills, fast mode etc. Blocked /model is rejected with error; blocked startup model replaced with warning. Blocked family alias runs the newest allowed version; other blocked values fall back to inherited model. enforceAvailableModels:true (v2.1.175+) extends to Default. deniedModels and availableModelsMatch:'exact' (v2.1.283+, managed only) block specific versions.
facts.limits: availableModels alone leaves Default on runtime default. Managed availableModels cannot be extended by lower scopes. availableModels: [] blocks all named selections. Version-blocking keys need requiredMinimumVersion since older versions ignore them.

facts.behavior: --fallback-model sonnet,haiku or fallbackModel setting; switches on overload, unavailability, non-retryable server error. Also applies to subagents.
facts.limits: Switch lasts the current turn only; max three models; auth, billing, rate-limit, request-size, transport errors never trigger; entries outside availableModels dropped; flag beats setting.

facts.feature: Model env vars and pinning (ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL, modelOverrides, custom options)
facts.behavior: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{FABLE,OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL set what each alias maps to (HAIKU also used for background functionality); modelOverrides maps Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific IDs; ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION adds a picker entry; _SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES declares effort/thinking support for pinned IDs. Docs warn to pin specific version IDs on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry.
facts.limits: Capability and display vars take effect only on third-party providers (name/description also behind a gateway), not direct api.anthropic.com. ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL deprecated. modelOverrides keys must be Anthropic model IDs; unknown keys ignored.

facts.behavior: Prompt caching on by default. DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 disables globally; per-tier DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_{HAIKU,SONNET,OPUS,FABLE}. Subagent/teammate/workflow-agent requests fall outside main conversation TTL bucket: cache holds 5 minutes by default; subagentPromptCacheTtl=1h keeps an hour at higher cache-write rate.
facts.limits: Forks share the parent's cache; non-fork subagents have a separate cache. /usage Prompt cache line covers main conversation only, not subagents.

facts.behavior: 'Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default.' Enable with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json env or environment. Without it no team is set up, no team dirs written, Claude does not spawn or propose teammates. While enabled, a subagent that Claude names launches as a teammate, even if you did not ask for a team; set variable to 0 to revert (reapplied on settings save).
facts.limits: Interactive sessions only: in -p / Agent SDK a named subagent runs as an ordinary subagent. Other settings sources (project, local, --settings, managed) can re-enable; Claude Code does not ask for confirmation before launching a teammate.

facts.feature: Agent teams: architecture and shared state
facts.behavior: Team lead (main session), teammates (separate Claude Code instances), shared task list, mailbox. Mailboxes at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent}.json; team config ~/.claude/teams/{team}/config.json (removed at session end); task list ~/.claude/tasks/{team}/ (stays on disk, governed by cleanupPeriodDays). Task claiming uses file locking; completing a task auto-unblocks dependents.
facts.limits: Do not hand-edit team config (overwritten). No project-level team config (.claude/teams/teams.json not recognized). One team per session; no nested teams (teammates cannot spawn teammates); lead is fixed; no session resumption of in-process teammates (/resume, /rewind); task status can lag; slow shutdown.

facts.behavior: In-process (default; any terminal) or split panes (tmux or iTerm2 with it2). teammateMode setting or --teammate-mode: in-process, auto, tmux, iterm2.
facts.limits: Split panes not supported in VS Code integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, or Ghostty. --teammate-mode is experimental and not in --help.

facts.behavior: Order: 1) model named in spawn prompt; 2) subagent definition's model (inherit = lead's model); 3) CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL if not inherit; 4) lead's current model. A mod's agent.spawn hook replaces the first source. With CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 the first two don't apply. Checked against availableModels with substitution rules. Teammates inherit lead's effort level by default.
facts.limits: teammateDefaultModel removed in v2.1.234 (ignored). A teammate's model and fast mode are fixed at spawn; /model and /fast from a teammate view set the lead's, not the teammate's. Before v2.1.251 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL came first.

facts.feature: Agent teams: using subagent definitions as teammates
facts.behavior: Naming a subagent type applies its tools (adds SendMessage, and Task tools in sessions that have them), model, disallowedTools, effort, autoCompactWindow (in-process only), and body (appended to default system prompt in-process; replaces it in split-pane).
facts.limits: skills are not applied in either mode; mcpServers applied only to split-pane teammates (in-process ignores); disallowedTools/effort/autoCompactWindow in-process only. Re-applied for a restored teammate only if the agent file's folder is trusted.

facts.behavior: Teammates start with the lead's permission mode (except dontAsk, not inherited); --dangerously-skip-permissions propagates. In-process teammates run under the lead's live allow/deny rules; split-pane teammates get --disallowedTools and --tools (v2.1.309+). Teammate permission prompts appear in the lead session.
facts.limits: Cannot set per-teammate permission modes at spawn (can change after). --allowedTools is not passed to split-pane teammates. A teammate cannot approve a permission prompt or supply consent on the user's behalf; in auto mode the classifier treats relayed approval claims as untrusted and reviews each inter-agent message.

facts.behavior: A teammate spawned while the lead is in plan mode works read-only until its plan is ready, then sends a plan approval request to the lead.
facts.limits: If the teammate's permission mode hasn't changed, Claude Code approves the plan automatically without lead review; lead reviews only if the user Shift+Tabs an in-process teammate into plan mode. Teammate edits still go through permission prompts.

facts.behavior: TeammateIdle (exit 2 sends feedback and keeps teammate working), TaskCreated (exit 2 prevents creation), TaskCompleted (exit 2 prevents completion).
facts.limits: Hook-based; only run if configured.

facts.feature: Agent teams: team size and cost
facts.behavior: 'There's no hard limit on the number of teammates'; docs recommend starting with 3-5 and 5-6 tasks per teammate. Agent teams 'use significantly more tokens'; costs page says approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode; advises Sonnet for teammates, small teams, focused spawn prompts, shutting down finished teammates.
facts.limits: Guidance only; no enforced cap. Teammates share no conversation history with the lead; two teammates editing one file overwrite each other (docs advise file ownership).

facts.behavior: 'A dynamic workflow is a JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents at once.' Claude writes the script; runtime executes it in the background. Triggered by ultracode keyword, asking 'use a workflow', /effort ultracode, or running /deep-research or a saved /<name>. Saved to .claude/workflows/ or ~/.claude/workflows/ (project wins on name collision). Plugin workflows under workflows/ namespaced plugin:name. Intermediate results stay in script variables.
facts.limits: Up to 16 concurrent agents by default (CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS 1-256), 4,096 items per parallel()/pipeline(), 1,000 agents total per run; no import(), no mid-run user input, Date.now()/Math.random() throw in script. Keyword only works in human-typed prompts, not -p, scheduled tasks, or relayed webhooks. Workflow tool is withheld from subagents.

facts.behavior: Per-run prompt (Yes / Yes don't ask again / View raw script / No) in manual and accept-edits modes; auto mode prompts first launch only; bypass mode never prompts; -p and Agent SDK never prompt and use permission rules (Workflow or Workflow(<name>) in allow). Spawned subagents use the session's permission rules and the subagent permission-mode rules; agent tool calls get normal permission checks and sandboxing.
facts.limits: Ultracode skips the first-launch approval in auto mode. Keyword does not bypass permissions.

facts.feature: Workflow agent model resolution and cost warning
facts.behavior: Each workflow agent's model is chosen 'in the same order it uses for subagents'; a model the script names for a stage counts as the per-invocation model; when nothing else assigns one the agent runs on the session's model (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL covers workflow agents not assigned a model another way). availableModels substitution applies. A 'Large workflow' warning shows when a run schedules more than 25 agents or projects over 1.5M tokens.
facts.limits: Warning is advisory: it doesn't pause or limit the run; not shown with ultracode on. workflowSizeGuideline (unrestricted/small<5/medium<10/large<50; default medium, small on Pro) is advice to Claude, not a cap; runtime caps (1,000 agents) still apply.

facts.behavior: disableWorkflows:true in settings, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1, /config toggle, or organization managed settings / admin toggle. Disables /workflows, workflow commands, /workflow-authoring skill, ultracode keyword and effort toggle.
facts.limits: A run already in progress keeps going.

facts.feature: Workflow resume, stall and usage-limit handling
facts.behavior: Runs are resumable in the same session by relaunching: completed agents return saved results until the first changed prompt. Stalled agents auto-restart up to 5 times (stallMs, CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS). On usage limit an interactive claude.ai session pauses and auto-continues (autoContinueAtUsageLimit).
facts.limits: Run does not continue on its own after exiting the session; pause does not occur in -p, SDK, background sessions, or teammate sessions, when reset is over 24h away, or after 2 waits.

facts.feature: Cost tracking: /usage, /insights, spend and rate limits
facts.behavior: /usage Session block shows locally computed list-price cost, per-model token usage, prompt cache line, plan attribution of usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, recommendations (press f to apply /effort fixes). /insights writes an HTML report. Org controls: Teams/Enterprise spend limits and usage credits; Console workspace spend limits; modelPricing managed setting to report contracted rates. Rate-limit TPM/RPM per-user table by team size (e.g. 1-5 users 200k-300k TPM; 500+ users 10k-15k TPM).
facts.limits: Cost figure is an estimate, not an invoice; /usage numbers computed from local history on this machine only. Cloud-provider usage is not in Anthropic analytics. Average enterprise cost cited ~$13 per developer per active day, $150-250 per month.

facts.behavior: Docs advise: /clear between unrelated tasks; custom /compact instructions; 'Sonnet handles most coding tasks well and costs less than Opus. Reserve Opus for complex architectural decisions'; model: haiku for simple subagent tasks; lower effort for simple tasks; delegate verbose ops to subagents; prefer CLI tools over MCP; keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines and move workflow instructions to skills; use plan mode; specific prompts.
facts.limits: All advisory; nothing enforces model choice or context size. Background token use occurs from session recap, idle compaction, prompt suggestions, scheduled tasks, cross-session messages, goal check-ins (max 3 idle check-ins per goal).

unreachable: Part of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md between roughly characters 100000 and the start of the offset-100000 read was not seen in full; the 'Resume subagents' naming details were only partly visible, and the final-segment read began mid-sentence. The model-config.md section from about character 70000 to 100000 (fast mode, advisor, organization effort limits, modelPicker details) was summarized by the fetch tool only partially. All four requested URLs and the linked workflows page were reachable.

area: git and GitHub integration: commits, PR creation, GitHub app and Actions, code review, branch handling, worktree branches

facts.feature: Commits (no dedicated commit feature in these pages)
facts.behavior: The fetched pages describe no commit-message format, commit hook, attribution rule, or commit-time guard. Commits happen only as Claude runs git through its tools. In the Action, 'Claude analyze code, implement changes, and push commits'. Sandboxed worktree sessions allow git commit because the shared .git writes are allowed.
facts.limits: Nothing in these four pages enforces commit style, co-author lines, or branch policy on commits. Any such rule would have to come from permissions, hooks or CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: 'You can create pull requests by asking Claude directly ("create a pr for my changes")', or step by step: summarize changes, 'create a pr', then refine the description. Docs tip: review Claude's generated PR before submitting.
facts.limits: Prompt-driven recipe only; no flag or command that creates a PR. The page does not say which tool is used beyond gh pr create / glab mr create in the session-link sentence.

facts.behavior: 'Claude Code links the session to the PR when Claude creates it with gh pr create or glab mr create, and when Claude works on an existing PR.' --from-pr opens the session picker filtered to sessions linked to that PR; accepts a PR number, GitHub or GitHub Enterprise PR URL, GitLab MR URL or Bitbucket PR URL. A PR URL can also be pasted into the /resume picker search.
facts.limits: Opens a picker, does not check out the PR branch. Linking is automatic only for PRs created via gh pr create or glab mr create or worked on in-session.

facts.behavior: Installs the Claude GitHub App, adds the auth secret (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) as a repository secret, pushes a branch with selected workflow files (claude.yml, optionally claude-code-review.yml) and opens GitHub in the browser with a PR ready to create. Can be re-run to update workflow file. Esc stops partway.
facts.limits: Works only with github.com repositories (exits with a notice for gitlab.com or bitbucket.org remotes). Needs admin access to the repo and the gh CLI authenticated (warns if missing). Quick setup works with Claude API and subscriptions; Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry need the cloud-providers page. You must create and merge the setup PR yourself.

facts.behavior: Install Claude GitHub App, add secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (from claude setup-token; Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise), copy examples/claude.yml to .github/workflows/. App permissions the Action relies on: Contents, Issues, Pull requests (read and write).
facts.limits: Requires repo admin access. Org rollout: install app once at org level, org-level secret, workflow file per repo or reusable workflow; use API key not OAuth token for shared secrets. Workload identity federation (OIDC) inputs available to avoid a long-lived secret; needs id-token: write.

facts.behavior: One shared app for the Action, Code Review and web auto-fix. Permissions granted: Actions r/w, Administration read, Checks r/w, Contents r/w, Discussions r/w, Issues r/w, Members read, Merge queues read, Metadata read, Pull requests r/w, Repository hooks r/w, Statuses read, Workflows r/w.
facts.limits: Installation accepts the full set; GitHub does not allow a subset. A custom GitHub App (Contents, Issues, Pull requests) can serve the Action only; Code Review and web auto-fix still require the official app. New permissions need owner approval and old ones remain until approved.

facts.behavior: With no prompt input, Claude waits for the trigger phrase (default @claude) in an issue or PR comment, PR review, or body or title of a newly opened issue, then responds and implements, with progress and results as a comment on the triggering issue or PR. trigger_phrase input changes the phrase.
facts.limits: Comment must contain @claude as a complete word (not /claude or @claude-bot). Workflow must exist in the repo. Workflow 'if' contains(...) keeps runners from starting; the Action also checks the phrase itself.

facts.behavior: When the workflow provides a prompt input, Claude runs on any GitHub event (including cron schedule) without a mention. By default results go to the workflow run log, not a comment; Claude can post to issue or PR only if the prompt directs it and it has a tool that can post.
facts.limits: For a plain-text prompt Claude has no shell or GitHub API access until granted via --allowedTools in claude_args or a permissions.allow rule in settings input. A skill invocation can use its allowed-tools frontmatter. Scheduled workflows run only from the default branch; in public repos GitHub disables schedule after 60 days of inactivity.

facts.behavior: Two checks before Claude starts, run fails if rejected: (1) on issue and PR events the triggering user must have write access (allowed_non_write_users plus own github_token can override); (2) on every event a bot actor is rejected unless listed in allowed_bots (prevents loops; also applies to scheduled runs attributed to the user who last changed the cron).
facts.limits: Write-access check skipped for events no user authors, such as schedule.

facts.feature: Action runs a skill or plugin skill (review workflow example)
facts.behavior: prompt accepts /skill-name (needs actions/checkout for repo .claude/skills) or /plugin-name:skill-name with plugin_marketplaces and plugins inputs. Example runs /code-review:code-review --comment on PR open, synchronize, ready_for_review, reopened. --comment makes Claude post inline comments or one summary comment; without it nothing is posted, only the run log.
facts.limits: claude_args must name --allowedTools mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment or the inline-comment MCP server is not started. Claude skips draft and closed PRs, PRs it judges not to need review, and PRs that already have a Claude comment. On public repos GitHub withholds secrets from fork PRs, so review runs only on same-repo branches. Before v2.1.229 the review went only to the run log.

facts.behavior: 'Create a CLAUDE.md file in your repository root to define code style guidelines, review criteria, project-specific rules, and preferred patterns. Claude follows these guidelines when creating PRs and responding to requests.'
facts.limits: Guidance only; Claude reads it every run, so keep it concise for cost.

facts.feature: Action credential handling and least privilege
facts.behavior: Docs warn never to commit API keys or OAuth tokens; store as GitHub Secrets. 'Grant the workflow only the permissions it needs, and review Claude's changes before merging.'
facts.limits: Documentation guidance; nothing scans for committed secrets.

facts.behavior: Runs consume GitHub Actions minutes and API tokens (OAuth token uses subscription). Recommended caps: --max-turns in claude_args, workflow-level timeouts, GitHub concurrency controls, specific requests, issue templates, concise CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: No default cap is stated; controls are opt-in.

facts.feature: CI not triggering on Claude's commits
facts.behavior: GitHub does not trigger workflows on commits made with the default GITHUB_TOKEN. If github_token: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN is passed, remove it so the Action authenticates as the Claude GitHub App (or pass a custom app token). CI triggers must include push or pull_request.
facts.limits: Troubleshooting note about a GitHub platform behavior.

facts.behavior: Inputs: prompt, claude_args (any CLI argument, e.g. --max-turns, --model, --mcp-config, --allowedTools, --debug), anthropic_api_key, claude_code_oauth_token, github_token (default: authenticates as Claude GitHub App), plugin_marketplaces, plugins, settings, trigger_phrase, use_bedrock/use_vertex/use_foundry. Beta to v1 migration: @beta to @v1, drop mode, direct_prompt to prompt, custom_instructions to --append-system-prompt.
facts.limits: Without --model the Claude Code default model is used.

facts.behavior: use_bedrock, use_vertex or use_foundry route inference through your cloud account, authenticating via OIDC federation with no static cloud credentials.
facts.limits: Details on a separate page (github-actions-cloud-providers.md), not fetched.

facts.behavior: Several agents review each GitHub PR on Anthropic infrastructure: Find, Verify (filters false positives), Rank, Post. Leaves inline comments, a summary in the review body, and a check run named 'Claude Code Review'. Default focus is correctness bugs, not formatting or missing tests. 'A review never approves or blocks the pull request.' The check run never concludes as failure (neutral or skipped). Reviews can miss bugs.
facts.limits: Team and Enterprise plans only; GitHub (incl. GHES and GHE Cloud data residency) only; unavailable with Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configuration, or CMEK; an Owner must turn it on. Read-only repo access, does not push commits, does not build or run code. Runs only on Anthropic infrastructure, not self-hosted environments. Model not selectable; admins pick Quick, Standard (default) or Deep level, org-wide or per repo.

facts.feature: Code Review triggers and run settings
facts.behavior: Per-repository setting for when reviews run: once when a PR opens, after every push, or only on request (Manual). Someone with write access can comment @claude review. Automatic reviews skip drafts and forks.
facts.limits: Set by an Owner in setup. A later automatic review focuses on changes since the last one and posts fewer nits and pre-existing findings; the review body states counts not posted.

facts.behavior: @claude review (single review, no subscription), @claude review once (same), @claude review always (review and subscribe PR to push-triggered reviews), @claude review stop / off / pause (end subscription, no review started). Works on draft PRs.
facts.limits: Must be a new top-level PR comment, whole command on first line, commenter needs write/maintain/admin (checked with GitHub; bot comments ignored), PR must be open. In After-every-push mode you cannot stop reviews by comment (convert to draft). Fork PRs: always does not subscribe, Re-run does not start a review. Starting @claude review also triggers the GitHub Action if its default trigger_phrase @claude is used; set a different trigger_phrase to separate. Before July 2026, @claude review subscribed the PR.

facts.feature: Code Review severity levels and responding to findings
facts.behavior: Three markers: Important (bug to fix before merge), Nit (minor), Pre-existing (not introduced by the PR). Resolve a thread on GitHub to dismiss; replying alone does not dismiss. Pushing a fix lets the next review resolve its own thread. Replies are read by the next review only; a reply does not start a review.
facts.limits: If branch protection requires conversation resolution, each finding thread must be resolved before merge (a GitHub rule, not Claude's). Check run Details contains a machine-readable last line '<!-- bughunter-severity: {...} -->'; no such line on failed, timed-out, canceled or superseded reviews.

facts.feature: Code Review keeps earlier result after some pushes
facts.behavior: If a push leaves the PR adding and removing the same lines (empty commit, clean base merge, clean rebase) and no Important thread was resolved, the check run is titled 'Code review skipped — no new changes' or 'Code review not repeated — earlier findings still open' instead of a new review.
facts.limits: Github.com only. Re-run or @claude review forces a review (Re-run not on forks).

facts.feature: REVIEW.md and CLAUDE.md customization for Code Review
facts.behavior: Service reads CLAUDE.md (root and parent dirs of changed files; subdirectory CLAUDE.md when PR changes files there) and REVIEW.md (root, plus subdirectory REVIEW.md on protected-branch setups). REVIEW.md is read from the PR's base or default branch, 'never from the pull request's own changes'. Can lower severity, exclude paths, cap nits, add checks; supports @file includes and skill SKILL.md includes.
facts.limits: Exclusions, severity lowering and nit caps honored only when REVIEW.md is read from a protected branch (classic rule or ruleset on default branch; ruleset only elsewhere). Includes only on protected branch; max 8 files, 150,000 bytes combined, root-level filenames only (skills via .claude/skills/<folder>/SKILL.md, 30,000 bytes, no symlinks), max 64 non-http/anchor links or whole root REVIEW.md is skipped. Local /code-review reads CLAUDE.md but NOT REVIEW.md. Code Review does not run skills.

facts.behavior: Code Review service (PR activity or @claude review); local /code-review in a Claude Code session on any plan; Ultrareview (cloud sandbox, requires claude.ai sign-in; claude ultrareview [target] CLI, --post posts findings as one plain PR comment from your GitHub account, --no-post default, v2.1.227+); Claude in your own CI via GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD; your own subagent or skill.
facts.limits: Only the Team/Enterprise managed service posts the Claude Code Review check run. claude ultrareview exits 0 on success, 1 on failure, 45-minute default timeout (--timeout), --json for raw payload.

facts.behavior: 'Start Claude in an isolated git worktree at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>'. By default created on a new branch named worktree-<name>. Name optional (generated, e.g. bright-running-fox). Re-using an existing name opens the existing worktree. --worktree is also accepted with -p.
facts.limits: Requires a git repo with at least one commit (else 'Failed to resolve base branch "HEAD"'), or WorktreeCreate hook for non-git VCS. Interactive runs need workspace trust accepted first. Refuses if .claude, .claude/worktrees or the worktree dir is a symlink. Skips repo-config filter drivers (Git LFS --local gives pointer files; run git lfs pull). Docs recommend gitignoring .claude/worktrees/. Branch name worktree-<name> applies to the default location only.

facts.behavior: New worktrees branch from the repository's default branch on the remote ('fresh', default, usually main). Setting worktree.baseRef to 'head' branches from current local HEAD (carrying unpushed commits). For 'fresh', origin/HEAD is fetched if not fetched in 24 hours (5-second cap, never prompts; falls back to cached ref, then local HEAD if no remote). Subagent worktrees use the same base.
facts.limits: baseRef cannot be a branch name; to start from a specific existing branch use git worktree add directly. Reopened worktree resets to default branch only if clean, on its own branch, and has no commits or its PR was merged and remote branch deleted; otherwise reopens at old tip.

facts.feature: Branch worktree from a PR or MR (--worktree '#1234' or URL)
facts.behavior: Pass #<number>, a GitHub PR URL or GitLab MR URL; Claude Code fetches the head commit from origin (github.com: pull/<n>/head; gitlab.com: merge-requests/<n>/head; other hosts try pull first then merge-requests) and creates .claude/worktrees/pr-<number>. Reads only the number from the URL; always uses origin.
facts.limits: Fetch never waits for a password/passphrase/host confirmation and fails with 'Failed to fetch PR/MR #<n>'. GitLab MR needs v2.1.233+. Quote '#'. Reopening a PR worktree reopens at old tip.

facts.behavior: Creates a tmux session for the worktree; uses iTerm2 native panes when available; --tmux=classic for traditional tmux.
facts.limits: Requires --worktree.

facts.behavior: Asking Claude to 'work in a worktree' makes it create one with the EnterWorktree tool; it can switch directly to another worktree under .claude/worktrees/. ExitWorktree leaves.
facts.limits: Entering a path outside the repo's .claude/worktrees/ requires user approval (not suppressed by an EnterWorktree permission rule or don't-ask-again; only bypassPermissions skips). Both tools are removed or refused when permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories is on. Hook ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} stays at the project root; hook input cwd follows the worktree.

facts.behavior: On exit of an interactive worktree session Claude checks for changed or untracked files, uncommitted submodule work and new commits. Clean unnamed session: worktree and branch removed automatically. Clean named session: prompts. Worktree with work, another branch checked out with commits past start, or unverifiable state: prompts keep or remove; removing deletes the directory and its own branch with the work; keeping preserves both and prints a 'claude --worktree <name> --resume' command.
facts.limits: Applies to worktrees Claude created with git; hook-created ones use WorktreeRemove. Non-interactive -p runs have no exit prompt, are not cleaned up and leave their lock until a later sweep; remove with git worktree remove (git worktree unlock first if locked).

facts.feature: Worktree isolation enforcement (blocks edits and git in main checkout)
facts.behavior: While a session is isolated in a worktree (via --worktree, EnterWorktree or resume), Claude Code blocks: Edit/Write/NotebookEdit targeting the main checkout; Bash/PowerShell/Monitor commands whose working directory resolves to the main checkout; Bash/Monitor git redirects into the main checkout (git -C, --git-dir, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, cd then git); commands whose git target cannot be verified from text (computed command names, unparseable syntax, ${!name} expansions). Covers subagents spawned from the session and background sessions.
facts.limits: Does not track files a shell command writes: cp or a shell redirect into the main checkout without running git there is not refused (falls to normal permissions and sandboxing). The command-shape check cannot be turned off. PowerShell gets only the working-directory check. Applies to the repo Claude Code was launched from and the main checkout a linked worktree is linked from.

facts.behavior: Resuming a session that ended inside a worktree returns it to that worktree (interactive, --continue/--resume with -p, Agent SDK) after verifying it is still a separate checkout. --fork-session starts in the launch directory. Deleted worktree: session resumes in launch dir with notice. Transcript moves with worktree for git-created worktrees.
facts.limits: Refuses (interactive: continues without isolation; -p/SDK: errors) for worktrees whose git identity resolves into the main checkout, network paths, or that cannot be vouched for when launched from inside them. Launch from the main checkout to resume. Pre-v2.1.212 non-interactive resume stayed in start dir.

facts.behavior: Subagents can run in temporary worktrees via 'use worktrees for your agents' or isolation: worktree in custom subagent frontmatter. Auto-removed when the subagent finishes without changes; worktrees with changes remain until the periodic sweep can remove them without losing work.
facts.limits: Subagent takes instruction files from the main conversation; for worktrees in the default .claude/worktrees/ location it does not load the worktree-root CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ even if they differ on that branch.

facts.feature: Periodic sweep of subagent and background-session worktrees
facts.behavior: Removes worktrees Claude created for subagents and background sessions once older than cleanupPeriodDays. Worktree lock (git worktree lock) held while the agent runs; sweep releases locks of dead sessions.
facts.limits: Leaves in place: worktrees with changed/untracked files or unpushed commits, submodule changes (v2.1.274+), unverifiable filter drivers, unbackgrounded --worktree sessions, worktrees you made with git worktree add, and any worktree lacking Claude's git-metadata marker (incl. hook-created). Never releases locks you set.

facts.behavior: A .gitignore-syntax file in the project root; files matching a pattern AND gitignored are copied into each new worktree Claude creates with git (--worktree, subagent, desktop parallel sessions).
facts.limits: Tracked files are never duplicated. Not processed when a WorktreeCreate hook is used. Special **/ semantics for wholly ignored directories.

facts.feature: WorktreeCreate / WorktreeRemove hooks (custom or non-git worktrees)
facts.behavior: A WorktreeCreate hook replaces the default git worktree logic entirely, including location other than .claude/worktrees/; it prints the directory path. Pair with WorktreeRemove. Enables --worktree and /batch (v2.1.281+) for SVN, Perforce, Mercurial.
facts.limits: Hook directory must be outside any git repository to pass isolation checks. Hook must print a valid directory or startup exits 1.

facts.feature: What worktrees share with the main checkout
facts.behavior: Shared .git directory (git commit works from a worktree even with sandbox enabled); project-scope plugins; permission approvals ('Yes, and don't ask again' saves to main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json and applies to all worktrees); untracked/missing .claude/skills, agents, commands read through from the main checkout (skills read-through v2.1.277+).
facts.limits: On Windows or where the repo root is not used, the rule stays with that worktree. Desktop-app worktree sessions read project config, hooks, skills, .mcp.json from the main checkout root; CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules still load from the worktree.

facts.behavior: Docs suggest git worktree add ../project-feature-a -b feature-a, or add from an existing branch, then cd and run claude; git worktree list / remove.
facts.limits: This is the documented route for starting from a specific existing branch or placing the worktree outside the repo; Claude Code's cleanup and sweep do not manage these worktrees.

facts.feature: claude rm for background sessions with worktrees
facts.behavior: Removes a background session from the list. If refused over its worktree, prints the exact flag: --discard-unpushed <commit>@<worktree-id> (discards unpushed commits, v2.1.260+) or --force-remove-worktree <worktree-id> (v2.1.268+).
facts.limits: Conversation transcript stays local, resumable via claude --resume.

facts.behavior: claude auto-mode defaults prints the built-in auto mode classifier rules as JSON; --label 'Git Destructive' prints only rules whose label starts with that prefix; claude auto-mode config shows effective config.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.208+. The CLI page only lists the command; what the Git Destructive rules contain is on the permission-modes page, not fetched.

facts.feature: Permission rules for git commands via CLI flags
facts.behavior: --allowedTools lets named tools run without prompting (example patterns Bash(git log *), Bash(git diff *)); --disallowedTools adds deny rules (scoped rule like Bash(rm *) leaves tool but denies matches). Same can be passed to the Action via claude_args.
facts.limits: Examples only in the CLI reference; rule semantics (Bash rule limits) live on the permissions page, not fetched.

facts.feature: Scheduling PR work (routines, desktop tasks, /loop, Actions)
facts.behavior: Options for recurring work like reviewing open PRs: cloud scheduled tasks/routines (can trigger on GitHub events), desktop scheduled tasks, GitHub Actions, and /loop in the current CLI session.
facts.limits: Prompt must state success criteria since tasks run autonomously and cannot ask questions.

facts.behavior: Example: git log --oneline -20 | claude -p "summarize these recent commits"; non-interactive mode usable in CI and pre-commit hooks.
facts.limits: Recipe only.

area: Settings precedence and merge chain, managed settings, model allow and deny lists, auto mode configuration, enterprise lockout

facts.behavior: Claude Code reads settings from four sources: User ~/.claude/settings.json (you, every project), Shared project .claude/settings.json (everyone in the folder; commit it), Project local .claude/settings.local.json (you, this project only), and Managed (managed-settings.json, MDM, or server-managed). ~/.claude.json is a fifth file Claude Code writes for itself (account details, MCP configs, per-project trust state, global config keys).
facts.limits: Installing Claude Code creates no settings file. Local file is kept out of git only when Claude Code creates it (adds **/.claude/settings.local.json to the global git excludes); a hand-created local file must be gitignored by you. Global config keys apply only from ~/.claude.json.

facts.behavior: Highest first: managed settings, command line (--settings), project local, shared project, user. 'A key set at a higher level overrides the same key set lower down.' A key left out at a higher level keeps its value from lower files. Nothing in your own files or --settings overrides a managed key.
facts.limits: Environment variables are not a level in the stack; flag/env-var versus key is decided per pair (ANTHROPIC_MODEL overrides the model key from any file; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL applies only when no file sets model). Other flags like --model are not part of the stack. A few security keys honor a stricter lower-level value (see exceptions).

facts.behavior: 'When you set the same list key, such as permissions.allow, in more than one file, Claude Code combines the lists instead of picking one, so each file can add entries without removing another file's.'
facts.limits: Four model-related keys follow their own rules: fallbackModel (whole value from highest-precedence file that defines it), modelPicker (whole value from highest of managed, --settings, user; ignored in project and local; v2.1.242+), availableModels (managed list applied as-is, user/project/local entries ignored; never merges across managed sources; non-managed scopes merge), modelSettings (resolved one model at a time with effortLevel).

facts.feature: Exceptions to managed settings precedence (stricter lower-level value wins)
facts.behavior: For restrictive keys Claude Code honors a stricter value from a scope that otherwise cannot override managed: disableClaudeAiConnectors true from any scope; enableArtifact false / disableArtifact true from any scope (v2.1.242+); isolatePeerMachines true from any scope; permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories true from any scope (v2.1.257+); permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories true from any scope (v2.1.314+); autoMode.classifyAllShell true from ~/.claude/settings.json or --settings; remoteControlAtStartup false from project/local; crossSessionInbound stricter value from project/local (accept < hold < refuse); useAutoModeDuringPlan false, syncClaudeAiSkills false, syncClaudeAiPlugins false from managed, --settings, user, or local; maxEffortLevel lowest cap from any scope (v2.1.267+).
facts.limits: A false in .claude/settings.json is ignored for useAutoModeDuringPlan/syncClaudeAiSkills/syncClaudeAiPlugins. A project/local remoteControlAtStartup true is ignored. Also, an embedding app that sets CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST has its model config override managed model, fallbackModel, modelPicker, modelOverrides and managed-env model variables, but a managed availableModels allowlist stays in force unless the app supplies its own.

facts.feature: Keys that never take effect from repository settings files
facts.behavior: Keys whose Scope is User, User or managed, User local or managed, Managed, or Global config never apply from the shared .claude/settings.json (apart from a few that a repo file can still switch off). permissions.defaultMode values auto and bypassPermissions do not take effect from project or local settings (set in user or managed, or --permission-mode); before v2.1.257 bypassPermissions took effect from any file. Telemetry export variables in an env block do not take effect from project/local settings apart from a few off values.
facts.limits: Applies to project and local files, not user/managed. VS Code extension conversations read only user, managed and --settings values for defaultMode.

facts.feature: Workspace trust for committed project keys
facts.behavior: permissions.allow rules, permissions.additionalDirectories, extraKnownMarketplaces, and most env values in the committed .claude/settings.json apply only after each teammate trusts the folder. 'deny and ask rules apply right away.' allow rules in an untracked .claude/settings.local.json apply without the trust step; if the local file is tracked by git the trust step applies to it too.
facts.limits: Until trust, teammates still see prompts and do not get plugins from a declared marketplace.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md (A committed key doesn't reach teammates; Keep personal settings out of a repository)

facts.feature: Location of settings.local.json and project settings in git repos/worktrees
facts.behavior: Starting in a subdirectory of a git repo, Claude Code reads and writes .claude/settings.local.json at the repository root (v2.1.211+); in a worktree it uses the main checkout's root file. Shared .claude/settings.json is read from the session's primary working directory, so start Claude Code at the repo root. After /cd the files are read from the new directory (v2.1.246+).
facts.limits: Local file stays with .claude/settings.json outside a git repo, when the repo root is the home directory, on Windows, or when ownership checks fail. Agent SDK resolveSettings() reads the file from the starting directory. 'Don't Always allow' choices are written only to the local file in the CLI.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md (Where Claude Code keeps the local file in a git repository)

facts.behavior: Pass a key as JSON inline or as a file path; Claude Code applies it above user, project and local files and below managed settings, for that session only, without writing to any file. It can set any key a user settings file can set.
facts.limits: Cannot set Managed or Global config keys; cannot override managed settings.

facts.feature: Settings reload and when edits take effect
facts.behavior: Claude Code watches settings files and reloads them on change, applying most edits (including permissions, hooks, apiKeyHelper) to the running session; runs the ConfigChange hook for each settings-file change detected. MDM/console managed settings arrive on a schedule (server-managed fetched at startup and polled hourly; MDM checked every 30 minutes; files reloaded on change).
facts.limits: Some keys are read once at session start. ConfigChange hook does not fire for managed settings arriving from MDM or the console. Removing permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories mid-session does not lift the block in running sessions; restart required. requiredMinimumVersion, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh and some user-editable keys take effect at next session start. A new/changed policyHelper takes effect next launch.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md (When edits take effect); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Where and when a policy applies)

facts.behavior: Settings Error: a user, project or local file with invalid JSON or schema-rejected value shows a dialog at interactive start (fix with Claude, exit, or continue without). Settings Warning: individual bad entries (malformed permission rule, unknown hook event) are skipped and the rest of the file stays in effect. A -p run shows no dialog and skips the broken file or values; claude doctor lists what was dropped. Settings files are strict JSON (no comments or trailing commas).
facts.limits: User/project/local files stay strict (whole file rejected on top-level failure); managed settings are more tolerant (see managed invalid entries).

facts.behavior: /status 'Setting sources' line lists each settings file loaded; for managed it shows the source in parentheses (remote, plist, HKLM, file, drop-ins, file + drop-ins, ... merged, HKCU, parent process, helper) and a 'Skipped sources' line (v2.1.242+) naming managed sources found but not selected. claude doctor lists rejected entries with source and field and, on v2.1.261+, an 'Organization policy' line.
facts.limits: The Setting sources line does not show which file supplied each key. /config Config tab is not a view of settings.json contents.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md (Confirm what loaded); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Check that a policy is in force)

facts.behavior: Cloud sessions run on a fresh clone: shared .claude/settings.json is read in a single-repo session outside a project's threads; user and project-local settings are not read; device MDM/managed-settings.json does not reach an Anthropic-hosted cloud session, only server-managed settings do. Self-hosted environments also read the managed settings file in the runner image. In project cloud threads none of a repo's settings.json permission rules, hooks or env apply. Multi-repo hosted sessions read only enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces from each repo.
facts.limits: /config in browser opens claude.ai settings rather than changing a value. Cloud sessions honor only acceptEdits, plan, default, auto for permissions.defaultMode.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md (Settings in cloud sessions); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Where and when a policy applies)

facts.behavior: Four ways: server-managed (claude.ai admin console or self-hosted Claude apps gateway; fetched at startup, polled hourly), MDM/OS policy (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist domain, Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode 'Settings' value; checked every 30 min), file-based (managed-settings.json plus managed-settings.d/ and managed-mcp.json in /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode, /etc/claude-code, or C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode; reloaded on change), and HKCU registry (Windows/WSL; checked every 30 min). All carry the same policy keys as settings.json. Applies on terminal, VS Code and JetBrains extensions, desktop Code tab and Agent SDK sessions (SDK loads managed settings even when settingSources excludes user/project/local).
facts.limits: Legacy path C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json is not read. A policy applies to everyone it reaches; claude.ai console cannot target a group yet (a self-hosted gateway delivers per IdP group). Cowork never fetches server-managed settings from console; remote sessions have no device policy. Claude Tag sessions don't receive server-managed settings. Managed settings bind Claude Code only, not other tools calling the API. Symlinked managed files are followed with a /status warning if target is outside the system directory.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Choose a delivery mechanism; Where each mechanism stores the policy)

facts.behavior: Source ranking: 1 remote (server-managed/gateway), 2 MDM/OS policy, 3 managed-settings files (managed-settings.d/*.json and managed-settings.json merged), 4 HKCU registry. Default 'first-wins': 'Claude Code uses the highest-ranked source that delivers at least one policy key and ignores the rest rather than merging them', no warning shown for skipped sources. 'merge' (v2.1.242+) applies every admin source: lists union, locks take strictest value, restriction allowlists (availableModels, allowedMcpServers, allowedProviders, strictKnownMarketplaces, allowedChannelPlugins, fallbackModel) taken whole from highest source that sets it, modelPicker/permissions.defaultMode/apiKeyHelper read from highest source only, env merged per variable.
facts.limits: Key is read only from the highest-ranked source carrying it or a policy key; HKCU and embedding-host parent settings never merge. Under merge, lower-source allow rules are added, so use only if all lower sources are admin-controlled. Remote settings are fetched only when authenticating directly to Anthropic API with an eligible credential or via a gateway; not on other providers or when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points elsewhere.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (How Claude Code combines managed sources; Compose every managed source); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md (managedSourcesBehavior)

facts.feature: Keys read from every admin source (cross-source keys)
facts.behavior: Under first-wins, these are still read from all admin sources (not HKCU): sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly and sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly (true in any source turns lock on, allowlists unioned), allowAllClaudeAiMcps, allowManagedMcpServersOnly (true in any source), deniedMcpServers and disableClaudeAiConnectors, sandbox binary paths/ripgrep, sandbox.filesystem.disabled, sandbox.network.strictAllowlist, useAutoModeDuringPlan/syncClaudeAiSkills/syncClaudeAiPlugins false, enableArtifact false, maxEffortLevel lowest cap, commit-trailer opt-out in attribution, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, and env merged per variable (v2.1.223+). allowedProviders has its own rule (v2.1.285+).
facts.limits: Most other keys are read only from the selected source even if it leaves them unset.

facts.behavior: Claude Code merges managed-settings.json first, then every *.json in managed-settings.d/ alphabetically (use numeric prefixes). Single values: later file replaces; lists: combine with duplicates removed; nested blocks (env, sandbox) merge key by key; fallbackModel, modelPicker: later replaces whole; extraKnownMarketplaces and managedMcpServers: same-name later entry replaces whole.
facts.limits: Hidden files and non-.json files ignored. File-based tier only.

facts.feature: Login keys come from MDM/file over remote settings
facts.behavior: On a machine with an MDM policy or managed settings file, Claude Code takes login keys (forceLoginOrgUUID, forceLoginMethod claudeai/console, gateway login keys) from that policy or file, even if remote settings set them. If MDM policy sets any policy key, login keys in the file are ignored even under merge. If the MDM/file omits forceLoginOrgUUID or forceLoginMethod, the remote value applies. Gateway login keys are never read from remote settings.
facts.limits: Until every client runs v2.1.299+, set the keys in server-managed settings too.

facts.behavior: A host app (Claude Desktop, IDE extension, Agent SDK) can pass managed settings via SDK managedSettings option ('parent settings'). By default Claude Code ignores parent settings whenever an admin source is present. parentSettingsBehavior 'merge' (read from highest-priority admin source) applies host settings under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. When any admin source sets allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, parent-supplied allow rules and additionalDirectories are dropped. Managed forceLoginOrgUUID, availableModels, allowedMcpServers (while allowManagedMcpServersOnly on), allowedProviders, strictKnownMarketplaces block parent-supplied values; a parent blockedMarketplaces applies in addition.
facts.limits: Unless allowManaged*Only locks are also set, host's permission allow rules and sandbox allowlists still apply under merge. No effect when no admin tier exists (host settings then apply as the only managed tier, still filtered to restrictive values).

facts.behavior: Managed-only key {path, timeoutMs (min 1000, default 10000), refreshIntervalMs (0 or >=60000)}: an executable run before the first prompt that emits JSON envelope with a managedSettings object (capped 1 MiB); that object becomes the only managed settings for the run (MDM, file, HKCU ignored; cross-source keys read from helper output alone; parent settings never merged).
facts.limits: Read only from macOS plist, Windows HKLM or managed settings file, and only when that is the highest source with a policy key; ignored in server-managed settings, HKCU, parent settings. Server-managed settings delivered at launch take precedence and the helper doesn't run. A bare settings object without a managedSettings key applies nothing and reports no error. Path must be absolute normalized.

facts.behavior: A failed startup run (non-zero exit, timeout, not executable, no file at path, over 1 MiB output, non-JSON stdout, unrepairable schema violation) prints the reason and 'refuses to start' (interactive, claude -p, Agent SDK, background sessions, most subcommands). A failed background refresh keeps the last successful policy in effect and /status shows the failing refresh.
facts.limits: Deliberate; a helper needing outage resilience should serve from its own cache and exit 0. Invalid policyHelper value is reported as a dropped entry and the session starts without running a helper.

facts.feature: Invalid managed entries: repair, drop, and fail closed
facts.behavior: For managed sources, Claude Code first skips each repairable entry with a warning, then drops values that still fail, unless the key fails closed. Fail-closed single-restrictive-value keys (e.g. allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, disableAutoMode, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt) read as the restrictive value until fixed (v2.1.282+). Per-key fallbacks: allowedMcpServers empty allowlist; allowedProviders empty allowlist (Claude Code doesn't start); availableModels empty allowlist (only Default model available); availableModelsMatch treated as exact; forceLoginOrgUUID no organization permitted; crossSessionInbound refuse; strictKnownMarketplaces empty allowlist; deniedModels wholly invalid value dropped (blocks no models); permissions/autoMode blocks repaired per field (invalid defaultMode reads as default; unreadable deny/ask withholds allow and additionalDirectories; unreadable soft_deny/hard_deny withholds allow and environment).
facts.limits: A managed file/drop-in/plist/HKLM value present but not parseable as a JSON object makes Claude Code refuse to start (even if another admin source is valid). Unreadable by OS permission: session starts without that source; other read errors: exit at startup. Invalid disableAllHooks is dropped. requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion fail open. Malformed HKCU never blocks launch. Interactive sessions show a startup dialog; -p prints to stderr; claude doctor lists entries.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Find entries Claude Code dropped; Keys that fail closed)

facts.feature: What a developer can still change under managed settings
facts.behavior: Managed values are not overridden by user/project/local/--settings. Outside that rule: a managed model is only a default (--model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL still pick the session model, constrained by availableModels); a managed autoCompactWindow is a default (--autocompact / CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW still set it); a local admin can edit the managed source itself; edits to the server-managed local cache last only until next successful fetch.
facts.limits: Managed settings bind Claude Code only, not other tools using the API.

facts.behavior: 'A managed list constrains /model, --model, and the model key in a developer's own files; a model outside it can't be selected.' A model ID entry such as claude-opus-5 also permits later versions (Opus 5.5) by default prefix matching; family aliases (opus) cover the family. Managed list applied as-is, entries in user/project/local ignored; never merged across managed sources.
facts.limits: With default prefix matching it does not touch the Default option on its own; pair with enforceAvailableModels. Scope is any file, but only enforced via managed. Invalid managed value => empty allowlist, only Default model available. A managed model key alone is not a lock.

facts.behavior: Managed-only (v2.1.283+), default 'prefix'. 'exact' makes each availableModels entry permit only the version it names (claude-opus-5 permits Opus 5 but not Opus 5.5); a family alias like opus still covers the whole family.
facts.limits: Ignored outside managed settings, with a warning. Invalid managed value treated as exact. Under merge it is a lock (strictest wins).

facts.behavior: Managed-only (v2.1.283+): blocks specific models even ones availableModels permits. A model ID with no minor version (claude-opus-5) also blocks later minor versions (Opus 5.5); write claude-opus-5-0 to block Opus 5 alone. Lists combine across managed sources under merge.
facts.limits: best, opusplan, and default entries are ignored. Non-string entries stripped; a wholly invalid value is dropped with a warning and blocks no models until fixed.

facts.behavior: Any-file key (v2.1.175+), default false. Makes availableModels also constrain the Default option. When the organization deploys any managed settings, Claude Code reads this key from the managed source alone and ignores it in other files.
facts.limits: No effect when availableModels is unset or empty.

facts.feature: model key and model selection precedence
facts.behavior: A managed model is 'a starting default, not a lock; the locks are availableModels and deniedModels.' --model picks only from models the organization allows. ANTHROPIC_MODEL overrides the model key from any file; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL applies only when no file sets model. /model saves to user settings as default for new sessions (press s in picker to switch without saving).
facts.limits: Switching models re-reads the conversation uncached (separate prompt cache per model). Embedding host with CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST overrides managed model/fallbackModel/modelPicker/modelOverrides.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md (Settings precedence; Exceptions); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (What a developer can change)

facts.behavior: Managed-only (v2.1.285+): array of anthropic, bedrock, vertex, foundry, anthropicAws, mantle, customEndpoint, gateway. 'A session on a provider that isn't listed is refused at startup, at login, and when it next contacts the API, so switching to an unlisted provider mid-session is refused too.' Machine-set (MDM/file) list keeps applying when server-managed delivers one; session may use only providers on both lists.
facts.limits: Unrecognized entries dropped and reported; empty list or all unrecognized => every provider refused and Claude Code doesn't start. Invalid value enforced as empty allowlist.

facts.behavior: Managed-only boolean: 'Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules. Claude Code then ignores allow, ask, and deny rules in user, project, local, and --settings files, ignores --allowedTools, hides the always-allow choices in permission prompts, and stops saving new rules.' From v2.1.282, allowed-tools frontmatter in repo/user skills and commands, --add-dir directories, and per-session inline plugins is ignored (v2.1.305+ for Desktop Code/Cowork sessions list).
facts.limits: --disallowedTools rules and the current session's deny/ask rules still apply (they only restrict). Parent-settings allow rules and additionalDirectories dropped; parent deny/ask kept except Read/Edit patterns starting with '!'. Doesn't lock the MCP allowlist (use allowManagedMcpServersOnly). Managed skills and bundled skills keep allowed-tools. Cowork folder pre-approval must be re-added as managed allow rules.

facts.behavior: Managed-only boolean: only hooks from managed settings, Agent SDK in-process hooks, and hooks from plugins force-enabled in managed enabledPlugins (matched on full plugin@marketplace ID) run. User, project, local hooks, other plugins' hooks and monitors, and agent-frontmatter hooks are blocked. Command-sourced plugins and marketplace headersHelper commands are disabled unless disableCommandPluginSources is explicitly false. statusLine, fileSuggestion, subagentStatusLine read from managed only.
facts.limits: Mods built into Claude Code keep running (allowManagedModsOnly blocks users' mods only). The /goal command can't run while set because it depends on hooks. Monitors block requires v2.1.310+.

facts.behavior: When true, only allowedMcpServers from managed settings are respected; deniedMcpServers still merges from all sources. A true in any admin source turns the lock on; the allowedMcpServers list comes from the highest-ranked admin source that sets one (v2.1.273+). If no admin source sets a list, every server passing the denylist loads. managedMcpServers (v2.1.259+) provides servers to all users; managed-mcp.json deployed alongside.
facts.limits: Invalid allowedMcpServers enforced as empty allowlist, but managedMcpServers and managed-mcp.json servers still load. Users can still add servers with claude mcp add or .mcp.json unless allowedMcpServers restricts them.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Keys only a managed source can set; Keys read from every admin source)

facts.feature: Other managed-only locks (marketplaces, plugins, sideload flags, channels)
facts.behavior: strictKnownMarketplaces (allowlist; an empty array 'is a complete lockdown that blocks every marketplace source, including the official Anthropic marketplace'), blockedMarketplaces (checked before download), strictPluginOnlyCustomization (true locks skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers from user/project sources; array/subkeys per surface), disableSideloadFlags (rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, --mcp-config at startup and exits with error; also CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS v2.1.280+, SDK addPlugins v2.1.301+), disableCommandPluginSources, allowedChannelPlugins, channelsEnabled, pluginSuggestionMarketplaces, pluginTrustMessage.
facts.limits: Users can still add MCP servers via claude mcp add / .mcp.json when only disableSideloadFlags is set. disableSideloadFlags in cloud sessions drops server-delivered --mcp-config entries rather than failing, except type sdk entries and Claude Tag Slack tools. Version requirements vary (disableSideloadFlags v2.1.193+, disableCommandPluginSources v2.1.229+).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Keys only a managed source can set); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md

facts.behavior: 'Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode.' Claude Code then rejects the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag and ignores an agent definition's permissionMode: bypassPermissions (subagent runs with parent's mode). Takes precedence over --dangerously-skip-permissions.
facts.limits: Scope Any file, typically set in managed settings; value is the string 'disable'. Before v2.1.223 frontmatter permission mode applied even with bypass disabled. Under merge it is a lock (strictest wins). Invalid managed value reads as restrictive.

facts.behavior: Sets the permission mode new sessions start in: default (reads only without asking), acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, manual (alias of default). --permission-mode and --dangerously-skip-permissions override for one session. 'Permission rules layer on top of every mode: deny rules block in every mode, including bypassPermissions.'
facts.limits: auto and bypassPermissions don't take effect from project or local settings. Read from highest-ranked managed source only under merge. Cloud sessions honor only acceptEdits, plan, default, auto. Invalid managed value reads as default.

facts.behavior: 'Remove auto mode from the Shift+Tab cycle. Any session that would otherwise start in auto mode, whether from --permission-mode auto, a settings file, or the built-in default, starts in default instead.' Administrators set it in managed settings to prevent developers from using auto mode. Also accepted as permissions.disableAutoMode.
facts.limits: Scope Any file, most useful in managed; value is the string 'disable'. Fail-closed key when invalid in managed settings.

facts.feature: Auto mode overview and ordering relative to permission rules
facts.behavior: Auto mode routes tool calls through a classifier that 'blocks anything irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your environment.' 'Deny and explicit ask rules are evaluated before the classifier and still block or prompt.' Content-scoped permissions.ask rules always force a prompt even in auto mode; permissions.deny blocks before the classifier is consulted and cannot be overridden. By default the classifier trusts only the working directory and the current repo's configured remotes. Available on all providers including Bedrock, Vertex-equivalent Agent Platform, Foundry and gateway sessions.
facts.limits: Ask rule like Bash(git push *) matches only commands beginning with that prefix; git -C <dir> push or git -c k=v push don't match (use a PreToolUse hook for full-text inspection). A boundary stated only in conversation can be lost if context compaction removes the message. Pushes to any branch of the working repo including default branch and PR creation are allowed by default, except branches named like deploy/publication targets (production, release, gh-pages) which are judged on their own terms; force push, secrets in commits stay blocked.

facts.behavior: Classifier reads autoMode from ~/.claude/settings.json, managed settings, and --settings/Agent SDK inline JSON. Entries from each scope are combined (arrays concatenated). Classifier also reads the same CLAUDE.md content Claude loads, so 'never force push' in CLAUDE.md steers both.
facts.limits: 'The classifier doesn't read autoMode from project settings in .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json' (repo-injected allow rules risk); move any autoMode block in settings.local.json to ~/.claude/settings.json. A developer can extend environment/allow/soft_deny/hard_deny but can't remove managed entries; however a developer-added allow entry can override an organization soft_deny: 'additive, not a hard policy boundary.'
