For must-never actions use permissions.deny in managed settings. Scope in settings reference: User or managed.

facts.behavior: Prose entries telling the classifier which repos, buckets, domains, services are trusted (context, trust, and sensitivity slots such as Source control, Trusted cloud buckets, Trusted internal domains, Key internal services, Sensitive remote targets, Protected IaC scopes). Include the literal string "$defaults" in an array to splice in built-in entries at that position and keep inheriting updates.
facts.limits: Entries are natural-language prose, not regex or tool patterns. Setting any of environment, allow, soft_deny, hard_deny without "$defaults" replaces the entire default list for that section (dropping e.g. built-in force-push, curl | bash, production-deploy blocks in soft_deny, and the data-exfiltration rule in hard_deny). Each section evaluated independently.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config.md (Define trusted infrastructure; Override the block and allow rules)

facts.behavior: Four-tier precedence inside the classifier: hard_deny blocks unconditionally (user intent and allow exceptions don't apply); soft_deny blocks next (user intent and allow can override); allow overrides matching soft_deny as exceptions; explicit user intent overrides remaining soft blocks only if the user's message directly and specifically describes the exact action.
facts.limits: General requests ('clean up the repo') don't count as explicit intent. These are prose rules judged by a model classifier, not tool-pattern rules; for tool-pattern hard blocks use permissions.deny.

facts.behavior: When true, every Bash and PowerShell command goes through the classifier while auto mode is active, suspending all shell allow rules (except critical-path removals handling). Default false: only broad rules like Bash(*) and wildcarded interpreter/shell-wrapper prefixes (and rules naming Monitor) are suspended; narrow rules like Bash(npm test) still pre-approve and skip the classifier unless the command carries per-command allowed domains. Requires v2.1.193+.
facts.limits: Trades latency for coverage (each shell command counts as a classifier call). Applies only while auto mode is active. A true from ~/.claude/settings.json or --settings is honored even when managed sets false.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md (autoMode.classifyAllShell); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config.md (Route all shell commands through the classifier)

facts.behavior: Default true: in plan mode the classifier reviews shell commands when auto mode is available and no prompt appears (except critical-path removals). false gives a permission prompt for every command outside the built-in read-only set. Shown in /config as 'Use auto mode during plan'.
facts.limits: Scope User, local, or managed; 'A repository can't turn it off for you.' A false from managed, --settings, user, or local turns it off; .claude/settings.json false is ignored; a left-out user/local file doesn't count (v2.1.314+).

facts.behavior: skipAutoPermissionPrompt (User or managed) skips the one-time notice describing auto mode shown when you first enter auto mode yourself. skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt (User, local, or managed) skips the one-time confirmation for bypass mode.
facts.limits: A repository can't set skipAutoPermissionPrompt for you. Only matters where the notice hasn't yet appeared.

facts.behavior: claude auto-mode defaults prints built-in environment/allow/soft_deny/hard_deny rules as JSON (--label <prefix> filters by case-insensitive rule label prefix); claude auto-mode config prints the effective rules with settings applied; claude auto-mode critique gives AI feedback on custom entries (ambiguous, redundant, false-positive-prone); claude auto-mode reset removes the autoMode section from ~/.claude/settings.json after a confirmation (--yes skips).
facts.limits: reset changes only ~/.claude/settings.json; managed and --settings autoMode rules still apply.
facts.citation: CLI: claude auto-mode defaults | config | critique | reset; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config.md (Inspect the defaults and your effective config)

facts.behavior: /auto-mode-setup drafts autoMode.environment (and sometimes rule) entries from CLAUDE.md, README, config files, git remotes, autoMode/permissions.allow settings, and hosts/buckets/command names from recent session commands (never your messages), plus two optional scans (shell history first words, remote hosts of repos under home); accepting writes to ~/.claude/settings.json, and offers to remove permissions.allow rules auto mode ignores (e.g. Bash(*)). /permissions Auto mode tab (v2.1.246+) views/edits classifier rules and environment entries, shows managed/--settings entries read-only, saves to ~/.claude/settings.json. Recently blocked tab lets you press r to approve a blocked action for retry.
facts.limits: Plan/version requirements (Pro/Max/Ultra/Team v2.1.228+; Enterprise or Console API key v2.1.283+). Draft accepted or discarded as a whole. Unavailable in cloud sessions. Approving a blocked action does not add a permission rule. Turn off with skillOverrides {"auto-mode-setup": "off"}; disableBundledSkills doesn't turn it off.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config.md (Generate environment entries; Edit rules from /permissions; Review denials)

facts.behavior: Restricts login to claudeai (claude.ai accounts only), console (Console accounts only), or gateway (sends people to a cloud gateway). Every first-party login path applies it (VS Code extension, Agent SDK, claude setup-token, /install-github-app) except the terminal's interactive /login or first-run screen, which pre-selects the method without enforcing it (before v2.1.212 only terminal logins applied it). With gateway set by a managed source, leftover login, API key or apiKeyHelper credentials are not used (v2.1.261+).
facts.limits: Scope Any file, but 'gateway' is honored only from the same sources as forceLoginGatewayUrl (never server-managed settings) and treated as unset elsewhere. Selecting a cloud provider via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK etc. skips the gateway sign-in.

facts.behavior: From a managed source, requires claude.ai account logins to belong to one organization (single UUID) or any of several (array). From any other settings file a single UUID only pre-selects the organization at login without restricting it (and stops offering keyless Console sign-in, creating an API key instead).
facts.limits: 'Only a managed source enforces the restriction.' Empty array or non-string/array managed value: Anthropic-account users can't start Claude Code or log in (message names the key). Invalid managed value => no organization permitted. Set in MDM policy/file (they outrank remote for login keys).

facts.behavior: Managed-only boolean: 'Block CLI startup until Claude Code has freshly fetched server-managed settings. If the fetch fails, Claude Code exits instead of continuing with cached or no settings.' A true from any admin-controlled managed source is honored. Unset: startup isn't blocked, though at sign-in startup it waits up to five seconds; a Cloud gateway session always waits.
facts.limits: Applies only in sessions that fetch server-managed settings (others start without waiting). claude auth subcommands exempt. Takes effect at next session start. Set in MDM/file to cover the time before first server payload.

facts.behavior: Managed-only (v2.1.163+): requiredMinimumVersion exits Claude Code at startup when the running version is older and tells the user to update through the approved method; requiredMaximumVersion exits at startup when newer. Background auto-updates and claude update skip versions above the ceiling. claude update, claude install, claude doctor keep working outside the range. Differs from minimumVersion which only prevents downgrades.
facts.limits: Check runs at startup only; a running session continues. Invalid version value is ignored (fail open); no warning when set outside managed.

facts.behavior: Managed-only (v2.1.282+): lets WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain (HKLM and Windows managed file first, then /etc/claude-code only when no Windows admin document is present, HKCU below). Honored only when set in HKLM or a file/drop-in under C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode.
facts.limits: No effect on native Windows. Default false (WSL reads only /etc/claude-code). A Windows source containing only this key doesn't count as a policy source. /etc/claude-code on WSL is user-writable.

facts.feature: Org-level toggles and telemetry via managed env
facts.behavior: On Team/Enterprise, an Owner enables/disables Remote Control and cloud sessions org-wide in claude.ai admin settings (turning Remote Control off disconnects connected sessions on v2.1.286+ at the next ~hourly policy refresh); disableRemoteControl disables per device. Telemetry can be turned off for all devs by delivering DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 in managed env (applied without the approval dialog), which also disables feature-flag fetching and stops data for the analytics dashboard.
facts.limits: Cloud sessions have no per-device managed settings key. Server-managed changes to settings needing approval (hooks, env) wait for the developer to accept a dialog in interactive sessions.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md (Keys only a managed source can set note; Turn telemetry off for your organization; Where and when a policy applies)

unreachable: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md (linked but not fetched; not in the assigned URL list)

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md characters roughly 0-100000 were summarized by the fetch model only (full entries for availableModels/model/modelOverrides/fallbackModel/modelPicker were not quoted verbatim); the final ~48000 characters (past offset 400000) were read only as returned. No assigned page returned a 404.

area: security model, secrets handling, data usage and retention, security guidance for agents

facts.behavior: A session's permission mode sets which actions Claude can take without asking you first. Auto mode is the built-in starting permission mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions.
facts.limits: Which mode a session starts in varies by version and surface; explicit ask and deny rules still apply; organization can turn auto mode off.

facts.behavior: A separate classifier model reviews actions instead of you and blocks the ones it judges unsafe.
facts.limits: Your explicit ask and deny rules still apply; organization can turn it off. Details live on permission-modes page (not read).

facts.behavior: Claude Code starts with read-only permissions. When it needs to edit files, run tests, or execute commands, it asks you first; you approve once or allow from then on. Runs a built-in set of read-only commands such as ls, cat, git status without asking.
facts.limits: Applies to Manual mode only.

facts.behavior: Sandbox bash commands with filesystem and network isolation, reducing permission prompts while maintaining security. Configure with /sandbox.
facts.limits: Applies to Bash commands; not on by default per the page (configure with /sandbox). Sandboxed commands can run without the injection-detection prompt.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, Claude Code asks you before its file tools read or write outside the folder where it was started and its subfolders.
facts.limits: The boundary is a permission prompt, so a Bash command you approve can still write anywhere your user account can. Read outside via additional directories; restrict Bash at OS level via sandboxing.

facts.behavior: Support for allowlisting frequently used safe commands per-user, per-codebase, or per-organization.
facts.limits: Configuration feature, not default behavior.

facts.behavior: Auto-approves file edits and a fixed set of filesystem Bash commands like mkdir, touch, rm, mv, cp, and sed for paths in the working directory.
facts.limits: Other Bash commands and out-of-scope paths still prompt.

facts.behavior: You're responsible for reviewing proposed code and commands for safety before approval.
facts.limits: Policy statement.

facts.behavior: Commands that fetch content from the web such as curl and wget are not auto-approved by default. In Manual mode they prompt like any other non-read-only Bash command; can add allow rule Bash(curl *) or deny via permissions.deny.
facts.limits: A deny rule matches the command as written; for network enforcement independent of command text use sandbox network isolation.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, most tools that make network requests require user approval by default.
facts.limits: Manual mode only; 'most' tools.

facts.behavior: For most fetches, WebFetch runs a separate model call over the page, and Claude receives that call's answer instead of the raw page.
facts.limits: 'Most fetches' only; see tools-reference WebFetch tool behavior.

facts.behavior: In an interactive session, Claude Code shows the workspace trust dialog when you start it in a folder you haven't trusted. Servers in a project's .mcp.json have their own approval prompt.
facts.limits: A -p session shows neither prompt. Starting directly in home directory: trust held for current session only, not written to disk, prompt reappears each launch, no setting to persist it; trust is saved per directory for project subdirectories.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, Claude Code asks before running a Bash command it can't fully analyze. An allow rule for part of a command, such as Bash(git *), doesn't skip that prompt.
facts.limits: Manual mode; sandboxed commands can run without it.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, unmatched commands require approval by default.
facts.limits: Manual mode only.

facts.behavior: API keys and tokens are stored in the macOS Keychain when available. On Linux in a file with mode 0600, on Windows in a file that inherits the access controls of your user profile directory.
facts.limits: Covers Claude Code's own API keys/tokens, not secrets in your repos or files Claude reads.

facts.behavior: Recommends against enabling WebDAV or allowing access to paths such as \\* that may contain WebDAV subdirectories; WebDAV may let Claude Code trigger network requests to remote hosts, bypassing the permission system.
facts.limits: Windows only.

facts.behavior: Review suggested commands before approval; avoid piping untrusted content directly to Claude; verify proposed changes to critical files; use VMs to run scripts and make tool calls especially with external web services; report suspicious behavior with /feedback.
facts.limits: Page states: no system is completely immune to all attacks.

facts.feature: Privacy safeguards (as described on security page)
facts.behavior: Limited retention periods for sensitive information; restricted access to user session data; user control over data training preferences (consumer users via claude.ai/settings/privacy).
facts.limits: Policy statements; details in Privacy Center and terms.

facts.behavior: Project-scoped servers are defined in .mcp.json; servers at other scopes, claude.ai connectors and plugins can also add servers, so reviewing .mcp.json doesn't show every server a session can load. Can configure Claude Code permissions for MCP servers; managed MCP configuration restricts servers org-wide. Anthropic reviews connectors against listing criteria before adding to the Directory.
facts.limits: Anthropic does not security-audit or manage any MCP server; encourages own servers or trusted providers.

facts.behavior: Page defers to the built-in IDE MCP server section of the vs-code page.
facts.limits: No detail on this page.

facts.behavior: Each cloud session runs in an isolated Anthropic-managed VM; network access limited by default and configurable to disabled or specific domains; GitHub credentials stored encrypted on Anthropic's servers and never enter the VM (short-lived session-scoped credential, GitHub proxy attaches credential server-side); GitHub proxy rejects branch deletions and pushes of anything other than a branch (e.g. tag), branch protection rules apply to the connected GitHub access; all operations logged for audit; VMs reclaimed after inactivity; sessions deletable.
facts.limits: Self-hosted environments: isolation, egress and git credentials are your responsibility. A branch protection rule that the connected access can bypass doesn't block a session's push. Cloud sessions don't load plugins from user settings or repo .claude/settings.json.

facts.behavior: Web interface connects to a Claude Code process on your local machine; all code execution and file access stays local; session traffic travels via Anthropic API over TLS; while connected the transcript is stored on Anthropic servers to sync across devices; uses multiple short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials.
facts.limits: No cloud VMs or sandboxing involved.

facts.feature: Working with sensitive code / team security recommendations
facts.behavior: Review all changes; use project-specific permission settings for sensitive repos; run whole Claude Code process inside sandbox runtime or dev container for extra isolation; audit permissions with /permissions; use managed settings to enforce standards; share permission configs via version control; monitor with OpenTelemetry metrics; audit or block settings changes with ConfigChange hooks.
facts.limits: Recommendations; ConfigChange hooks and managed settings are opt-in configuration.

facts.behavior: Report Claude Code vulnerabilities via HackerOne, do not disclose publicly.
facts.limits: Process for Claude Code product vulnerabilities only.

facts.behavior: Run an on-demand security pass over the changes on your current branch.
facts.limits: Covers only changes on the current branch; reads source in checkout, not a running site.

facts.behavior: Plugin (security-guidance@claude-plugins-official) makes Claude review its own code changes for common vulnerabilities while it works and fix what it finds in the same session; runs automatically once installed.
facts.limits: Not built in: must be installed (/plugin install). Requires Python 3.7+ (3.10+ for agentic commit review) and git repo for end-of-turn/commit reviews (skipped silently outside a repo). Creates venv under ~/.claude/security/ and installs the Claude Agent SDK. Model-backed reviews skip with no Anthropic auth/provider. None of the layers block writes or commits; findings reach Claude as instructions and the review can miss issues. Not loaded in cloud sessions from user or repo settings.

facts.behavior: When Claude writes to a file, the plugin scans new content for risky patterns (eval(, new Function, os.system, child_process.exec, pickle, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, .innerHTML =, document.write, edits under .github/workflows/). Deterministic string match, no model call, no usage cost. Runs after the edit lands and appends warning to Claude's context; fires once per pattern per file per session.
facts.limits: Hooks on Edit, Write and NotebookEdit tool calls (not Bash-made file changes); does not block the write; works outside git repos.

facts.behavior: After each turn, computes a git diff of everything changed in the working tree during the turn (edit tools, Bash, subagents) and sends it to a separate Claude security review in the background; if issues found, Claude is re-prompted to address them.
facts.limits: Up to 30 changed files per turn; fires at most three times in a row before yielding; needs git repo and auth; does not block; uses model usage (Opus by default, SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL).

facts.feature: Security guidance: commit and push review
facts.behavior: When Claude runs git commit or git push through its Bash tool, a deeper agentic review runs in the background, reading surrounding code (callers, sanitizers).
facts.limits: Only commits/pushes Claude makes via Bash tool; commits from your own shell including the ! escape are not reviewed; capped at 20 per rolling hour; duplicates of end-of-turn findings not re-prompted; does not block commits; model set by SG_AGENTIC_MODEL.

facts.behavior: Add .claude/claude-security-guidance.md (also ~/.claude/claude-security-guidance.md user scope, .claude/claude-security-guidance.local.md project local) describing threat model and checklist; loaded as additional context for model-backed reviews.
facts.limits: Additive only; cannot suppress a vulnerability class; combined 8 KB cap; guidance for the reviewer, not deterministic guardrails. For hard enforcement use a hook that blocks the edit or a CI check.

facts.behavior: Add .claude/security-patterns.yaml (or .yml/.json) with rule_name, reminder (1 KB cap), regex or substrings, optional paths/exclude_paths globs; deterministic string matches alongside built-ins. Same lookup locations as guidance file.
facts.limits: Up to 50 custom rules; regexes prone to catastrophic backtracking skipped; YAML requires PyYAML importable (else ignored, use JSON); additive only, cannot disable built-ins; warns rather than blocks.

facts.behavior: ENABLE_PATTERN_RULES=0 disables per-edit check; ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0 end-of-turn; ENABLE_COMMIT_REVIEW=0 commit/push; ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0 all model-backed reviews; SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE=1 disables plugin entirely. /plugin disable or uninstall also available.
facts.limits: If enabled via managed settings only an administrator can disable it; built-in checks cannot be removed individually.

facts.behavior: Built on hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit (captures baseline), PostToolUse on Edit/Write/NotebookEdit, Stop, PostToolUse on Bash filtered to git commit/push. Diagnostics at ~/.claude/security/log.txt.
facts.limits: Hooks used for review, not blocking.

facts.behavior: In session: plugin; on demand: /security-review; deep scan: Claude Security plugin; on PR: Code Review (Team and Enterprise); CI: existing static analysis and dependency scanners.
facts.limits: Plugin is not a complete security solution and does not replace later checks or CI scanning.

facts.behavior: Consumer (Free, Pro, Max, Ultra): data may be used to train new models when the setting is on (including Claude Code use). Commercial (Team, Enterprise, API, 3rd-party platforms, Claude Gov): Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms, unless customer opts in (e.g. Developer Partner Program).
facts.limits: Developer Partner Program available only for Anthropic first-party API, not Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform.

facts.behavior: Consumer: 5 years if data use for model improvement allowed, 30 days if not. Commercial (Team, Enterprise, API): standard 30 days; zero data retention available to qualified accounts for Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise (per-organization, not in standard Enterprise plan).
facts.limits: Cloud sessions deletable at any time, permanently removing event data.

facts.behavior: Claude Code clients store session transcripts locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default to enable session resumption. Adjust with cleanupPeriodDays.
facts.limits: Plaintext, so secrets appearing in sessions are stored on disk; transcripts of sessions started/continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork are exempt from the limit by default. Stated under commercial-user retention bullets.

facts.feature: Data in transit and encryption at rest
facts.behavior: Claude Code sends all user prompts and model outputs over the network, encrypted via TLS 1.2+. At rest: Anthropic API AES-256 disk encryption; Bedrock AES-256 (customer-managed keys via KMS); Google Cloud Agent Platform Google-managed keys (CMEK available); Foundry depends on hosting option.
facts.limits: All prompts and model outputs, including any file contents Claude reads, go to the model provider.

facts.behavior: Repo cloned into isolated VM; Anthropic stores session transcript; GitHub credentials stored encrypted and never enter the VM; all outbound traffic goes through a security proxy for audit logging and abuse prevention; session data follows same policies as local use.
facts.limits: Anthropic-hosted only; self-hosted environments run on your infrastructure. Claude accesses only the repository where the session is initiated, not other connected repos.

facts.behavior: Follows the local data flow since execution is on your machine; while connected the transcript is also stored on Anthropic servers to sync across devices.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Latency, reliability, usage patterns sent to Anthropic and third-party logging over TLS. Metrics never include your code, prompts, or file paths. DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out.
facts.limits: Default on for Claude API; default off on Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS (unless CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST). DISABLE_TELEMETRY also disables feature-flag evaluation, possibly making Remote Control unavailable.

facts.behavior: Error messages and stack traces from Claude Code internals sent to a third-party error tracking service over TLS. Known patterns of secrets, file paths, email addresses and other personal information are redacted before leaving the machine. DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1 to opt out.
facts.limits: On only when: signed in with Pro/Max/Ultra, v2.1.198+, direct to Claude API, and org has no ZDR or HIPAA agreement. Redaction is pattern-based.

facts.behavior: Sends a copy of your conversation history including code to Anthropic (stored in Google Cloud Storage; optionally a GitHub issue created in the public repository). You choose history scope: current session (default) or other sessions from same project over last 24 hours or 7 days. Transcripts retained for 5 years. DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1 to opt out.
facts.limits: On Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry or no Anthropic credentials, writes to local archive ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ with known API key/token patterns redacted; nothing sent until you forward it. User-initiated.

facts.behavior: Claude can draft a feedback report and queue it on your machine for review; nothing is sent until you choose to send; same submission path and retention as /feedback.
facts.limits: Transcript included only if chosen on the draft's review screen.

facts.behavior: The 'How is Claude doing this session?' rating records only your rating (including Dismiss); no transcripts or session data. Optional follow-up asks to share transcript: Yes uploads conversation transcript, subagent transcripts and raw session log (known API key and token patterns redacted; source code and file contents uploaded as-is; retained up to 6 months); No / Don't ask again send nothing. Responses cannot be used to train models.
facts.limits: Disable with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1; also disabled by DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DO_NOT_TRACK, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC; feedbackSurveyRate setting (0-1) controls frequency. Runs regardless of provider. Follow-up never shown under ZDR, org-disabled feedback, or nonessential-traffic disabled. On Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/Claude apps gateway, Yes writes to ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ instead.

facts.behavior: Disables all non-essential traffic at once (telemetry, error reporting, surveys, feature-flag evaluation).
facts.limits: Does not affect WebFetch domain safety check or official plugin marketplace auto-install (opt-outs: skipWebFetchPreflight; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL). Env vars can be put in settings.json.

facts.behavior: Error reporting, telemetry and bug reporting are disabled by default on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS. Signed-in Claude apps gateway sessions disable usage analytics, error reporting and survey ratings via the gateway credential with no setting to re-enable.
facts.limits: Session quality surveys and WebFetch domain safety check run regardless of provider.

facts.behavior: Before fetching a URL, WebFetch sends the requested hostname to api.anthropic.com to check against a safety blocklist. Only hostname sent, not full URL, path, or content. Passing hostname cached 5 minutes; blocked/failed rechecked on next request.
facts.limits: Not affected by CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC; if api.anthropic.com is blocked, WebFetch fails unless skipWebFetchPreflight: true is set (then no blocklist consulted; combine with WebFetch permission rules).

area: Checkpointing and rewind of file edits

facts.behavior: Claude Code automatically tracks Claude's file edits; checkpointing 'automatically captures the state of your code before each prompt you send that starts a turn.' Every prompt that starts a turn creates a new checkpoint. It tracks 'all changes made by its file editing tools'.
facts.limits: Only files edited by Claude's file editing tools in the session are tracked. No user action needed or available to opt out per the page.

facts.behavior: Claude Code keeps file snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session. Discarding an older checkpoint deletes snapshot files no remaining checkpoint references, except each file's first snapshot (used by the VS Code extension as baseline for session diffs).
facts.limits: Older than 100 checkpoints cannot be restored.

facts.behavior: Checkpoints are saved with the conversation, so /rewind still works after resuming a session.
facts.limits: Subject to the snapshot retention sweep.

facts.behavior: Claude Code deletes a session's file snapshots in the retention sweep, by default about 30 days after the session last saved one. Rewinding to a checkpoint whose snapshots are gone can fail with 'No files were restored'. Set cleanupPeriodDays to keep snapshots longer.
facts.limits: Default about 30 days; after that code restore can fail.

facts.behavior: Run /rewind, or press Esc twice when the prompt input is empty, to open the rewind menu listing prompts sent during the session. Actions: Restore code and conversation; Restore conversation (keep current code); Restore code (keep conversation); Summarize from here; Summarize up to here; Never mind.
facts.limits: If the prompt input contains text, double Esc clears it instead (saved to input history; press Up). The two code-restore options appear only when the selected checkpoint has tracked file changes to revert; otherwise only Restore conversation, summarize options, and Never mind.

facts.behavior: After restoring the conversation or choosing Summarize from here, the original prompt from the selected message is restored into the input field to re-send or edit. Summarize up to here leaves you at the end of the conversation with input empty.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Rewound messages can return if you exit before next prompt
facts.behavior: If you exit before sending another prompt, rewound messages can return. Claude Code saves the rewound conversation together with the next prompt. To remove them again, run /rewind and select the same prompt, then Restore conversation.
facts.limits: Files you restored stay as the rewind left them.

facts.behavior: If /clear was run earlier in the same process, the rewind menu shows an extra top entry '/resume <session-id> (previous session)' to resume the pre-clear conversation.
facts.limits: Available only until you exit Claude Code or resume a different session.

facts.feature: Summarize from here / up to here
facts.behavior: Compresses the conversation from (or before) the selected point into a summary, freeing context window space; a 'Summarized conversation' marker appears. You can guide the summary by typing instructions in the 'add context (optional)' row; number key summarizes immediately without instructions. Like a targeted /compact.
facts.limits: Summarizing doesn't change files on disk; original messages stay in the session transcript. It stays in the same session; to branch use /branch or claude --continue --fork-session.

facts.behavior: Once Claude has edited a file with its file editing tools in the conversation, /rewind undoes changes Bash commands make to that file afterward. The rewind menu counts changes to files Claude had already edited, whatever made them.
facts.limits: A file that only Bash commands changed is not tracked and stays as it is; use version control such as Git to revert it.

facts.behavior: Claude Code usually doesn't capture subagent edits in session checkpoints. A foreground forked skill (context: fork, background: false) edits the working tree during your own turn, so rewinding restores its edits as usual.
facts.limits: For any other subagent (including a background forked skill, the default, and a background /code-review --fix run), rewinding restores only files Claude had already edited in the conversation; the subagent's edits to other files stay. Use Git to revert.

facts.behavior: Checkpointing only tracks files edited within the current session.
facts.limits: Manual changes outside Claude Code and edits from other concurrent sessions are normally not captured, unless they modify the same files as the current session.

facts.behavior: A message typed while Claude was still working can be marked 'No code restore' in the rewind menu; it has no checkpoint of its own. Selecting the prompt that started the turn and choosing Restore code or Restore code and conversation reverts Claude's file edits from the whole turn.
facts.limits: No per-message code restore for mid-turn messages.

facts.behavior: On Restore code or Restore code and conversation, Claude Code skips any tracked path that is a symlink or hard link and shows a 'Restored the code, but skipped N files' warning. /debug logging (~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt) names each skipped path.
facts.limits: Skipped files keep current contents; ask Claude to reverse the edit or edit manually. Examples: dotfile-manager symlinks, pnpm hard links.

facts.behavior: 'Checkpoints are designed for quick, session-level recovery. For permanent version history and collaboration, continue using version control, such as Git, for commits, branches, and long-term history.' Git is the documented fallback for Bash-only changes and non-captured subagent edits.
facts.limits: Checkpoints are not a replacement for version control; the docs do not say checkpoints create git commits or touch git state.

area: Anthropic best-practices and common-workflows guidance for Claude Code, and the /doctor prompt audit

facts.behavior: Prompt, CLAUDE.md and skills are non-deterministic: 'there's no guarantee that it'll follow your instructions'. Hooks, deny rules and managed settings are deterministic: 'Claude Code applies this every time, no matter what the model decided to do.' Doc: 'If you keep adding emphasis to a CLAUDE.md line and Claude still misses it, that's a sign the line belongs in a hook.' Conversely, hooks for mere preferences should be deleted.
facts.limits: Guidance only; the page itself enforces nothing. A prompt or agent hook asks another model, so it is not deterministic either; use command or http hooks (optionally onFailure block) for real enforcement.

facts.feature: Only write down what Claude can't find in the repo
facts.behavior: 'Only write down what Claude can't find by reading the repo, or what it would otherwise spend time rediscovering every session.' Test: could it find this by reading the code, and would it actually go and look? If both yes, leave it out. 'Describe your architecture and file layout in CLAUDE.md' is listed under advice to stop doing.
facts.limits: Advice only; no tool checks this (except /doctor, which proposes trims for checked-in CLAUDE.md).

facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md loads into every session; best practices says keep it to commands, misleading places, decisions not in the repo, and anything corrected twice. Memory page: 'target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.'
facts.limits: Target not a hard cap for content, but Claude Code skips a file over 4 MiB. Imports (@path) do not reduce context cost because imported files load with the importing CLAUDE.md.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Write effective instructions; 'My CLAUDE.md is too large')

facts.behavior: 'If one of your instruction files is over the recommended length, you see a warning at startup and when you run /status. You also see a warning when files that are each within that length add up past a combined limit at session start.'
facts.limits: Each CLAUDE.md, rules file, and @path import counts as a separate file. Warning only; does not truncate or block (except the 4 MiB skip).

facts.behavior: 'run /doctor prompt-audit in a session. Claude looks for problems such as instructions written for older models, references to files or commands that don't exist, and files that contradict each other. You get a report of findings with proposed edits, and nothing in your files changes until you ask Claude to apply them.' Default scope: CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md, plus the rules, skills, commands, subagents and output styles under .claude/ and ~/.claude/. Pass a path to audit one file or directory (e.g. /doctor prompt-audit .claude/skills/deploy).
facts.limits: On demand only, not automatic or run at session start; report-only, makes no edits until asked. Runs through the bundled /claude-api skill and is unavailable if that skill is turned off via skillOverrides or disableBundledSkills. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later. Model-driven review, so findings are advisory.

facts.behavior: 'run /doctor inside Claude Code for an automated check of your installation, settings, extensions, and context usage; it proposes fixes it can apply after you confirm.' Best practices: '/doctor suggests cuts for anything Claude can already work out from the code.' Memory page: it 'proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md: it cuts content Claude can derive from the codebase, such as directory layouts, dependency lists, and architecture overviews, and keeps pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults.'
facts.limits: Interactive and manual; fixes applied only after confirmation. Trim proposals are for a checked-in CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: 'Check the health of your Claude Code installation. Reads settings files in the current directory without a trust prompt. For a full checkup that can also fix issues, run /doctor in a session.' Troubleshooting: run `claude doctor` from your shell if claude won't start; it also shows the Search line (e.g. 'OK (bundled)' or system ripgrep path). Footer 'Auto-update failed · Run claude doctor' points to it.
facts.limits: Only option is -h/--help. It does not fix issues and does not run the prompt audit (that is /doctor prompt-audit in a session). Shows Search OK even when WSL cross-filesystem search is slow/incomplete.

facts.behavior: 'Older models sometimes needed the emphasis. Current ones follow a plainly worded line, and piling on emphasis mostly makes Claude over-apply the rule. If it's a rule that can't bend, turn it into a hook or a deny rule. If the line is getting lost in a long file, the file needs to be shorter.'
facts.limits: Guidance only; nothing detects or strips emphasis other than the model-based prompt audit (older-model patterns).

facts.feature: Other 'what you can stop doing' advice
facts.behavior: Table of outdated advice: aggressive context-window management (1M windows, auto compaction; /clear between tasks still worthwhile); subagents to protect context; delegating to a subagent for a better answer; 'think hard/think harder/be thorough' (ordinary prompt text, effort is the control; ultrathink still works for one turn); 'keep going, loop until done, don't be lazy' (more likely to cause over-work; use /goal or Stop hook); describing architecture/file layout in CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: Advisory documentation. 'be ambitious' is stated as still helpful (scope, not thinking). Giving Claude a check to pass is still worth doing.

facts.feature: Effort level as the control for thinking
facts.behavior: 'Effort is the main control for how long Claude thinks, and it replaces most of what people used to do with prompt wording.' Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 default to medium. /effort low|high|xhigh|max; max for hard unattended problems (tends to overthink on ordinary tasks); ultrathink in a single prompt for one-off deep reasoning.
facts.limits: Wording like 'think step by step' only nudges within the effort setting, 'it won't lift it past it'.

facts.behavior: 'put it in .claude/rules/ with a paths: filter so it only loads when Claude is actually working there' (example: paths: src/api/**/*.ts).
facts.limits: Applies only to rule files that carry a paths: frontmatter glob; rules without it are not path-scoped. Detail of loading semantics is on the memory page.

facts.behavior: Team procedures go in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. For a model-invocable skill, only name and description are in context each session and the full file is read when needed. 'disable-model-invocation: true' means Claude can't start the skill on its own; it runs only when the user types /name. Doc says the CLAUDE.md rule applies to skills too: only write what Claude can't find.
facts.limits: Skill descriptions still cost context every session. The flag stops Claude invoking it; it does not stop the user.

facts.behavior: 'Your personal preferences go in CLAUDE.local.md instead of CLAUDE.md, and you add that file to .gitignore so it stays out of the repo.'
facts.limits: Gitignoring is the user's job; not enforced by the harness.

facts.behavior: '/init generates a starting version from your codebase. From there the work is mostly removing lines.'
facts.limits: A starting point only; memory guide recommends staying under 200 lines.

facts.behavior: A Stop hook runs a script when Claude tries to end its turn and 'sends Claude back to work if the script exits with code 2'. stderr is fed back as the reason. 'enforced by Claude Code (the harness)'.
facts.limits: If the hook blocks eight stops in a row with no tool call between them, Claude Code overrides the next block and ends the turn; cap raised via CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.

facts.behavior: 'sets a condition that a separate model checks against the conversation after every turn, and Claude keeps going until it's met.' Useful for long background runs.
facts.limits: Model-judged, non-deterministic; keeps sending requests (cost) while running.

facts.behavior: /code-review 'reviews the diff in a fresh subagent that never saw your conversation'. /verify 'has Claude build and run the app and look at the result.' Ask for evidence (command and output), not just 'all tests pass'. Reviewer prompt tip: keep 'skip style'.
facts.limits: Non-deterministic; reviewers asked to find problems will always find something.

facts.feature: Hooks for rules with zero exceptions
facts.behavior: Hooks run at fixed points (before/after a tool call, on stop, session start). Types: shell command, HTTP POST, MCP tool call, prompt/agent hook. Example PostToolUse hook matcher Edit|Write runs prettier; PreToolUse hook exits code 2 to block edits under migrations/. 'a hook is for a rule with zero exceptions'; 'Prefer named exports' stays in CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: prompt/agent hooks are model-decided, not deterministic. onFailure: "block" needed to also block when the hook crashes or times out. Doc says keep the enforced set small; each hook can fire wrongly. @-file references do not trigger PreToolUse hooks (see common-workflows).

facts.behavior: 'deny rules hold in every permission mode, including auto and bypassPermissions'. Example Read(./.env) denies. The Read rule catches `cat .env` because common file-reading commands are recognized. /sandbox gives OS-level confinement of shell commands on macOS, Linux, WSL2 and picks up Read deny and WebFetch(domain:) rules. Strict sandbox mode turns off the retry-outside-sandbox request.
facts.limits: Rules match tool calls not intent: they won't catch a script that opens the file; a WebFetch domain deny does nothing about curl to that domain unless the sandbox is on. Clipboard tools (pbcopy etc.) can fail inside the sandbox.

facts.behavior: .claude/settings.local.json and ~/.claude/settings.json are personal; .claude/settings.json is repo-wide (deny rules apply right away, allow rules wait for the trust dialog, workspace trust gates hooks); managed settings belong to the organization and cannot be overridden by personal files.
facts.limits: Keep enforced set small (doc: forty is likely too many).

facts.behavior: Interactive terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode: a classifier checks risky actions (curl|bash, production deploys/migrations, force pushes over others' work, sensitive data to external endpoints, actions driven by content Claude read). After three blocks in a row or twenty total it pauses and asks. autoMode config uses plain English; keep "$defaults" in lists.
facts.limits: 'a classifier model judging each action rather than a hard rule' and can be wrong; org can disable. Runs after deny/ask rules and PreToolUse hooks. autoMode block is ignored in project settings, must live in ~/.claude/settings.json. Stating 'don't push until I've reviewed' in chat is a signal that can be lost on compaction. 'your "never" rules belong in deny rules or hooks.'

facts.behavior: 'scans your recent transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP calls and adds them to an allowlist in .claude/settings.json.'
facts.limits: Manual command; read-only calls only.

facts.feature: Subagents and custom reviewer tool restriction
facts.behavior: Claude delegates on its own (Explore agent for broad searches, forked side tasks, background by default). Costs tokens; may be slower. A custom subagent in .claude/agents/ with `tools: Read, Grep, Glob` cannot edit: 'that limit is enforced by Claude Code rather than requested in a prompt.' model: haiku for simple subagents.
facts.limits: Same-or-smaller model, so parallelism or fresh eyes but not a smarter answer.

facts.feature: Context and cost controls (/usage, /clear, /compact, prompt cache)
facts.behavior: /usage breaks usage down by skill, subagent, plugin and MCP server and flags patterns over 10%. /clear between unrelated tasks (/clear <name> names the left session). /compact with a focus. Prompt cache about one hour on subscription, five minutes on API key/cloud/credits; subagents five minutes. Idle sessions past about 200K tokens on one-hour cache are compacted before cache expiry. Conversation auto-compacts.
facts.limits: Breakdown available on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise.

facts.behavior: Esc stops mid-action keeping work; /rewind (or Esc twice) rolls code, conversation or both back; after two failed corrections run /clear and write a better prompt; /btw answers a side question without adding to history; /rename then `claude --resume <name>`; `claude --continue` resumes most recent.
facts.limits: Checkpoints cover only files edited with Claude's own file tools in the main conversation; files touched only by Bash are not restored; work alongside git, not a replacement.

facts.behavior: Five questions: knows what done looks like, can check its own work, what it may touch, what stops it (--max-turns, --max-budget-usd, spend limit), who signs off. `claude -p` flags: --bare (skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, CLAUDE.md, ignores claude.ai login), --allowedTools, --permission-mode dontAsk, --output-format json, --max-turns. Auto mode works with -p via --permission-mode auto; a block denies that action and the run continues.
facts.limits: Checklist is advisory; the flags are enforced by the CLI. --bare skips CLAUDE.md so house rules do not load in such runs.

facts.behavior: /loop repeats a prompt in the open session; /schedule creates cloud scheduled tasks (needs claude.ai login); protect main with a branch rule the task can't bypass. claude -w <name> starts a session in a new git worktree; .worktreeinclude at repo root (gitignore syntax) copies listed gitignored files into every worktree; worktree.symlinkDirectories for large dirs. Unnamed worktree sessions with nothing in them are removed on exit; subagent worktrees vanish if unchanged; leftover subagent/background worktrees swept after cleanupPeriodDays when they hold no work. /batch splits a mechanical change into 5 to 30 units, each in its own worktree with a PR.
facts.limits: A `claude -p --worktree` run is cleaned up manually (git worktree remove, git worktree unlock if locked). Worktree needs at least one commit. .worktreeinclude copies, not links.

facts.behavior: Ask Claude to 'Interview me until you could write the spec, then write it to SPEC.md', then build in a fresh session.
facts.limits: Prompt pattern only.

facts.behavior: Name the file, symptom and what fixed looks like; state preference between approaches; hand over @file, images, or piped output. 'be ambitious' tells Claude about scope.
facts.limits: Advisory prompting guidance.

facts.feature: Connect tools: CLIs, MCP, code intelligence plugins
facts.behavior: CLIs such as gh are the easiest way in; claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>; /mcp shows servers. 'Connected servers add their tool names and instructions to the context even when you're not using them', so disable unused ones.
facts.limits: MCP cost is paid every session while connected.

facts.behavior: @path includes file contents when it fits the Read tool token limit (25,000 tokens default); a text file larger than 256KB isn't included. Directory references show listings, not contents. @ references add CLAUDE.md from the file's directory and parents to context. MCP resources via @server:resource.
facts.limits: PreToolUse hooks do NOT run for @ references because no tool call is made. Block with a Read deny rule (the file isn't included) or set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS=1 (v2.1.299+; ignored in project and local settings, honored in shell env, user or managed settings).

facts.behavior: 'Claude Code works in any directory. Run it inside a notes vault... The .claude/ directory and CLAUDE.md sit alongside other tools' config directories without conflict. Claude reads files fresh on each tool call.'
facts.limits: None stated.

facts.behavior: claude --continue resumes the most recent session in the directory ('No conversation found to continue' if none); claude --resume or /resume to choose. A session is linked to a PR when Claude creates it with gh pr create or glab mr create; find with `claude --from-pr <n>`.
facts.limits: Linking happens only for PRs created that way or worked on by Claude.

facts.behavior: 'Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve.' Start with claude --permission-mode plan or Shift+Tab; status bar shows plan mode on.
facts.limits: Manual opt-in per session.

facts.feature: Scheduled-task prompt guidance and scheduling options
facts.behavior: Scheduled prompts should state what success looks like and what to do with results since they can't ask clarifying questions. Options: cloud scheduled tasks (routines), desktop scheduled tasks, GitHub Actions, /loop (current session; --resume/--continue restore unexpired fixed-interval loops).
facts.limits: /loop only runs while a session is open.

facts.feature: Subagent delegation recipe and pipe to scripts
facts.behavior: 'use a subagent to investigate...' reads files in its own context and reports a summary. `git log --oneline -20 | claude -p "..."` for non-interactive use.
facts.limits: Prompt recipes only.

facts.behavior: /compact for high CPU/memory; claude --safe-mode disables all customizations to test whether a plugin, MCP server or hook is the cause; critical memory warning when heap passes 2.5GB; /heapdump (hidden from command menu) writes <session-id>.heapsnapshot and -diagnostics.json to ~/Desktop (snapshot contains full conversation and credentials; share only diagnostics.json). Autocompact thrashing error stops retries when context refills repeatedly; recover via smaller reads, /compact with focus, subagent, /clear, /context. Tables over 200 rows render first 200 only. Search failures: set USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 and verify with claude doctor.
facts.limits: Diagnostics are manual. Config problems (settings, hooks, MCP not loading) go to the Debug your configuration page, not this one.

area: Tools reference, context window and compaction, prompt caching, and implications for instruction-file size and tool behavior

facts.behavior: The tool names are the exact strings you use in permission rules, subagent tool lists, and hook matchers. Same ToolName(specifier) rule format accepted in permissions.allow/deny, --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, Agent SDK options, skill allowed-tools frontmatter, and hook if conditions. Hook matcher fields use bare tool names.
facts.limits: Tools like ExitPlanMode and ShareOnboardingGuide accept only the bare name. WebSearch takes no specifier. The advisor tool is an API server tool with no name usable in rules or matchers.

facts.behavior: Yes (prompts in Manual mode inside working dir): Artifact, Bash, Edit, EnterWorktree, ExitPlanMode, Monitor, NotebookEdit, PowerShell, ShareOnboardingGuide, Skill, WebFetch, WebSearch, Workflow, Write. No: Agent, AskUserQuestion, Cron*, EndConversation, EnterPlanMode, ExitWorktree, Glob, Grep, LSP, Read, Task*, etc. In auto mode a classifier decides most prompts.
facts.limits: File-access tools marked No (Read, Grep, Glob) still prompt for paths outside the working directory and additional directories. Bash runs a built-in set of read-only commands without prompting.

facts.behavior: An Edit(...) allow rule also grants read access to the same path. A Read(...) deny rule also blocks Edit and Write on the same path, including creating a new file there.
facts.limits: Write's Read-deny check requires v2.1.228+.

facts.behavior: Spawns a subagent in a separate context window; the parent sees only the final result, not intermediate tool calls. Launching does not itself prompt; the subagent's own tool calls are checked against permission rules. Claude Code runs subagents in the background by default apart from foreground cases. maxTurns in the subagent definition caps turns; result marked partial at the limit.
facts.limits: Tools: neither field set inherits all tools available to subagents; tools only = listed; disallowedTools only = all but listed; both = disallowedTools wins. Never granted a tool not available to subagents. Zero-match tools list errors instead of launching.

facts.behavior: A subagent handles research in its own separate context window, so large file reads stay out of yours. Only the summary and a small metadata trailer come back.
facts.limits: Subagent starts its own conversation with its own system prompt and tool set; its first request does not read the parent's cache. Forks inherit parent prompt, tools and history so they do read parent cache.

facts.behavior: Asks multiple-choice questions; questions stay open until answered by default. Typed answers relayed with neutral wording.
facts.limits: Optional askUserQuestionTimeout (60s, 5m, 10m) auto-closes and lets Claude proceed on its own judgment; timer never starts in background sessions, screen reader mode, or Remote Control. Applies only to AskUserQuestion, never to permission prompts or plan approval.

facts.behavior: Each command runs in a separate process. cd carries over to later Bash commands while it stays inside the project directory or an additional working directory. If cd lands outside, Claude Code resets to the project directory and appends 'Shell cwd was reset to <dir>' to the tool result.
facts.limits: Subagent sessions never carry over cd. CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 disables carry-over. Environment variables do not persist (export in one command not available in next); use CLAUDE_ENV_FILE or a SessionStart hook. Aliases/functions from ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile are sourced at session start and applied.

facts.behavior: Each command runs under a timeout managed by Claude via the timeout parameter. BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS default two minutes; BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS ceiling ten minutes. A foreground command reaching timeout is moved to the background instead of stopped (unless it starts with sleep).
facts.limits: User cannot set a per-command timeout. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 or bare mode disables auto-backgrounding so the command stops. cd inside a moved command never carries over.

facts.behavior: Output streamed to a working file; a command whose output passes 5 GB is killed. Valid result: inline up to roughly 30,000 characters by default; past that, a file path saved to the session directory (truncated past 64 MiB) plus a preview of up to first 2,000 characters. Failure result: inline up to roughly 10,000 characters, a head-and-tail excerpt, no file path.
facts.limits: Exit 1 counts as valid only for grep, rg, egrep, fgrep, find, diff, test, [, git diff, git grep; any other exit 1 (pgrep, jq -e, cmp) is a failure. BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH read-back window 30,000 default, hard ceiling 150,000, does not raise inline ceilings. bashOutputMaxChars setting up to 128,000 sizes both, then BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH ignored (v2.1.261+).

facts.feature: Bash: background commands and time limit
facts.behavior: run_in_background starts a background task; /tasks lists and stops. Main-conversation or background-subagent commands keep running after a final response; a foreground subagent's commands stop when its run ends. In unattended sessions (-p, Agent SDK, CI, cloud) background commands get a time limit: 30 minutes default, max 2 hours (10 minutes default for -p with text prompt); Claude Code stops it and tells Claude.
facts.limits: Local terminal/desktop/VS Code sessions have no time limit. Time limit requires v2.1.285+. Raise via BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS above 1800000 and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS above 7200000; lower values cannot shorten.

facts.behavior: CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT (e.g. 4G) caps memory for Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands using a memory cgroup; one cap shared across all of a session's commands. CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_CGROUP_EXCLUDE exempts kinds (mcp, lsp, hooks, plugin, helper, agent).
facts.limits: Linux and WSL only; v2.1.233+ (exclude var v2.1.246+). If cgroup setup fails, commands run uncapped. Kernel kill result does not name the cap. Hooks that can block/change an action and MCP servers they call are always excluded. Held until relaunch.

facts.behavior: Exact string replacement (old_string to new_string); no regex or fuzzy matching. Checks: read-before-edit (a PARTIAL view read does not count), exact match including whitespace, uniqueness (exactly once unless replace_all). A file changed on disk after last read can still be edited if old_string matches current content exactly and unambiguously and reading needs no prompt.
facts.limits: Claude Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and older always require the read; newer models can edit an unread file when reading wouldn't need a permission prompt and Read is available. Viewing via cat, nl, bat, batcat, head, tail, sed -n 'X,Yp', grep, egrep, fgrep, rg on one file with no pipes or redirects satisfies the read (not if nothing of the file's text was printed). Read deny rules refused first.

facts.behavior: Edit and NotebookEdit refuse files that are not valid UTF-8 (unless Edit file starts with a little-endian UTF-16 BOM) and leave the file untouched. Write can still replace such a file unless new content contains U+FFFD; it saves as UTF-8, losing original encoding.
facts.limits: Applies to legacy encodings (Windows-1252, Shift-JIS), binary files, invalid UTF-8.

facts.behavior: Creates a new file or overwrites an existing one with the full content; does not append or merge. For partial changes Claude uses Edit.
facts.limits: Read-before-overwrite: Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and older always require it (error otherwise); newer models can overwrite an unread file under the same conditions as Edit. Notebooks and PARTIAL-view files require the read on every model. Not required for new files. Viewing via Bash satisfies it per Edit rules.

facts.behavior: Returns file contents with line numbers; Claude is instructed to always pass absolute paths. Empty file returns a notice; offset past end returns line count. Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) returned visually, resized/recompressed. PDFs: short read whole; over 10 pages read in ranges via pages param, up to 20 pages at a time (needs pdftoppm/poppler). .ipynb returns all cells with outputs.
facts.limits: Reads only files, not directories. Refuses binary extensions (.xlsx, .parquet, .heic, .zip). Refuses image over 128 MB; notebook over 256 KB or over token limit errors; notebook over 100 MB refused. Permission: No in-working-directory.

facts.behavior: By default one call returns at most 25,000 tokens (CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) and refuses a whole file over 256 KB. Whole file over token limit: first page with a PARTIAL view notice. Whole file over 256 KB, or offset/limit read over token limit: an error telling it to read a portion with offset and limit or use Grep. v2.1.296+: allow_large: true reads whole file sized against remaining context window.
facts.limits: Images, PDFs, notebooks keep their limits under allow_large.

facts.behavior: On macOS, Linux, WSL, Glob and Grep are absent from the default tool set; Claude searches with find and grep through Bash (embedded bfs and ugrep), and those searches reach hooks and permission rules as Bash calls. On Windows they are in the default set.
facts.limits: Restored by naming Glob/Grep in --tools or --allowedTools at startup (not a settings-file allow rule), when Bash is removed by deny rule/--disallowedTools/--restricted, or when a subagent lists them without Bash.

facts.behavior: Finds files by pattern; results sorted by modification time and capped at 100 files, with a truncation flag. Does not respect .gitignore by default (CLAUDE_CODE_GLOB_NO_IGNORE=false to change).
facts.limits: Permission decided before checking whether the path exists; null byte in pattern/path errors.

facts.behavior: Built on ripgrep (ripgrep regex syntax, not POSIX). Modes: files_with_matches (default), content, count. Respects .gitignore (pass the path directly to search ignored files). Single-line matching unless multiline: true. Rejected pattern returns ripgrep's diagnostic as an error (before v2.1.208 reported 'No files found').
facts.limits: Absent by default on macOS/Linux/WSL; permission decided before path existence check.

facts.behavior: Code intelligence via language servers; after each file edit automatically reports type errors and warnings. Supports definitions, references, type info, symbols, implementations, call hierarchies.
facts.limits: Inactive until a code intelligence plugin is installed; user installs the server binary; not started in cloud sessions; errors per call if server cannot start.

facts.behavior: Runs a command in the background and feeds each output line to Claude; can open a WebSocket (ws/wss) where each text message is an event. Every watch has a deadline: 5 minutes by default, at most 30 minutes, at most 10 minutes in -p single-prompt runs; Claude gets one notice at the deadline. Uses the same permission rules as Bash; in auto mode allow rules naming Monitor are set aside.
facts.limits: WebSocket: binary frames replaced by placeholder; message over 1 MiB ends the watch; private/link-local/cloud-metadata URLs denied; opening prompts for approval with no 'don't ask again for host'. Windows needs Git Bash. v2.1.310+ in some provider/telemetry-off configs.

facts.behavior: Modifies Jupyter notebook one cell at a time by cell_id; modes replace (default), insert (needs cell_type), delete. Permission rules use Edit(...) path format.
facts.limits: No string replacement across notebook; refuses non-UTF-8 notebooks.

facts.behavior: Runs PowerShell natively. Auto-enabled on Windows without Git Bash; opt-in on Linux/macOS/WSL via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1 (needs pwsh 7+). Hooks should match Bash|PowerShell. On Windows with Git Bash, any Bash deny rule (even scoped) turns PowerShell off without warning.
facts.limits: Preview: profiles not loaded; no sandboxing on Windows. Spawned with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass at process scope.

facts.behavior: EnterWorktree creates an isolated git worktree and switches into it, or with path switches into an existing one. Paths outside .claude/worktrees/ prompt for approval; new-worktree creation and paths under .claude/worktrees/ do not. From inside a worktree session only the path form is available and the target must be under .claude/worktrees/ of the session's repository.
facts.limits: Scope: the .claude/worktrees/ prompt rule applies only to the path form. ExitWorktree not available to subagents already in their own working directory (isolation: worktree). Both tools removed/refused once permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories is on. Before v2.1.206 no prompt.

facts.behavior: Ends the session only for sustained abusive input after a warning, or when the user asks for a demo. Session locks afterward; only /clear, /resume, /help, /exit, /feedback run.
facts.limits: Never prompts; PreToolUse hooks don't run for it; deny/ask rules, --disallowedTools and --tools cannot remove it while another tool remains. Not available to subagents, -p, Agent SDK, VS Code panel, GitHub Actions, cloud sessions, bare mode, or cloud providers. Models: Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5 or later.

facts.behavior: Provided by default only on Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and earlier models (v2.1.268+). TodoWrite replaces them when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0. Left out on other models because tool definitions and reminders take up context; Claude keeps track of multi-step work without a checklist. Always provided in background and cloud sessions.
facts.limits: Opt in with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1, --allowedTools, or --tools. Subagents have them only when the session does. TaskOutput removed in v2.1.277 (Claude reads the output file with Read).

facts.behavior: Fetches a URL, converts HTML to Markdown, then runs the prompt against content in a separate model call; Claude receives the result of that call, not the raw page (lossy by design). Reads up to 100,000 characters per call; 15-minute response cache (CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS, v2.1.233+); five-minute download deadline (CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_DEADLINE_MS, v2.1.268+). HTTP upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects returned as text, not followed.
facts.limits: Refuses localhost and hostnames without a dot (use curl). Prompts in Manual and acceptEdits modes except allowed/denied domains and a built-in preapproved documentation domain set; auto and bypassPermissions skip the prompt unless an ask rule matches. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH=1 (v2.1.285+) disables. Team/Enterprise may withhold it until org policy loads.

facts.behavior: Runs a query against Anthropic's web search backend and returns titles and URLs; does not fetch pages. Up to eight backend searches per call. allowed_domains or blocked_domains (not both). Interactive session limit of 200 calls shared with subagents, refilling about 100/hour (v2.1.290+); /clear resets.
facts.limits: Backend not configurable (use an MCP search server). Cap raisable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION but not removable. In -p/Agent SDK limit is per turn. Not on Amazon Bedrock.

facts.feature: Skill, Workflow, ToolSearch and misc tools
facts.behavior: Skill executes a skill in the main conversation (permission Yes). Workflow runs a script orchestrating subagents in the background (Yes). ToolSearch loads deferred tools when tool search is enabled. WaitForMcpServers appears only when tool search is disabled. SendFeedback drafts feedback locally under ~/.claude/feedback/drafts/, sends nothing until the user chooses (queue of 10, 30-day expiry, max 3 cards per session by default). CronCreate/Delete/List are session-scoped. PushNotification, SendUserFile, RemoteTrigger need Anthropic-hosted infra.
facts.limits: SendFeedback absent in -p, Agent SDK, cloud, cloud-provider, ZDR and HIPAA sessions; CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK=0 or feedbackDrafts=off disables. Skills run through the Skill tool rather than adding tool entries.

facts.feature: What loads before the first prompt
facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP tool names, and skill descriptions all load into context before you type. AGENTS.md files can load in place of CLAUDE.md. Output style and --append-system-prompt text may add more.
facts.limits: Page uses representative token counts; gives no numeric size limit or recommended length for CLAUDE.md or MEMORY.md. /context shows live breakdown by category with optimization suggestions; /memory opens files.

facts.feature: Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md loading
facts.behavior: Path-scoped rules (paths: frontmatter) load automatically alongside matching files when Claude reads, writes, or edits their trigger file; nested CLAUDE.md in subdirectories likewise load on demand. They load into message history.
facts.limits: Compaction summarizes them away; they are reloaded on demand only. 'If a rule must persist across compaction, drop the paths: frontmatter or move it to the project-root CLAUDE.md.'

facts.behavior: System prompt and output style still apply. Project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules re-injected from disk. Auto memory re-injected from disk. Skill descriptions rebuilt and re-injected (v2.1.304+). Git status refreshed. Plan-mode plan re-injected. Background commands/subagents keep running. SessionStart hooks matching the compact source run and add output.
facts.limits: Context hooks added earlier are summarized with the conversation. Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md reload on demand only. Summarization inherits session extended-thinking config (v2.1.198+).

facts.feature: Compaction: file re-read and skill-body caps
facts.behavior: After compaction Claude Code re-reads up to five files Claude read or edited, most recently modified first; a file over 5,000 tokens comes back as a path reference (Referenced file) without content. Invoked skill bodies re-injected capped at 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 tokens total; oldest dropped first; truncation keeps the start of the file.
facts.limits: Advice: put the most important instructions near the top of SKILL.md.

facts.behavior: Claude Code compacts automatically as you approach the limit. /compact accepts focus instructions; /rewind offers Summarize from here / up to here; /autocompact <tokens> sets how full the window gets before the automatic pass; /clear between tasks; delegate large reads to subagents. Idle conversations may also be compacted (idleCompaction setting, can be disabled, v2.1.290+).
facts.limits: Per-model thresholds are on model-config.md (Default auto-compact thresholds), not on these three pages. 1M-token window supported by Fable models, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.6 and later, Sonnet 4.6.

facts.feature: Prompt cache layout and prefix matching
facts.behavior: Requests are ordered system prompt (core instructions, tool definitions), project context (CLAUDE.md, auto memory, unscoped rules; changes at session start, /clear, /compact), then conversation. The match is exact on the prefix, so a change anywhere recomputes everything after it; no per-file caching. A system prompt change invalidates everything.
facts.limits: Each model has its own cache; on most models each effort level has its own cache (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.1 with API key/subscription keep cache). Fast mode and standard speed keep separate caches.

facts.behavior: Project-root and user-level CLAUDE.md are read once at session start and held in memory. Editing mid-session does not invalidate the cache, but the edit also doesn't apply; the new content loads on the next /clear, /compact, or restart.
facts.limits: Nested CLAUDE.md and paths: rules load later on demand; editing one before it loads takes effect, after load it is in history and edits don't change it.

facts.behavior: Switching models (/model asks confirmation only while cache is warm; opusplan toggles, auto model fallback, skill/command model frontmatter count); changing effort on most models; turning fast mode on/off; adding/removing tool definitions (MCP server connect without tool search, deny rule removing a tool when tool search off); compacting; image/PDF accumulation (oldest batch removed); upgrading Claude Code (first conversation after upgrade).
facts.limits: With tool search active (default on supported models) MCP connect/disconnect and bare-tool deny rules do not change tool definitions and keep the cache. Plugin skills/commands/agents/hooks/monitors/themes never invalidate. Advisor toggle keeps cache. Scoped deny rules like Bash(rm *) and allow/ask rules don't change tools seen.

facts.behavior: Editing repo files (appends a system-reminder noting the change), editing CLAUDE.md mid-session, changing permission mode, changing output style (delivered as a message), invoking skills and commands (injected as user messages), /recap, /rewind (hits earlier cache entry), spawning a subagent.
facts.limits: opusplan plan-mode toggle and skills naming a different model are model switches and do invalidate.

facts.behavior: Compaction invalidates the conversation layer by design; system prompt and project context can stay cached (project context only if CLAUDE.md and memory unchanged since session start). The summarization request reuses the cached prefix while warm; after a break past the cache lifetime it reprocesses history uncached (costs most when resuming an old session).
facts.limits: Advice: run /compact at natural breaks; /rewind instead to abandon a path.

facts.behavior: Cached prefixes expire after inactivity; each hit resets the timer. Main conversation gets one hour only on a Claude subscription within plan usage; otherwise five minutes. Everything else (subagents, workflows, teammates, forks, compaction, titles) gets five minutes, except server-controlled helper requests on subscription.
facts.limits: Controls: promptCacheTtl / CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, subagentPromptCacheTtl / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL (5m or 1h, v2.1.242+), subagent experimental cacheTtl (v2.1.248+), ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1, FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 (wins). Over plan limit drops main to five minutes. Gateways must forward the anthropic-beta header.

facts.behavior: Effectively scoped to one machine and directory: system prompt embeds auto memory paths and the conversation opens with working directory, platform, shell, OS version. Parallel sessions in the same directory can share cache; sequential sessions share only if the startup git status snapshot matches.
facts.limits: Caches isolated between organizations and, on some providers, workspaces.

facts.behavior: Resumed conversation keeps the system prompt it started with by default; changes from upgrade or different --append-system-prompt take effect on compaction or a new conversation.
facts.limits: Reads from cache only the unchanged prefix still within its lifetime.

facts.behavior: /usage shows a 'Prompt cache (main)' line with hit ratio, miss count, warm state and likely cause of last miss (v2.1.251+, cause text v2.1.260+). Status line scripts read current_usage (cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens) and prompt_cache.
facts.limits: Diagnostic only.

facts.behavior: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING disables for all models; per-model DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS/FABLE.
facts.limits: Per-family variables apply only to the model the alias resolves to; other pinned model IDs keep caching. Docs say for normal use leave caching enabled.

facts.behavior: Claude Code marks the mid-conversation system-context block (e.g. file-change notices) for caching on every provider; if a gateway rejects with 400 naming cache_control, it moves the marker to the last conversation message until exit; if a gateway silently strips markers the whole history bills uncached.
facts.limits: Depends on gateway; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS sends that block uncached.

facts.behavior: None of the three pages states a maximum or recommended size for CLAUDE.md, rules, or MEMORY.md. They establish that CLAUDE.md, auto memory, unscoped rules and skill descriptions load every session and are re-injected from disk after every compaction, that skill bodies are capped at 5,000 tokens each (25,000 total) after compaction, and that 'old conversation ... costs tokens on every message'. /context gives optimization suggestions.
facts.limits: No documented line or token cap, no warning or truncation for CLAUDE.md on these pages (size guidance, if any, lives on memory.md / best-practices.md / costs.md, not fetched).
